The world is cut into 8×8-chunk regions; 7 in 10 hide a §6deposit§r of 3×3 to 5×5 chunks whose ore depends on the biome (mountains: iron and copper; deserts: copper, gold, hematite; jungles: zinc, gold; swamps: lead, zinc, coal; forests and plains: iron, tin, coal; cold: lead, tin; Nether: gold). Each holds a §lreserve§r of 16,000 to 180,000 ores depending on the metal (doubled in 1.0.4); colored §6outcrops§r on the surface give them away.

§6Prospector’s hammer§r (right-click the ground): direction and distance of the nearest; on site, its ore and reserve.
§6Steam drill§r (Guillaume's shape): itself in the middle of the front of a 3 × 3 base (7 §6bases§r, one a §lport§r: steam and output), the §6bronze drill string§r 4 blocks high in the center, a tower of §6derricks§r in a cross around it and the §6crown§r on top. One ore every 3 s for 24 mB/t of steam; the deposit runs out.

pages.title: Ores and concentration
pages.text:
The new ores lie in §ltier 2 deposits§r that only the §6drill§r (multiblock) can work: chalcopyrite, pentlandite, chromite, vanadinite, bauxite, zircon, fluorite, wolframite and ilmenite (rare), argentite, pitchblende, kimberlite, beryl, corundum, pegmatite, olivine, lazurite, halite (redstone is a tier 1 deposit: from the steam drill on).

The usual path: §6crusher§r (crushed x2) → §6crusher (fine grinding)§r → §6flotation§r, §6ore separator (magnetic separation)§r or §6ore separator (shaking table)§r (concentrate) → §6roasting§r → §6reduction§r → §6electrorefining§r. Gems go through the §6ore separator (optical sorting)§r, then the §6machining center (grinding)§r. Each metal's routes, and what sets them apart: “Metallurgy” chapter.

pages.title: Chemistry and light metals
pages.text:
§6Roasting§r sulfides gives §lsulfur dioxide§r: with water and oxygen the §6chemical reactor§r turns it into §lsulfuric acid§r. §6Electrolysis§r of water gives hydrogen and oxygen; that of brine gives chlorine, caustic soda and hydrogen.

§lAluminum§r: bauxite → §6Bayer digesters§r (alumina + red mud) → §6Industrial Electrolyzer (Hall-Héroult)§r (alumina, cryolite, carbon anodes). §lTitanium, zirconium§r: chlorination → §6Kroll reactor§r (magnesium) → sponge → §6industrial crucible (vacuum)§r. §lTungsten§r: oxide → hydrogen reduction → §6sintering§r. Every route: “Metallurgy” chapter.

pages.title: The world before
pages.text:
Before you, the Stewardship built factories and entrusted them to its Servitors. What remains are §6ruins§r: derelict MKI to MKIII multiblocks, half collapsed, guarded by §6Sentinels§r that sleep and still obey.

A ruin is visited like a small dungeon:
1. §lFind§r it, and its brick and stone §lannexes§r.
2. §lCalm§r the site with its Console, or §lfight§r its guards.
3. Read what is left: §lparchment notes§r, §larchive pages§r.
4. Choose: §ldismantle§r it for scrap, or §lrestore§r it so it serves a village. Not both: a ruin that has been broken into can no longer be restored.

The Sentinels are not evil. They are waiting for an order that will not come.

pages.title: Finding a ruin
pages.text:
Ruins are born with the world, in the §lOverworld§r only, with no link to villages. Each one is the worn version of a real multiblock of the mod, placed at random, rotated, half collapsed.
• §6MKI§r: from the spawn point on, on the surface; 25 to 40% of the blocks are missing. 1 to 2 Sentinels.
• §6MKII§r: at least 600 blocks from spawn, on the surface or in a pit; 35 to 50% wear. 3 to 5 Sentinels.
• §6MKIII§r: at least 1,500 blocks away, in an underground hall or on a mountainside; 45 to 60% wear. 5 to 8 Sentinels and a Foreman.
Never an MKIV ruin, nor a reactor.

To find them: walk, look. The §6Salvager§r sees derelict blocks glow within 24 blocks; the §6Ruin Map§r and villagers' Confidences give directions (“Trade and villages” chapter). Density is set in the config (ruins).

pages.title: Annexes and cabinets
pages.text:
Around each ruin, 24 to 80 blocks away, brick and stone §6annexes§r: the outbuildings of a site that once lived. No Sentinel, no alarm: breaking their blocks wakes nothing.
• From MKI: worker's cabin, pump well, forge workshop, refectory, dormitory. From MKII: guard post, school, low warehouse.
• One chest each (two in the warehouse): parchment notes, some scrap, provisions and tools of the time. Never an archive page.

Inside the ruin, one or two §6Archive Cabinets§r: they open like a chest and drop their scrap when broken. Inside: 1 to 4 §larchive pages§r depending on the tier, 1 to 3 §lparchment notes§r, scrap of the ruin's category and, in one of them, the §lService Note§r that holds the Console's code.

pages.title: Notes, pages and the Codex
pages.text:
Lore is not told: it is found, in pieces.
• §6Parchment Note§r: one to three sentences, often cut short. An image, a gesture, a place. Forty in all, in the chests of ruins and annexes.
• §6Archive Page§r: rare, precise, only in the cabinets. An author, a date in Stewardship Years, a voice.
• §6Memory Module§r: a Servitor's recording. The Foreman always carries one; a Guardian or a Repairer, about one time in twelve (8%).
Right-click opens the reading and files the writing in the notebook's §6Codex§r; the item stays, to keep or give away. Draws favor what you have not read yet.

Each first reading of a page or a module counts with the Restorers (+1 reputation, five a day at most). Notes give nothing. They are just there.

pages.title: Derelict blocks and dismantling
pages.text:
A ruin is made of §6derelict blocks§r: casings, ports and trade blocks (gearbox, pump, heater, coil, computer, sensor array, robot arm). None works, none forms a machine.
• Broken: a §lcasing§r or a §lport§r drops 1 to 2 structural scrap; a §ltrade block§r, 2 to 3 scrap of its category. Fortune counts.
• With §lSilk Touch§r: the block itself, for decoration; a crusher then turns it into 1 scrap (casing, port) or 2 (trade block).
• §lRubble§r sometimes gives a scrap (30%).
• Breaking a derelict block §lwakes§r the Sentinels within 12 blocks (except on Standby) and §lbreaks into§r the ruin: it can no longer be restored. Rubble does not.
The Salvage skill makes breaking faster, and every derelict block broken by hand gives its XP.

pages.title: Scrap
pages.text:
Twenty-four kinds of §6scrap§r: eight categories (structure, motion, fluids, thermal, electrical, electronics, sensors, robotics) in three tiers, MKI to MKIII. §lNo recipe makes any§r: it comes from ruins and Sentinels, and there is only so much of it.
• §lRecycler§r: the best use, but it comes at the end of a tier (next page).
• §lDismantling§r at the Metalworker's Bench, with a hammer: 1 MKI scrap → 2 steel nuggets. Never a component. The aluminum of MKII scrap and the titanium of MKIII scrap only come out of a recycler of their tier.
• §lSelling§r: traveling Peddlers buy all scrap (about 2, 7 or 19 Shining apiece from MKI to MKIII; for MKIII scrap, only one of each kind a day); Peddler villages buy MKI and MKII (2 and 6 Shining). Other villages refuse.
A scrap's tooltip gives its tier, its category and the recycler it needs.

pages.title: Recyclers
pages.text:
The §6recycler§r turns a scrap into §lcomponents of its own age§r, drawn at random within its category: simple parts come out often, key components (motors, pumps, processors) rarely. It only takes scrap: nothing you make can be recycled.
• §lCompact Recycler MKI to MKIV§r (Assembly Bench), and the §lIndustrial Recycler§r, a multiblock (Shift + right-click the controller: the plan). Each comes at the end of a tier and handles its tier and those below; there is no MKIV scrap, the MKIV only goes faster.
• §lTime§r: 40 s for an MKI scrap at MKI, 20 s for an MKII at MKII, 10 s for an MKIII at MKIII; each machine tier above goes twice as fast.
• §lDraws§r: 2 to 3 per scrap, +1 per machine tier above MKI; +25% for a Salvager. The owner's Salvage skill speeds up sorting.
• §lByproduct§r: a 25% chance of steel, aluminum or titanium dust, depending on the scrap's tier.
In JEI, one slot cycles through the draws; its tooltip gives the chance of each.

pages.title: Sentinels
pages.text:
Former perimeter Servitors: protect the site, refuse entry without clearance. Hostile to players only.
• §6Guardian§r (melee): 60 / 100 / 160 HP (MKI / MKII / MKIII); at MKIII, a front shield stops half of the hits from the front.
• §6Patroller§r (drone, shoots at 10 blocks): 20 / 30 / 40 HP; raises the alarm at MKII, dodges at MKIII.
• §6Turret§r (fixed, shoots at 18 blocks): 80 / 120 HP, MKII and MKIII; a charged, visible 1.5 s laser at MKIII.
• §6Repairer§r: 40 / 60 HP; heals its kind (4 HP/s within 6 blocks); shield bubble at MKIII.
• §6Foreman§r: MKIII only, 400 HP, armor 8, three phases, boss bar; it calls in Patrollers.
§lWaking§r: a player within 6 blocks in sight (3 sneaking; Patrollers 16 and 8) or a derelict block broken within 12 blocks; a fight wakes the whole site. §lLeash§r: never more than 40 blocks from its post; 30 s without a target and it goes back to sleep. Lightning and a plasma rifle shot §lstun§r them for 3 s.
Loot: robotics scrap of their tier, sometimes a memory module.

pages.title: Standby and the Console
pages.text:
Each ruin has its §6Perimeter Console§r: a four-digit keypad. The code is unique to the ruin.
• Where to find it: the §lService Note§r, in one of the Archive Cabinets, always in a guarded spot; or the §lConfidences§r of a villager who trusts you.
• §lRight code§r: the site goes on §6Standby§r for one game day. The Sentinels return to their posts and go back to sleep; breaking blocks no longer wakes anyone.
• §lThree wrong codes§r: the alarm wakes the whole site, and the Console locks for 5 minutes.
• Hitting a Sentinel during Standby breaks the Standby of the whole site.
Reading pays off: Standby counts with the Restorers (+6) and pleases villages within 400 blocks (+3 affinity, once a day). But you can also clear everything with a sword. Standby is not enough for a restoration: the site must have no Sentinel left.

pages.title: Restoring a ruin
pages.text:
Restoring costs more than building new. You do not do it to save: you do it to §lwake§r something up, for a village.
Right-click the §6Derelict Controller§r: the site sheet, in four stages.
1. §lSurvey§r: free; the list of parts, the duration, the cost. It needs an intact Controller, a ruin never broken into and the required Restoration level (0 at MKI, 3 at MKII, 6 at MKIII).
2. §lClearing§r: “Open the site”. The ruin's blocks become untouchable. Remove the §lrubble§r and destroy §lall§r the site's Sentinels.
3. §lRepair§r: the site uses up its reserve, day after day.
4. §lCommissioning§r: the ruin becomes the real multiblock of its tier.

pages.title: The site
pages.text:
• §lCost§r: three times the multiblock's bill of materials, and a cash share: 10% of its value in Shining (economy off: 48 steel, 96 aluminum or 160 titanium ingots depending on the tier).
• §lDuration§r: 5, 10 or 20 game days (MKI, MKII, MKIII). The Restoration skill of whoever opens the site cuts the cost (−20%) and the duration (−25%); a Scout pays 10% more.
• §lReserve§r: any player within 64 blocks drops in what they carry (“Deposit”); each contribution is recorded. A day only passes if the reserve covers that day's share.
• The site keeps going with its chunk unloaded; commissioning waits for the Controller to be loaded.
• §lWorkers§r: up to four villagers hired at the Needs Board, −10% duration each; with the skill, −60% at most.
• §lCancel§r (whoever opened it, Shift + click): half of the remaining reserve is returned.

pages.title: Back in service
From ore to shape
A metal's routes
Ore yields
Purity
pages.text:
A freshly reduced metal can be §limpure§r: a §lfull diamond§r on its icon (very impure) or a §lhalf-full§r one (slightly). With no mark it is pure.

Advanced recipes (stainless steel, nichrome, vacuum alloys, circuits) require §lpure§r inputs. §6Electrorefining§r makes a metal pure (and sometimes yields §lanode slime§r: gold, silver, platinum, osmium, iridium). Each tier above the recipe, and running it in a multiblock, removes one step of impurity.

pages.title: Iron and steel
pages.text:
§lIron§r (3 routes): MKI §6crusher§r, §6industrial crucible§r melting the crushed ore (144 mB ×1.5 at MKI, ×3 at MKIV) and §6casting machine§r (simple, from your first power: §l3 iron per ore at MKI§r, 6 at MKIV, no coke or pig iron; acid leaching from MKII: 5 to 7); in the §6blast furnace§r from §lpellets§r (screen, ore separator (magnetic separation), compactor: twice the iron; its gas heats the §6hot blast stove§r, its slag makes cement); by §ldirect reduction§r with syngas (MKII: sponge iron, then the §6arc furnace§r, two and a half times the iron, no coke).
§lSteel§r (4 routes), the MKI metal, §lonly in the blast furnace§r (1.0.5: never in the crucible, the converter or the arc furnace): §lpig iron§r in the crucible (2 crushed ore, 2 coke, 1 lime) refined in the §6blast furnace§r (simple); blast furnace pig iron refined with hot blast in the same blast furnace (large volumes, §lThomas slag§r for fertilizer); §lscrap bales§r melted into pig iron in the blast furnace, then refined (MKII: they recycle); crude steel blown with oxygen in the blast furnace (from MKI, with its §lvanadium slag§r), alloyed in the ladle in the crucible and cast in the §6industrial casting machine (continuous casting)§r (MKII: §lvanadium steel§r, slabs and billets straight away).

pages.title: Copper, tin, lead, zinc and gold
pages.text:
They all have iron's simple route: §6crusher§r, §6industrial crucible§r (raw ore, crushed ore or ore dust), §6casting machine§r: §l3 ingots per ore at MKI, 6 at MKIV§r, no byproduct; and §lacid leaching§r from MKII (5 to 7).
§lCopper§r: black copper in the crucible after roasting (simple: half the copper, impure); §lmatte§r, converter and §6electrorefining§r (complex: cathode copper for all electrical work, sulfuric acid and §lanode slime§r); leaching the §ltailings§r of every route, solvent extraction and electrowinning (MKII, no sulfur dioxide).
§lTin§r (two routes): ore separator (shaking table), roasting, reduction and liquation in the crucible, casting.
§lLead, zinc, silver§r: galena roasted and reduced (simple: the zinc fumes off, the silver stays in the lead); bulk flotation and shaft furnace, zinc condensed from its vapor; selective flotation, electrolytic zinc and lead desilvering (MKII: pure zinc, silver).
§lGold§r: ore separator (shaking table) (40% of the gold); amalgamation with mercury recovered from roasting gases (80%, a little mercury lost each cycle); anode slime in aqua regia (pure gold and a platinum-group solution, no gold ore needed).

pages.title: Nickel, vanadium and aluminum
pages.text:
§lNickel and cobalt§r: pentlandite roasted and smelted in the arc furnace (simple: §lferronickel§r, fine for stainless steel and invar, not for pure nickel); flotation, matte, converter and electrolysis (pure nickel and cobalt); pressure leaching, solvent extraction and the carbonyl process (MKII: very pure nickel and cobalt, platinum-group concentrate).
§lVanadium§r: ferrovanadium from the blast furnace's vanadium slag (oxygen blowing; free, but only a ferroalloy); ammonium metavanadate and pentoxide (catalysts, flow cells); aluminothermy and vacuum remelting (MKII: vanadium metal).
§lAluminum§r, the MKII metal: its §lfirst route§r runs at MKI, as the mastery test: bauxite ground and floated, §6Bayer digesters§r, drying, calcination into alumina, then the §6Industrial Electrolyzer (Hall-Héroult)§r (multiblock, Söderberg anodes, cryolite). Later: remelting offcuts compacted into bales (5% of the energy, but you need offcuts); prebaked anodes, recycled cryolite and iron from red mud (MKII, twice as fast).

pages.title: Magnesium, zirconium, niobium and platinum
Titanium, chromium and stainless steel
pages.text:
§lTitanium§r opens MKIII. Its §lfirst route§r, at MKII: ilmenite ground and separated, chlorination, distilled tetrachloride, the §6Kroll reactor§r (magnesium), sponge pressed into a compact, remelting in the industrial crucible (vacuum). MKIII adds §ldirect electrolysis§r of titanium slag (4 steps, no chlorine; commercial, impure titanium: no aluminide, nitinol or niobium-titanium), remelting §lbaled offcuts§r, and chlorinated slag in a fluidized bed with its magnesium-chlorine loop (twice the titanium, pig iron as a coproduct).
§lChromium§r: ferrochrome in the arc furnace (fast, it feeds stainless steel); sodium roasting and aluminothermy (chromium metal); electrolytic chromium through chrome alum (MKIII, 99.9%: superalloys).
§lStainless steel§r, from ferroalloys: ferrochrome, ferronickel and scrap in the induction furnace (plain, impure stainless); arc furnace then oxygen converter (in volume; the chromium in the slag comes back with ferrosilicon); argon-oxygen converter (MKIII: low-carbon, pure stainless).

pages.title: Tungsten, osmium and iridium
pages.text:
§lTungsten§r opens MKIV. Its §lfirst route§r, at MKIII, is long: wolframite ground and concentrated, caustic soda in the autoclave, extraction as §lammonium paratungstate§r, roasting into oxide, hydrogen reduction, powder pressed and then sintered in the §6industrial furnace (sintering)§r. At MKIV: §lhydrogen plasma§r reduction (4 steps, huge power draw) and ultrapure paratungstate with isostatic pressing (more tungsten per ore). The §lcarbide§r of worn tools is recycled with zinc (MKIII, 80% of the carbide).
§lOsmium and iridium§r only come from the §lplatinum-group residue§r: alkaline fusion, then tetroxide distilled in a §6hot cell§r (MKIII, both metals); chloride leaching and ion exchange (MKIV, twice as much per residue). The metals of other worlds round out MKIV (page “Metals of other worlds”).

pages.title: Metals of other worlds
pages.text:
Each world has its metal, processed at §lthat world's tier§r: MKIII for the Moon, Mars, Phobos, Deimos and meteorites, MKIV beyond; never in a furnace. Two routes each:
• the shared §lsimple§r route: raw ore in the §6crusher (fine grinding)§r, powder reduced under hydrogen in the §6industrial furnace (reduction)§r (two powders per ingot, worthless slag);
• the route of its §larchetype§r: §loxide§r (optical sorting, coke reduction, arc furnace refining: two ingots per ore, plus the world's byproduct at sorting); §lsulfide§r (flotation, sulfating roast into salts, electrolysis, vacuum remelting: sulfur, acid, and a precious metal at the cell); §lexotic§r (MKIV: optical sorting, then a §lsignature step§r in the chemical reactor with a block from that world (lunar sand, Martian clay, Ceres salt…), autoclave, remelting: two and a half ingots per ore).
Meteoritite comes from §lrocky meteorites§r that fall on Earth (ore separator (magnetic separation)). Iron, volcanic and ice meteorites give ferronickel, sulfur, water and carbon dioxide (MKIII).

pages.title: Silicon
Alloys
Semi-finished products and shapes
pages.text:
Parts of the §lbench metals§r (iron, copper, bronze, tin, brass, zinc, lead, gold, solder, steel) follow the routes of the page “Metal parts”: by hand at the §6basic components bench§r, or in machines at the metal's tier. Semi-finished products: §lslab§r (a block in the §6compactor§r), §lbillet§r (a slab in the compactor), §lwire rod§r (a billet in the §6rolling mill§r: 9 wire rods); a slab rolls into 9 plates, a billet extrudes into 18 rods.
Other metals are worked §lin machines only§r: melted in the crucible then cast in a §ldie§r (plate, rod, gear blank) at MKI, or forged into a §lbillet§r by the §6power hammer§r (titanium, tungsten, nichrome, metals of other worlds…); at §lMKII§r, the §6industrial casting machine (continuous casting)§r makes slabs, billets and beam blanks, which the §6rolling mill§r and the §6extruder§r turn without offcuts; wire rod goes to the §6power hammer (cold heading)§r (8 screws or bolts). §lMKIII§r: lubricated hobbing, precision springs, rolled rings, grinding, thin strip.

pages.title: The basic components bench
Metal parts
The extruder and its shapes
The shaping machines
The foundry
Cooling a casting
The compactor and its binders
The extractor: three techniques
The optical engraver and its objectives
Heat and surface treatment
pages.text:
The §6industrial furnace (heat treatment)§r (the former industrial furnace (heat treatment)) heats, then cools: §lquenching§r in water or oil (90% returned) for steel, tools, armor and the wrench; §ltempered glass§r; §lannealing§r; §lcarburizing§r and §lnitriding§r under ammonia for drill bits, saw blades, pins and dies.
The §6chemical bath§r (the former chemical bath) lays one metal over another: hot-dip §lgalvanizing§r (galvanized steel plates, rods, beams, sheets, wires and rings), §ltinning§r (tin cans), electroforming of nickel and copper (foils), silvering of mirrors.

pages.title: Glass and fiber
pages.text:
The §6industrial crucible (glass)§r melts industrial glass: soda glass and flat glass, colored glass from metal oxides (gold, cobalt, chromium, copper, silver), §lborosilicate§r frit and glass (MKII), §lfused silica§r and arc lamps (MKIII). The induction furnace no longer makes glass; the potter's kiln keeps plain glass.
The §6wiremill (fiber drawing)§r pulls molten glass or a precursor through a bushing: §lglass fiber§r (MKII), §loptical fiber§r and fluoride glass (MKIII, MKIV), §lcarbon§r fiber (pitch) and §laramid§r fiber (MKIII).

pages.title: Milling
pages.text:
§6Milling§r at the §lmachining center§r (formerly the Machining Center (milling)) removes material from a block: casting §ldies§r (ingot, plate, rod, gear) cut from vanadium steel, §lwax patterns§r and §lsand molds§r for the foundry, pickaxe heads from the billet (duralumin, stainless steel, titanium at MKII; stellite, nitinol, osmiridium, titanium aluminide, carbide at MKIV); its chips come back as nuggets.
Knife, saw and scythe blades are turned at the machining center; meshes are woven at the rolling mill (calendering); iron doors and bars are made at the metalworker's bench.

pages.title: Plasma spraying
pages.text:
§6Plasma spraying§r at the §lchemical bath§r (MKIII) melts a powder or a rod and sprays it as a coating over a nichrome bond coat: §ldiamond discs§r and Graviton plating (MKIII), modular gear plating, §ldrill heads§r rebuilt with metals of other worlds, and the iridium crucible (MKIV).
Mining hammer and pickaxe heads of the hard alloys are turned at the machining center or sintered in the industrial furnace; §lcarbide cutting tools§r are sintered in the industrial crucible, from tungsten carbide powder.

pages.title: Reading a process diagram
Process: Aluminum
pages.text:
§lAluminum§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 7 steps) — Bayer and molten salt electrolysis (first route): crushing → fine grinding → flotation → digestion → drying → roasting → molten salt electrolysis (Söderberg). §6+§r the only first aluminum; §6−§r huge energy, anodes to remake, red mud. First route: the test that opens the tier.
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 4 steps) — Remelting compacted offcuts: compacting → melting → casting. §6+§r 5% of the primary route’s energy, two machines; §6−§r depends on ruins and offcuts: no first aluminum. Alongside: recycling (Aluminum Dust).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 11 steps) — Prebaked anodes, red mud and recycled cryolite: crushing → fine grinding → flotation → digestion → drying → roasting → molten salt electrolysis (prebaked anodes). §6+§r more metal per alumina, twice as fast; iron from the red mud, recycled cryolite; §6−§r multiblocks and fluorine handling, petroleum coke. Alongside: compacting (Green Anode), sintering (Prebaked Anode), chemical reaction (Molten Cryolite), drying (Iron Dust).

pages.title: Process: Titanium
pages.text:
§lTitanium§r: 4 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 8 steps) — Kroll in a sealed retort (first route): crushing → fine grinding → magnetic sorting → chemical reaction → stripping → Kroll process → compacting → vacuum remelting. §6+§r the first titanium: the test that opens MKIII; §6−§r magnesium and chlorine, slow. First route: the test that opens the tier.
• §lSimple route§r (MKIII, 3 steps) — Vacuum remelting of baled offcuts: compacting → vacuum remelting. §6+§r simple, chlorine-free; bales melt at 95% and twice as fast; §6−§r depends on offcuts and ruin scrap. Alongside: vacuum remelting (Titanium Ingot).
• §lSimple route§r (MKIII, 4 steps) — Titanium slag and direct oxide electrolysis: crushing → magnetic sorting → melting → direct oxide electrolysis. §6+§r four steps, no chlorine or magnesium, more metal per ore than Kroll; §6−§r commercial (impure) titanium: not pure enough for the aluminide, nitinol or niobium-titanium.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIII, 10 steps) — Chlorinated slag in a fluidized bed, magnesium-chlorine loop: crushing → fine grinding → magnetic sorting → melting → fluidized bed chlorination → distillation → Kroll process → compacting → vacuum remelting. §6+§r twice as much titanium per ore, pig iron as a coproduct, magnesium and chlorine recycled; §6−§r argon, vacuum, fluidized bed. Alongside: electrolysis (Crude Magnesium).

pages.title: Process: Zirconium
pages.text:
§lZirconium§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Fused zirconia in the arc furnace: crushing → fine grinding → gravity tabling → arc furnace. §6+§r storable refractory in four steps (slurry for shell molds); also chlorinates in the Kroll route, faster than the concentrate; §6−§r no metal.
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 7 steps) — Chlorination and Kroll of the crude tetrachloride: crushing → fine grinding → gravity tabling → chemical reaction → Kroll process → compacting → vacuum remelting. §6+§r alloy-grade zirconium in seven steps; §6−§r hafnium included: less zirconium per tetrachloride, no hafnium oxide.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 9 steps) — Zirconium-hafnium separation and Kroll: crushing → fine grinding → gravity tabling → chemical reaction → hafnium separation → Kroll process → compacting → vacuum remelting. §6+§r nuclear-grade zirconium (zircaloy) and hafnium oxide for MOSFETs; §6−§r solvent (acetone), extraction column, more chlorine. Alongside: chemical reaction (Hafnium Oxide).

pages.title: Process: Tungsten
pages.text:
§lTungsten§r: 4 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIII, 10 steps) — Hydrometallurgy and hydrogen sintering (first route): crushing → fine grinding → gravity tabling → autoclaving → chemical reaction → drying → roasting → reduction → compacting → sintering. §6+§r the first tungsten: the test that opens MKIV; §6−§r hydrogen, long. First route: the test that opens the tier.
• §lSimple route§r (MKIII, 3 steps) — Zinc recycling of carbide: compacting → zinc condensation → fine grinding. §6+§r 80% of the carbide in cutting tools, no chemistry; §6−§r depends on worn tools; carbide only (no tungsten metal).
• §lSimple route§r (MKIV, 4 steps) — Hydrogen plasma reduction: crushing → gravity tabling → plasma reduction → plasma reduction. §6+§r four steps instead of ten, without APT chemistry; §6−§r huge electricity, coarse powder (sintered without pressing).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIV, 11 steps) — Ultrapure paratungstate and hot isostatic pressing: crushing → fine grinding → gravity tabling → autoclaving → solvent extraction → crystallization → roasting → reduction → compacting → hot isostatic pressing. §6+§r more tungsten per ore (solvent extraction, crystallization), dense ingot, fast; §6−§r solvent, ammonia, pressurized argon. Alongside: ammonia synthesis (Ammonia).

pages.title: Process: Platinum
pages.text:
§lPlatinum§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 3 steps) — Platinum sponge (aqua regia and cementation): chemical reaction → aqua regia refining → induction melting. §6+§r fast, three machines; §6−§r impure platinum; only half of the PGM residue comes out.
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 5 steps) — Ammonium chloroplatinate and calcination: leaching → chemical reaction → roasting → vacuum remelting. §6+§r pure platinum; §6−§r chlorinated reagents, ammonia. Alongside: centrifuging (Platinum-Group Concentrate).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIII, 10 steps) — Full PGM separation: PGM separation → solvent extraction → roasting → vacuum remelting. §6+§r platinum, osmium and iridium from one stream; half again as much platinum per solution; §6−§r many reagents, solvent, hot cell. Alongside: melting (Fused PGM Cake), hot cell work (Iridium Residue), chemical reaction (Osmium Dust), chemical reaction (Iridium Dust), sintering (Osmium Ingot) ….

pages.title: Process: Osmium
pages.text:
§lOsmium§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lComplex route§r (MKIII, 6 steps) — Alkaline fusion and tetroxide distillation in a hot cell: melting → hot cell work → chemical reaction → sintering. §6+§r both metals (osmium, iridium); §6−§r toxic tetroxide: hot cell; half of the residue. First route: the test that opens the tier. Alongside: chemical reaction (Iridium Dust), sintering (Iridium Ingot).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIV, 8 steps) — Chloride leaching and ion exchange: leaching → hot cell work → chemical reaction → sintering. §6+§r twice as much osmium and iridium per residue; §6−§r resins (solvent) to regenerate, two liquors, hot cell. Alongside: ion exchange (Iridium Residue), chemical reaction (Iridium Dust), sintering (Iridium Ingot), chemical reaction (Hydrochloric Acid).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIII, 10 steps) — Full PGM separation: PGM separation → melting → hot cell work → chemical reaction → sintering. §6+§r platinum, osmium and iridium from one stream; half again as much platinum per solution; §6−§r many reagents, solvent, hot cell. Alongside: solvent extraction (Ammonium Chloroplatinate), roasting (Platinum Dust), vacuum remelting (Platinum Ingot), chemical reaction (Iridium Dust), sintering (Iridium Ingot).

pages.title: Process: Iridium
pages.text:
§lIridium§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIII, 10 steps) — Full PGM separation: PGM separation → melting → hot cell work → chemical reaction → sintering. §6+§r platinum, osmium and iridium from one stream; half again as much platinum per solution; §6−§r many reagents, solvent, hot cell. Alongside: solvent extraction (Ammonium Chloroplatinate), roasting (Platinum Dust), vacuum remelting (Platinum Ingot), chemical reaction (Osmium Dust), sintering (Osmium Ingot).
• §lComplex route§r (MKIII, 6 steps) — Alkaline fusion and tetroxide distillation in a hot cell: melting → hot cell work → chemical reaction → sintering. §6+§r both metals (osmium, iridium); §6−§r toxic tetroxide: hot cell; half of the residue. First route: the test that opens the tier. Alongside: chemical reaction (Osmium Dust), sintering (Osmium Ingot).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIV, 8 steps) — Chloride leaching and ion exchange: leaching → hot cell work → ion exchange → chemical reaction → sintering. §6+§r twice as much osmium and iridium per residue; §6−§r resins (solvent) to regenerate, two liquors, hot cell. Alongside: chemical reaction (Osmium Dust), sintering (Osmium Ingot), chemical reaction (Hydrochloric Acid).

pages.title: Process: Chrome
pages.text:
§lChrome§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Ferrochrome in the arc furnace: crushing → fine grinding → magnetic sorting → arc furnace. §6+§r fast, feeds stainless steel; §6−§r iron included: a ferroalloy. First route: the test that opens the tier.
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 7 steps) — Sodium roasting and aluminothermy: crushing → fine grinding → magnetic sorting → chemical reaction → drying → aluminothermy → vacuum remelting. §6+§r chromium metal; §6−§r aluminum consumed. First route: the test that opens the tier.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIII, 8 steps) — Electrolytic chromium (chrome alum): crushing → fine grinding → magnetic sorting → arc furnace → crystallization → chromium electrowinning → vacuum remelting. §6+§r twice as much chromium per concentrate; 99.9%: superalloys, chrome plating; §6−§r sulfuric acid, ammonia, energy. Alongside: ammonia synthesis (Ammonia).

pages.title: Process: Silicon
pages.text:
§lSilicon§r: 5 routes (routes 1 to 4 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 1 step) — Metallurgical silicon in the arc furnace: arc furnace. §6+§r alloys (silicon steel, ferrosilicon); §6−§r 98%: no electronics.
• §lSimple route§r (MKIII, 3 steps) — Recycling scrap wafers: fine grinding → centrifuging → crystal pulling. §6+§r fast, no chemistry; §6−§r depends on wafer production.
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 5 steps) — Distilled trichlorosilane and Siemens deposition: arc furnace → fluidized bed → distillation → autoclaving. §6+§r polysilicon for solar cells and Gen 2 chips; §6−§r chlorine, hydrogen, tetrachloride to recycle. Alongside: autoclaving (Trichlorosilane).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 8 steps) — Czochralski single crystal: arc furnace → fluidized bed → distillation → autoclaving → crystal pulling → wafer sawing. §6+§r Gen 2 and Gen 3 wafers; §6−§r silica crucibles, argon. Alongside: autoclaving (Trichlorosilane), air separation (Nitrogen).

pages.title: Process: Silicon (continued)
pages.text:
§lSilicon§r: 5 routes (routes 5 to 5 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lComplex route§r (MKIII, 6 steps) — Chlorine-free metallurgical route: leaching and float zone: arc furnace → leaching → float zone refining → fine grinding. §6+§r polysilicon without chlorine or hydrogen, more polysilicon per silicon than Siemens deposition; §6−§r slow (float zone passes), small rods, hydrofluoric acid. Alongside: chemical reaction (Gypsum), air separation (Nitrogen).

pages.title: Process: Iron
pages.text:
§lIron§r: 4 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 5 steps) — Crusher, industrial crucible and casting: crushing → melting → casting. §6+§r 3 ingots per ore at MKI (crucible ×1.5), then 4 / 5 / 6 at MKII / MKIII / MKIV, three MKI machines from the very first power; §6−§r neither pig iron nor steel: steel goes through pig iron (see steel). Alongside: melting (Molten Iron), smelting (Iron Ingot).
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Acid leaching and electrolysis (MKII): crushing → leaching → aqueous electrolysis → smelting. §6+§r one ingot more than the crucible at the same tier: 5 / 6 / 7 ingots per ore at MKII / MKIII / MKIV; §6−§r sulfuric acid (250 mB per crushed ore), electricity; no byproduct.
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 7 steps) — Blast furnace on pellets: crushing → screening → magnetic sorting → compacting → blast furnace → converting. §6+§r twice as much iron; blast furnace gas heats the stove; slag for cement; §6−§r multiblocks (blast furnace, stove, converter), constant coke. Alongside: hot blast (Hot Blast).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 8 steps) — Reverse flotation and direct reduction with syngas: crushing → screening → fine grinding → selective flotation → compacting → direct reduction → arc furnace. §6+§r two and a half times as much iron, no coke; sponge iron opens direct steel in the arc furnace; §6−§r syngas to produce, massive electricity. Alongside: gasification (Syngas).

pages.title: Process: Steel
pages.text:
§lSteel§r: 4 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 3 steps) — Crucible pig iron and blast furnace: crushing → smelting reduction → blast furnace. §6+§r pig iron from the crucible, no pelletized ore; §6−§r small batches of pig iron (coke and lime), blast furnace multiblock for the steel.
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 6 steps) — Blast furnace: pig iron refined with hot blast: crushing → screening → magnetic sorting → compacting → blast furnace → blast furnace. §6+§r large volumes; Thomas slag (fertilizer); §6−§r two passes through the blast furnace; phosphorous steel, no special steel.
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 3 steps) — Scrap in the blast furnace: compacting → blast furnace → blast furnace. §6+§r recycles scrap, less ore; §6−§r coke, scrap to sort and compact, two passes through the blast furnace.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 9 steps) — Oxygen blast furnace, ladle metallurgy and continuous casting: crushing → screening → magnetic sorting → compacting → blast furnace → blast furnace → ladle metallurgy → continuous casting. §6+§r vanadium steel (plain steel comes from the blast furnace), direct slabs and billets; §6−§r oxygen from the industrial gas separator (air separation), long chain. Alongside: air separation (Oxygen).

pages.title: Process: Copper
pages.text:
§lCopper§r: 5 routes (routes 1 to 4 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 5 steps) — Crusher, industrial crucible and casting: crushing → melting → casting. §6+§r 3 ingots per ore at MKI (crucible ×1.5), then 4 / 5 / 6 at MKII / MKIII / MKIV, three MKI machines from the very first power; §6−§r no byproduct, plain metal. Alongside: melting (Molten Copper), smelting (Copper Ingot).
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Acid leaching and electrolysis (MKII): crushing → leaching → aqueous electrolysis → smelting. §6+§r one ingot more than the crucible at the same tier: 5 / 6 / 7 ingots per ore at MKII / MKIII / MKIV; §6−§r sulfuric acid (250 mB per crushed ore), electricity; no byproduct.
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 3 steps) — Black copper in the crucible: crushing → roasting → smelting reduction. §6+§r immediate; §6−§r half the copper, sulfur dioxide to handle; impure copper (electrorefine it for fine wire and electronics).
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 7 steps) — Matte, converter and electrorefining: crushing → fine grinding → flotation → roasting → smelting reduction → converting → electrorefining. §6+§r cathode copper for all electricity; sulfuric acid; anode slime (gold, silver, PGMs); §6−§r electricity, copper sulfate to maintain.

pages.title: Process: Copper (continued)
pages.text:
§lCopper§r: 5 routes (routes 5 to 5 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Tailings leaching, solvent extraction and electrowinning: leaching → solvent extraction → chemical reaction → electrolysis. §6+§r puts every route’s tailings to use, no sulfur dioxide; §6−§r slow, solvent to maintain, acid.

pages.title: Process: Tin
pages.text:
§lTin§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 5 steps) — Crusher, industrial crucible and casting: crushing → melting → casting. §6+§r 3 ingots per ore at MKI (crucible ×1.5), then 4 / 5 / 6 at MKII / MKIII / MKIV, three MKI machines from the very first power; §6−§r no byproduct, plain metal. Alongside: melting (Molten Tin), smelting (Tin Ingot).
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Acid leaching and electrolysis (MKII): crushing → leaching → aqueous electrolysis → smelting. §6+§r one ingot more than the crucible at the same tier: 5 / 6 / 7 ingots per ore at MKII / MKIII / MKIV; §6−§r sulfuric acid (250 mB per crushed ore), electricity; no byproduct.
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 6 steps) — Gravity tabling, roasting, reduction and liquation: crushing → gravity tabling → roasting → smelting reduction → melting → casting. §6+§r tin for solder and tinning; niobium from the heavy sands; §6−§r rich slag lost.

pages.title: Process: Lead
pages.text:
§lLead§r: 5 routes (routes 1 to 4 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 10 steps) — Crusher, industrial crucible and casting: crushing → melting → casting. §6+§r 3 ingots per ore at MKI (crucible ×1.5), then 4 / 5 / 6 at MKII / MKIII / MKIV, three MKI machines from the very first power; §6−§r no silver or byproduct: plain lead and zinc. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Zinc Ore), melting (Molten Lead), smelting (Lead Ingot), melting (Molten Zinc), melting (Molten Zinc) ….
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 8 steps) — Acid leaching and electrolysis (MKII): crushing → leaching → aqueous electrolysis → smelting. §6+§r one ingot more than the crucible at the same tier: 5 / 6 / 7 ingots per ore at MKII / MKIII / MKIV; §6−§r sulfuric acid (250 mB per crushed ore), electricity; no byproduct. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Zinc Ore), leaching (Acidic Zinc Solution), aqueous electrolysis (Zinc Dust), smelting (Zinc Ingot).
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 3 steps) — Galena roasted and reduced with coke: crushing → roasting → reduction. §6+§r fast; §6−§r zinc flies off, silver stays in the lead (impure).
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 9 steps) — Bulk flotation, shaft furnace and zinc condensation: crushing → flotation → roasting → smelting reduction → heat exchange → casting → casting. §6+§r lead and zinc from the same charge; §6−§r impure zinc and base bullion, two ores to blend. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Lead Ore), melting (Molten Lead).

pages.title: Process: Lead (continued)
pages.text:
§lLead§r: 5 routes (routes 5 to 5 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 12 steps) — Selective flotation, electrolytic zinc and lead desilvering: crushing → fine grinding → selective flotation → roasting → solution purification → electrolysis → desilvering → casting. §6+§r pure zinc (galvanizing, brass), silver, soft lead; §6−§r acid, electricity, many reagents. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Lead Ore), fine grinding (Ground Lead Ore), reduction (Lead Bullion), desilvering (Silver Nugget).

pages.title: Process: Zinc
pages.text:
§lZinc§r: 4 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 10 steps) — Crusher, industrial crucible and casting: crushing → melting → casting → casting. §6+§r 3 ingots per ore at MKI (crucible ×1.5), then 4 / 5 / 6 at MKII / MKIII / MKIV, three MKI machines from the very first power; §6−§r no silver or byproduct: plain lead and zinc. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Zinc Ore), melting (Molten Lead), smelting (Lead Ingot), melting (Molten Zinc), melting (Molten Zinc) ….
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 8 steps) — Acid leaching and electrolysis (MKII): crushing → leaching → aqueous electrolysis → smelting. §6+§r one ingot more than the crucible at the same tier: 5 / 6 / 7 ingots per ore at MKII / MKIII / MKIV; §6−§r sulfuric acid (250 mB per crushed ore), electricity; no byproduct. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Lead Ore), leaching (Acidic Lead Solution), aqueous electrolysis (Lead Dust), smelting (Lead Ingot).
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 9 steps) — Bulk flotation, shaft furnace and zinc condensation: crushing → flotation → roasting → smelting reduction → heat exchange → casting. §6+§r lead and zinc from the same charge; §6−§r impure zinc and base bullion, two ores to blend. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Lead Ore), melting (Molten Lead), casting (Lead Ingot).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 12 steps) — Selective flotation, electrolytic zinc and lead desilvering: crushing → fine grinding → selective flotation → roasting → solution purification → electrolysis. §6+§r pure zinc (galvanizing, brass), silver, soft lead; §6−§r acid, electricity, many reagents. Alongside: crushing (Crushed Lead Ore), fine grinding (Ground Lead Ore), reduction (Lead Bullion), desilvering (Silver-Zinc Crust), desilvering (Silver Nugget) ….

pages.title: Process: Gold
pages.text:
§lGold§r: 5 routes (routes 1 to 4 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 5 steps) — Crusher, industrial crucible and casting: crushing → melting → casting. §6+§r 3 ingots per ore at MKI (crucible ×1.5), then 4 / 5 / 6 at MKII / MKIII / MKIV, three MKI machines from the very first power; §6−§r no byproduct, plain metal. Alongside: melting (Molten Gold), smelting (Gold Ingot).
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Acid leaching and electrolysis (MKII): crushing → leaching → aqueous electrolysis → smelting. §6+§r one ingot more than the crucible at the same tier: 5 / 6 / 7 ingots per ore at MKII / MKIII / MKIV; §6−§r sulfuric acid (250 mB per crushed ore), electricity; no byproduct.
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 4 steps) — Gravity separation on the ore separator: crushing → gravity tabling → melting → casting. §6+§r immediate; §6−§r only 40% of the gold.
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 7 steps) — Mercury amalgamation and distillation: crushing → fine grinding → leaching → fired heating → melting → casting. §6+§r 80% of the gold; §6−§r 10% of the mercury lost each cycle (mercury drawn from roasting gases). Alongside: chemical reaction (Mercury).

pages.title: Process: Gold (continued)
pages.text:
§lGold§r: 5 routes (routes 5 to 5 here). JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Refining anode slime with aqua regia: aqua regia refining → chemical reaction → melting → casting. §6+§r pure gold, silver and a PGM solution, without gold ore; §6−§r depends on the complex copper route; aqua regia.

pages.title: Process: Nickel
pages.text:
§lNickel§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 3 steps) — Pentlandite roasted and smelted in the arc furnace: crushing → roasting → arc furnace. §6+§r immediate; §6−§r a ferroalloy: stainless steel and invar yes, pure nickel no.
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 6 steps) — Flotation, matte and electrolysis: crushing → fine grinding → flotation → smelting reduction → converting → electrolysis. §6+§r pure nickel and cobalt; §6−§r electricity, converter.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 10 steps) — Pressure leaching, solvent extraction and carbonyl: crushing → fine grinding → flotation → pressure leaching → solvent extraction → crystallization → reduction → carbonyl process → carbonyl process. §6+§r nickel and cobalt separated, very pure; PGMs; §6−§r carbon monoxide, autoclave, solvent and hydrogen. Alongside: reduction (Cobalt Dust).

pages.title: Process: Vanadium
pages.text:
§lVanadium§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKI, 2 steps) — Ferrovanadium from blast furnace slag: arc furnace. §6+§r a free byproduct of steel; §6−§r ferroalloy only (vanadium steel). Alongside: blast furnace (Crude Steel).
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 7 steps) — Roasting, leaching and ammonium metavanadate: crushing → fine grinding → flotation → roasting → leaching → chemical reaction → roasting. §6+§r pentoxide: catalysts, flow cells; lead recovered; §6−§r no pure metal.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 9 steps) — Aluminothermy and vacuum remelting: crushing → fine grinding → flotation → roasting → leaching → chemical reaction → roasting → aluminothermy → vacuum remelting. §6+§r vanadium metal: fusion first wall, titanium alloys; §6−§r aluminum consumed, argon.

pages.title: Process: Magnesium
pages.text:
§lMagnesium§r: 2 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 4 steps) — Magnesia and ferrosilicon under vacuum (Pidgeon process): chemical reaction → roasting → silicothermic reduction. §6+§r no electrolysis or chlorine; §6−§r slow, ferrosilicon consumed, one magnesia for half an ingot. Alongside: arc furnace (Ferrosilicon).
• §lComplex route§r (MKI, 5 steps) — Dehydrated bischofite and molten chloride electrolysis: leaching → fluidized bed → electrolysis → melting → casting. §6+§r chlorine given back (Kroll, chemistry); titanium-magnesium loop: Kroll chloride goes back to the cell; §6−§r tricky dehydration under hydrochloric acid.

pages.title: Process: Niobium
pages.text:
§lNiobium§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 3 steps) — Pyrochlore and ferroniobium by aluminothermy: crushing → gravity tabling → aluminothermy. §6+§r fast ferroalloy, then dissolved in hydrofluoric acid for niobium; §6−§r ferroalloy only.
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 7 steps) — Hydrofluoric attack, solvent extraction and aluminothermy: crushing → gravity tabling → leaching → solvent extraction → roasting → aluminothermy → vacuum remelting. §6+§r niobium metal; §6−§r hydrofluoric acid, fluorinated raffinate to recycle.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIV, 9 steps) — Pressure attack, recycled fluorides and electron beam: crushing → gravity tabling → autoclaving → solvent extraction → roasting → reduction → electron beam melting. §6+§r half again as much niobium per concentrate, fluorine recycled, superconducting niobium (electron beam melting); §6−§r high vacuum, hydrofluoric acid. Alongside: stripping (water), chemical reaction (Gypsum).

pages.title: Process: Stainless Steel
pages.text:
§lStainless Steel§r: 3 routes. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lSimple route§r (MKII, 1 step) — Ferrochrome, ferronickel and scrap in the induction furnace: induction melting. §6+§r fast, one machine; §6−§r uncontrolled carbon: plain (impure) stainless steel. First route: the test that opens the tier.
• §lComplex route§r (MKII, 3 steps) — Arc furnace and oxygen converter: arc furnace → oxygen converter. §6+§r common stainless steel in volume; chromium from the slag recovered with ferrosilicon; §6−§r oxygen to produce, chromium lost in the slag. First route: the test that opens the tier. Alongside: reduction (Ferrochrome).
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIII, 4 steps) — Argon oxygen converter: arc furnace → argon oxygen decarburization. §6+§r low-carbon stainless steel (nuclear, cryogenics), pure; little chromium in the slag; §6−§r argon and compressed air. Alongside: reduction (Ferrochrome), air separation (Nitrogen).

pages.title: Process: Vanadium Steel
pages.text:
§lVanadium Steel§r: 1 route. JEI: “Process” page, §lR§r on the product. Each route, from the starting material to the product:
• §lVery complex route§r (MKII, 9 steps) — Oxygen blast furnace, ladle metallurgy and continuous casting: crushing → screening → magnetic sorting → compacting → blast furnace → blast furnace → ladle metallurgy → continuous casting. §6+§r vanadium steel (plain steel comes from the blast furnace), direct slabs and billets; §6−§r oxygen from the industrial gas separator (air separation), long chain. Alongside: air separation (Oxygen).

pages.title: Process: Metals of the worlds
pages.text:
The §l30 metals of the worlds§r follow one pattern: a §lsimple route§r (grinding, hydrogen reduction) and the route of their §larchetype§r (oxide, sulfide, exotic), at the world’s tier. The diagram shows one world per archetype; JEI has one page per metal.
• §lSimple route§r (MKIV, 2 steps) — Grinding and hydrogen reduction (world pattern, simple route): fine grinding → reduction. §6+§r common reagents, two machines; §6−§r yields little (two dusts per ingot), worthless slag, hungry reduction. Every world with ore.
• §lComplex route§r (MKIV, 5 steps) — Oxide archetype: optical sorting, coke reduction and arc furnace refining: optical sorting → reduction → arc furnace. §6+§r two ingots per ore; the world’s byproduct at sorting; §6−§r coke, electrodes and argon; hungry reduction. Alongside: sintering (Graphite Electrode), air separation (Nitrogen). Worlds: Borealite, Deimite, Edenite, Pallasite, Phobite, Sulcite, Tolimanite, Valhallite, Veronite, Vestalite.
• §lComplex route§r (MKIV, 5 steps) — Sulfide archetype: flotation, sulfating roast, electrolysis and remelting: flotation → roasting → electrolysis → vacuum remelting. §6+§r two ingots per ore, sulfur and acid, precious metal at the cell; §6−§r electricity, sulfuric acid. Alongside: chemical reaction (Sulfuric Acid). Worlds: Hygeite, Lokite, Mercurium, Messinite, Mordorite, Pyrrhite, Terminite, Tharsium, Venusium.
• §lVery complex route§r (MKIV, 8 steps) — Exotic archetype: the world’s signature step: optical sorting → world signature step → autoclaving → vacuum remelting. §6+§r two and a half ingots per ore; a material of its own; §6−§r a block of the world to bring back, hot cell and cracker for the active residues. Alongside: fired heating (sand), chemical reaction (Hydrochloric Acid), electrolysis (Hydrogen), air separation (Nitrogen). Worlds: Ahunite, Conamarite, Flarium, Krakenite, Lunarium, Marsium, Ruachite, Sputnikite, Thalassite, Tigrite.
