pages.title: The four tiers
pages.text:
Every machine exists in §lMKI§r (basic), §lMKII§r (advanced), §lMKIII§r (elite) and §lMKIV§r (ultimate); one-block machines are called "compact", multiblocks "industrial". At MKI a machine uses §l1,024 FE/t§r; each tier costs §lx4 energy for x2 speed§r. A new machine accepts energy through §levery face§r. §lCleanroom§r machines are the exception: no tier, a fixed capacity (page “Multiblock shapes”).

Why go up: many recipes need a §6minimum tier§r, that of their material or their process (page “Machine tiers”); above a recipe's tier the machine runs faster; ore yields §lx1 / x1.25 / x1.5 / x2§r; metals come out purer. An §6upgrade kit§r moves a machine to the next tier keeping everything (right-click).

pages.title: Machine tiers
pages.text:
A machine only runs recipes of §lits own tier or a lower one§r. A recipe's tier comes from two locks:
• the §lmaterial§r: each tier has its own, only obtained by moving on: §lMKI§r steel; §lMKII§r aluminum (duralumin, magnesium); §lMKIII§r titanium (chromium, stainless steel); §lMKIV§r tungsten (osmium, iridium) and the metals of other worlds. It makes the §6frame§r, the §6fasteners§r, the §6casings§r and the §6upgrade kit§r of the tier;
• the §lprocess§r: some are §lreserved§r for a tier: continuous casting, hot rolling, extrusion, cold heading, Kroll, solvent extraction (MKII); vacuum remelting and casting, sintering, oxide electrolysis, helical hobbing, grinding, liquid nitrogen (MKIII); plasma, electron beam, isostatic pressing, liquid helium, signature steps of other worlds (MKIV).
The §lfirst batch§r of a tier material is always made at the tier before (the mastery test: first aluminum at MKI, first titanium at MKII, first tungsten at MKIII), and a §ltier N casing§r is made with tier N−1 machines: enough to build the tier's first multiblocks.
A machine whose tier is too low shows “§lTier too low: MKIII required§r” and uses nothing up; in the §6recipe selector§r, a red corner marks those recipes. Above a recipe's tier: x2 speed per tier (x4 energy), x4 parallelism in multiblocks, ore x1.25, x1.5, then x2.

pages.title: The assembly bench
pages.text:
The §6assembly bench§r is reserved for §lmachines§r and §lmultiblock§r parts (controllers, casings, ports, modules, radiators), no longer in the grid. Three neighboring benches share the rest (1.11.1):
• the §6basic components bench§r: ingot-based components, by hand (plates, rods, wires, springs, gears…);
• the §6advanced components bench§r: the component catalog (frames, motors, bearings, pumps, circuits, kits);
• the §6logistics parts bench§r: rockets and spaceport, railroad tracks and posts, harbors, robotics, hypertubes (vehicles are made at the §6railroad works§r and the §6shipyard§r).
Each one has its automatable §ltwin machine§r (4 tiers and a multiblock): the §6press (forming)§r, the §6assembler (components)§r and the §6assembler (logistics)§r; the §6assembler§r keeps the machines.

1. Put the §6wrench§r in a tool slot.
2. Put the parts in the 6 material slots: frames, circuits, plates, motors… in whole stacks.
3. The grid shows what can be built: buildable machines come first, lit. Pick one, then “Make” (or “× n” for all).
It is crafted in the grid: steel plates and rods, steel ingots, a wrench and the metalworker's bench.

pages.title: Sides and ejection
pages.text:
Every machine has a §lsides panel§r: a tab on the right edge of its interface. It shows the unfolded block (front, back, sides, top, bottom, seen from the front) and §lone chip per resource§r: items, fluids, gases, heat, compressed air, data. Each resource has its own settings.
• Click a side: next setting; right-click: previous. §lClosed§r (gray), §linput§r (blue), §loutput§r (orange), §linput and output§r (green).
• The switch at the bottom right: §lautomatic ejection§r of that resource; the machine pushes its output into whatever touches its output sides (cable, chest, machine).
• “Close all” closes the resource's sides; some sides are reserved by the machine (front, screen).
• §lEnergy§r enters through every side of a machine, and leaves through every side of a generator, whatever the other settings.
With a cable: a neutral plug receives what the machine ejects; an input plug pulls from its output sides.

pages.title: The recipe selector
The machine interface
pages.text:
Every machine has §lthe same interface§r: compact MKI to MKIV machines, mechanical and steam machines, generators, buffers, platform posts, industrial and special multiblocks.
• §lAt the top§r: the name, then the §6tier chip§r (MKI to MKIV, in the tier's color) or the §lage chip§r (Mechanical, Bronze; Industrial for some workbenches); a small §lmultiblock icon§r when the machine also exists in a large version.
• §lOn the left§r: energy (reserve, battery below) or §lmotive power§r (rotation speed with its useful range, pressure gauge, firebox); then the inputs, the §lRecipe§r slot above the arrow, the outputs and their gauges; at the bottom, the §lstatus screen§r: state, bar, two values.
• §lTool slot§r (gold edge, below the arrow; 1.0.5-beta): a machine whose recipes give their tool back (§6dies§r, molds, extrusion dies and shapes, catalysts, photomask, etching objectives…) keeps it in this reserved slot, never in an input. The recipe reads it there and gives it back; §lshaping tooling§r (molds, dies, extrusion dies and shapes, mandrel) is §lunbreakable§r in a machine (returned 100% of the time, never consumed), catalysts and the other tools wear with the recipe's chance; cables, hoppers, multiblock ports and Shift + click put it there, ejection never empties it. Empty slot: an icon and, in the tooltip, the accepted tools; JEI's “+” places the tool.
• The §linventory§r sits inside the frame, below the machine; the interface opens centered.
• §lTabs on the right§r: §lRecipes§r (the §6selector square§r, laid over the machine), §lSides§r (inputs and outputs per resource, ejection), §lRedstone§r, §lInfo§r (tier, consumption, speed, recipes, sides, short help), and §lStructure§r for a multiblock.
• §lUnformed multiblock§r: the machine is grayed out, the §lNot formed§r chip replaces the tier and a red band says §lwhat to fix§r, §lwhere§r (right, up, deep, counted from the controller) and the §lexpected block§r; the Structure tab shows the state, the size, the first fault and two buttons: §lShow the plan§r (the projection, like Shift + right-click) and §lSee in JEI§r.
The §6workbenches§r keep their grid of parts, in the same frame (age chip, Info tab); the §6computer§r, the logic controllers and the relay cabinet keep their editing screens.

pages.title: Generic machines
pages.text:
Patch 1.0.4: fewer, more generic machines. One machine per §6role§r (crush, sort, smelt, melt…); the specialties that did the same job are §lmerged§r into it: their recipes move to the base machine §lat the same tier§r (same inputs, outputs, durations), sorted by §lfamilies§r.
Merged machines: ball mill, flotation cell, magnetic separator, shaking table, optical sorter, roasting furnace, reduction furnace, sintering furnace, heat treatment furnace, diffusion furnace, vacuum furnace, glass furnace, steam cracker, delayed coker, fluid catalytic cracker, hydrocracker, catalytic reactor, fluidized bed reactor, polymerizer, catalytic reformer, fischer-tropsch reactor, ammonia plant, nitric acid plant, steam methane reformer, gasifier, vulcanizer, membrane cell, electrorefiner, fluorine plant, hall-héroult potline, anaerobic digester, distillation tower, vacuum column, stripping column, leaching tank, solvent extractor, oil press, decanter, desalter, cyclone separator, crystal puller, psa unit, air separation unit, gas processing plant, laser isotope separator, chiller, plate heat exchanger, reprocessing plant, vitrification furnace, photobioreactor, brine well, oil derrick, gas wellhead, forming station, industrial forging press, cold header, calender, fiber draw tower, wire strander, spring coiler, continuous caster, injection molder, cnc mill, precision grinder, gear hobber, wafer saw, plasma sprayer, acid etcher, component assembler, logistics assembler, arc welder.
§6Existing worlds§r: a merged machine already placed becomes the base machine at the same tier, with its contents (slots, tanks, energy, sides, locked recipe). A multiblock built for a merged machine reforms if it fits the base's template; otherwise it shows “Not formed” and the base's blueprint (Shift + right-click the controller): its blocks stay in place.
When two recipes share the same inputs, the machine takes its own recipe first; lock the other one in the §lRecipes§r tab.

pages.title: The crusher
pages.text:
The §lcrusher§r stays the kit machine (same mechanism: raw ore into 2 crushed ores, its fixed duration) and also does the §6fine grinding§r of the former ball mill: crushed ore → dust, often with a little §lwater§r (an extra fluid tank).
§6Families§r
• §lCrushing§r (own recipes): 8 recipes
• §lFine grinding§r (former ball mill): 94 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The ore separator
pages.text:
The §lore separator§r (formerly the vibrating screen) §6concentrates§r ore by every physical route: screening, flotation (water and reagent: 2 inputs, water tank), magnetic separation, gravity tabling, optical sorting (up to 4 outputs).
§6Families§r
• §lScreening§r (own recipes): 17 recipes
• §lFlotation§r (former flotation cell): 25 recipes
• §lMagnetic separation§r (former magnetic separator): 15 recipes
• §lGravity (table)§r (former shaking table): 9 recipes
• §lOptical sorting§r (former optical sorter): 28 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: crushed ilmenite, crushed redstone ore, tailings. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The industrial furnace
pages.text:
The §lindustrial furnace§r (formerly the electric furnace, still the kit machine for smelting) gains five §6families§r: §loxidize§r (roasting sulfides, sulfur dioxide out), §lreduce§r (oxide + reductant + flux), §lsinter§r (powders under gas), §lheat-treat§r (quench, anneal, carburize: the quench fluid has an input and an output tank) and §ldope§r (wafers under phosphine or diborane). Three inputs, two outputs, one fluid and one gas tank each way.
§6Families§r
• §lSmelting§r (own recipes): 18 recipes
• §lOxidize (roasting)§r (former roasting furnace): 32 recipes
• §lReduce§r (former reduction furnace): 60 recipes
• §lSinter§r (former sintering furnace): 46 recipes
• §lHeat-treat (quench, anneal)§r (former heat treatment furnace): 17 recipes
• §lDope (diffusion)§r (former diffusion furnace): 8 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The industrial crucible
pages.text:
The §lindustrial crucible§r (formerly the electric crucible) melts metals and ore, and takes over §6vacuum§r work (reactive metals under argon, float-zone silicon, Josephson junction…) and the §6glass§r of the former glass furnace (soda glass, float glass, borosilicate frit, fused silica, arc lamp…). Three solid inputs (+ one gas) → one molten metal and a byproduct (slag). Since 1.0.5-beta, §6direct§r alloys (solid → solid) are made in the §linduction furnace§r, a machine of its own again, and the crucible no longer makes plain steel: steel comes from the §lblast furnace§r.
§6Families§r
• §lMelt§r (own recipes): 356 recipes
• §lVacuum§r (former vacuum furnace): 51 recipes
• §lGlass§r (former glass furnace): 13 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Cracker
pages.text:
The §lCracker§r (formerly the fired heater) §6cracks§r hydrocarbons. Its multiblock, the §lindustrial cracker§r, takes over §lsteam cracking§r (ethane, naphtha → ethylene, propylene), §ldelayed coking§r (residues → petroleum coke), §lcatalytic cracking§r (vacuum gas oil → gasoline) and §lhydrocracking§r (under hydrogen and pressure): §lmultiblock-only§r recipes. The compact keeps the fired heater's recipes: visbreaking, pyrolysis of plastics and sludge, activated carbon, carbon black, acetylene, vinyl chloride, radon, catalyst regeneration, fat rendering.
§6Families§r
• §lHeating§r (own recipes): 28 recipes
• §lSteam cracking§r (former steam cracker; multiblock only): 9 recipes
• §lDelayed coking§r (former delayed coker; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lCatalytic cracking§r (former fluid catalytic cracker; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lHydrocracking§r (former hydrocracker; multiblock only): 11 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: fuel oil, atmospheric residue. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The chemical reactor
pages.text:
The §lchemical reactor§r gathers all synthesis. Compact and multiblock: §6catalysis§r (the catalyst goes in an input slot; it comes back 95% of the time, wears out 5% of the time and is regenerated at the Cracker), the §lfluidized bed§r (uranium conversion) and §lpolymerization§r (pellets, PTFE, butyl rubber). Multiblock only: §lcatalytic reforming§r, §lFischer-Tropsch§r, §lammonia§r (Haber-Bosch, under pressure), §lnitric acid§r (Ostwald), §lsteam reforming§r and §lgasification§r. Two item inputs and three outputs, three fluid tanks each way, three gas inputs and two outputs.
§6Families§r
• §lSynthesis§r (own recipes): 87 recipes
• §lCatalysis§r (former catalytic reactor): 26 recipes
• §lFluidized bed§r (former fluidized bed reactor): 14 recipes
• §lPolymerization§r (former polymerizer): 8 recipes
• §lCatalytic reforming§r (former catalytic reformer; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lFischer-Tropsch§r (former fischer-tropsch reactor; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lAmmonia (Haber-Bosch)§r (former ammonia plant; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lNitric acid (Ostwald)§r (former nitric acid plant; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lSteam reforming§r (former steam methane reformer; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lGasification§r (former gasifier; multiblock only): 11 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: hydrogen and nitrogen (iron catalyst), natural gas and steam, methane and steam, ammonia and oxygen, nitrogen dioxide and water. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The autoclave
pages.text:
The §lautoclave§r runs reactions under pressure (leaching, composites, urea, soda ash, zeolite) and takes over the §6vulcanization§r of the former vulcanizer: vulcanized rubber, rubber sheets, soles, coated canvas, tires, conveyor belts. Its MKI model is built with a §lleather gasket§r: it is the machine that makes the rubber for rubber gaskets.
§6Families§r
• §lAutoclaving§r (own recipes): 32 recipes
• §lVulcanization§r (former vulcanizer): 9 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The electrolyzer
pages.text:
The §lelectrolyzer§r splits water, brine and molten salts, and takes over §6membrane electrolysis§r (caustic soda, hypochlorite, deuterium, tritium, lithium) and §lelectrorefining§r (pure metals). Multiblock only: §lfluorine§r and §lHall-Héroult aluminum§r (alumina from the Bayer digesters, cryolite, anodes). The industrial electrolyzer's controller is built with two §lcarbon anodes§r, like the former potline.
§6Families§r
• §lElectrolysis§r (own recipes): 26 recipes
• §lMembrane electrolysis§r (former membrane cell): 8 recipes
• §lElectrorefining§r (former electrorefiner): 16 recipes
• §lFluorine§r (former fluorine plant; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lAluminum (Hall-Héroult)§r (former hall-héroult potline; multiblock only): 8 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: brine. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The fermenter
pages.text:
The §lfermenter§r makes ethanol, drinks and fermented food, and takes over the §6anaerobic digestion§r of the former anaerobic digester: biomass + water → §lbiogas§r, digestate and a little fertilizer.
§6Families§r
• §lFermentation§r (own recipes): 39 recipes
• §lAnaerobic digestion§r (former anaerobic digester): 16 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: vegetables, fruit, wheat. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The distillation column
pages.text:
The §ldistillation column§r (multiblock only, formerly the atmospheric column: each fraction leaves through the port tier at its height) distills crude oils and takes over the §6rectification§r of the former tower (alcohols, benzol, tar, liquid air), §lvacuum distillation§r (residues → vacuum gas oil, base oils, paraffin) and the §lstripping§r of the former stripping column (sour gas and water, Girdler heavy water, spirits from the still). A compact stripping column already placed becomes the column's controller (its contents do not follow).
§6Families§r
• §lAtmospheric distillation§r (own recipes): 8 recipes
• §lRectification§r (former distillation tower; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lVacuum distillation§r (former vacuum column; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lStripping§r (former stripping column): 12 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: bitumen, heavy crude oil, raw oil, synthetic crude, coal tar, crude titanium tetrachloride. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The extractor
pages.text:
The §lextractor§r pulls a substance out of its carrier with hot water, steam, a solvent or supercritical CO₂, and takes over the §6leaching§r of the former tank (acids and cyanide on crushed ores: metal solutions for the electrolyzer), the §lsolvent extraction§r of the former solvent extractor (uranium, nickel, cobalt, rare earths, platinum group) and the §loil pressing§r of the former press (seeds, fish, algae → oil and press cake; kitchen juices). Two item inputs and two outputs, two fluid tanks each way, one gas tank.
§6Families§r
• §lExtraction§r (own recipes): 42 recipes
• §lLeaching§r (former leaching tank): 30 recipes
• §lSolvent extraction§r (former solvent extractor): 9 recipes
• §lOil pressing§r (former oil press): 25 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: press cake and naphtha. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The centrifuge
pages.text:
The §lcentrifuge§r separates phases by density (sugar, cream, honey, red mud; the light isotopes — lithium-6, carbon-13, nitrogen-15 — stay here) and takes over the §6decanting§r of the former decanter (water, oil, sludge), crude §ldesalting§r (desalted crude, brine) and the gas §ldust removal§r of the former cyclone separator. Its MKI model has a bowl driven by a §lleather belt§r.
§6Families§r
• §lCentrifuging§r (own recipes): 16 recipes
• §lDecanting§r (former decanter): 9 recipes
• §lDesalting§r (former desalter): 8 recipes
• §lDust removal (cyclone)§r (former cyclone separator): 8 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: red mud, produced water. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The crystallizer
pages.text:
The §lcrystallizer§r grows crystals and gems (salts, sulfates, Verneuil gems) and takes over the Czochralski §6crystal pulling§r of the former crystal puller: single-crystal silicon ingots and gem boules, to be sawn into wafers.
§6Families§r
• §lCrystallization§r (own recipes): 11 recipes
• §lCrystal pulling (Czochralski)§r (former crystal puller): 8 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Gas Separator
pages.text:
The §lGas Separator§r (formerly the membrane separator) splits gas mixtures: §6membranes§r (helium, hydrogen, nitrogen) and §lPSA adsorption§r (pure hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen), compact and multiblock. Multiblock only: the §lair separation§r of the former unit (nitrogen, oxygen, argon, neon, krypton, xenon; only in an atmosphere, as before) and the §lgas processing§r of the former plant (raw gas → methane, ethane, LPG, condensate; sulfur and helium). The industrial separator's controller is built like the former gas processing plant (heat exchangers, mesh, pump).
§6Families§r
• §lMembranes§r (own recipes): 8 recipes
• §lAdsorption (PSA)§r (former psa unit): 8 recipes
• §lAir separation§r (former air separation unit; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lGas processing§r (former gas processing plant; multiblock only): 8 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: refinery gas. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The centrifuge cascade
pages.text:
The §lcentrifuge cascade§r (multiblock only) enriches uranium hexafluoride stage by stage and takes over the §6laser separation§r of the former laser isotope separator: the same isotopes, faster at MKIV (lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab). A compact laser separator already placed becomes the cascade's controller: its items drop on the ground.
§6Families§r
• §lGas centrifuging§r (own recipes): 6 recipes
• §lLaser separation§r (former laser isotope separator): 6 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: carbon dioxide, uranium hexafluoride, enriched uranium hexafluoride, HALEU hexafluoride, nitrogen, depleted uranium hexafluoride. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Cryogenic Unit
pages.text:
The §lCryogenic Unit§r (formerly the gas compressor) compresses and §6liquefies§r gases (LPG, LNG, liquid hydrogen), takes over the §lrefrigeration§r of the former chiller (below 250 K: liquid chlorine, butane, cold crystallization) and the §lheat exchange§r of the former plate heat exchanger (heat recovery, vaporization of liquefied gases).
§6Families§r
• §lCompression, liquefaction§r (own recipes): 13 recipes
• §lRefrigeration§r (former chiller): 8 recipes
• §lHeat exchange§r (former plate heat exchanger): 12 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: ammonia, natural gas, hydrogen, butane. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Hot Cell
pages.text:
The §lHot Cell§r is now a §6multiblock only§r: it opens irradiated targets, separates isotopes, makes sources and takes over the PUREX and THOREX §lreprocessing§r of the former plant (uranium, plutonium, neptunium, waste) and the §lvitrification§r of high-level waste of the former furnace. Its controller is built with lead and stepper motors; its trade block, the manipulator station, with the tempered glass of the window. A compact hot cell already placed becomes the controller: its items drop on the ground.
§6Families§r
• §lHandling§r (own recipes): 11 recipes
• §lReprocessing (PUREX)§r (former reprocessing plant; multiblock only): 8 recipes
• §lVitrification§r (former vitrification furnace): 8 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: high-level waste, irradiated thorium blanket and nitric acid. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The hydroponic farm
pages.text:
The §lhydroponic farm§r (multiblock only) grows crops at scale and takes over the §6microalgae§r of the former photobioreactor (water + CO₂ + light → microalgae, algae oil, oxygen). A compact photobioreactor already placed becomes the farm's controller: its items drop on the ground. Trees have their own machine again, the §ltree plantation§r.
§6Families§r
• §lCrops§r (own recipes): 174 recipes
• §lMicroalgae§r (former photobioreactor): 8 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The pumpjack
pages.text:
The §lpumpjack§r (multiblock only) pumps §6every fluid deposit§r below it: oil, brine (formerly the brine well) and natural gas (formerly the gas wellhead), with associated gas and helium through its second gas output. Injected water or mud restores pressure. The oil derrick is merged into it too: its advancement is earned at four operations at once. A well multiblock already built does not have the pumpjack's shape: “Not formed”, pumpjack blueprint with Shift + right-click.
§6Families§r
• §lOil§r (deposits of the former pumpjack)
• §lBrine§r (deposits, former brine well)
• §lDeep oil§r (deposits, former oil derrick)
• §lGas§r (deposits, former gas wellhead)
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Press
pages.text:
The §lPress§r (formerly the electric press) only §6flattens§r: ingot + die → plate, plate → sheet or foil, laminates pressed flat (plywood, epoxy board, perforated and etched boards). Anything that does not flatten is made at the machine of its action: rods and tubes at the extruder or the machining center, rivets and nails at the power hammer (cold heading), compacts and pellets at the compressor, slabs and panes at the industrial saw, mixes at the mixer, assemblies at the assembler. The forming station is merged into it; a station already placed becomes a Press of the same tier. The compact steam press is its tier 1.
§6Families§r
• §lPressing§r (own recipes): 89 recipes
• §lForming§r (former forming station): no recipe (its copies duplicated other machines)
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Power Hammer
pages.text:
The §lPower Hammer§r forges by impact: billets of non-castable metals, die-forged gear blanks, punched and seamless rolled rings. It takes over the §6cold heading§r of the former cold header (screws, bolts, rivets, nails and balls, from wire rod or wire) and, in its multiblock only, the §lIndustrial Power Hammer§r, the §lhot forging§r of tool heads and blades of the former industrial forging press. The forge hearth keeps its two bloom recipes. It no longer has a steam age: the steam hammer is gone (1.0.5).
§6Families§r
• §lDrop forging§r (own recipes): 69 recipes
• §lHot forging (tool heads)§r (former industrial forging press; multiblock only): 100 recipes
• §lCold heading (fasteners)§r (former cold header): 15 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Rolling Mill
pages.text:
The §lRolling Mill§r (formerly the electric rolling mill) §6rolls§r between cylinders: ingot → plate, plate → foil, slab → plates, billet → wire rod, and now §lblock → 9 plates§r (MKII, the former cutting table route). It takes over the §lcalendering§r of the former calender: rubber and plastic sheets, gaskets, sheets, woven meshes.
§6Families§r
• §lRolling§r (own recipes): 165 recipes
• §lCalendering§r (former calender): 34 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: plate (foil or sheets), slab (plates or sheets). The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Wiremill
pages.text:
The §lWiremill§r (formerly the electric wiremill) §6draws§r metal into wire: ingot, wire rod or rod → wire, wire ropes. It takes over the §lfiber drawing§r of the former fiber draw tower (glass, optical and fluoride glass fibers, carbon and aramid fibers: the molten glass or the precursor enters through its tank) and the §lstranding§r of the former wire strander (lossless wire ropes, wiring harnesses, network cables, hemp ropes).
§6Families§r
• §lWire drawing§r (own recipes): 52 recipes
• §lFiber drawing§r (former fiber draw tower): 8 recipes
• §lStranding§r (former wire strander): 8 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: hemp fiber, wire (wire rope). The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The bender
pages.text:
The §lBender§r bends and rolls: rings, seamed tubes, bent plates and tubes. It takes over the §6coiling§r of the former spring coiler: springs from wire, rod or wire rod, oil-tempered precision springs at MKIII (an extra fluid tank).
§6Families§r
• §lBending§r (own recipes): 29 recipes
• §lCoiling (springs)§r (former spring coiler): 40 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: copper rods (lightning rod or spring), iron rods (iron bars or spring), metal rod (rings or spring). The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The casting machine
pages.text:
The §lCasting Machine§r casts liquid metal in a mold (die or foundry mold, coolant) and takes over the plastic §6injection molding§r of the former injection molder (pellets + mold → parts). In its multiblock only, the §lcontinuous casting§r of the former caster: ingots in series, slabs, billets, beam blanks, under water or oil at MKIII.
§6Families§r
• §lMold casting§r (own recipes): 412 recipes
• §lContinuous casting§r (former continuous caster; multiblock only): 81 recipes
• §lInjection molding§r (former injection molder): 9 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: liquid metal and die (part or continuous casting). The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Machining Center
pages.text:
The §lMachining Center§r (formerly the CNC lathe) machines from stock: shafts, screws, blades, tool heads and precision parts. It takes over the §lmilling§r of the former CNC mill (dies, foundry patterns and molds), the §lgrinding§r of the former precision grinder (tungsten fasteners, balls, gems, objectives) and the §6gear hobbing§r of the former gear hobber (from a blank or plates, lubricated at MKIII). The metal 3D printer is removed: its heads and tools are made here, in the industrial furnace and in the industrial crucible; a printer already placed becomes a Machining Center at the same tier.
§6Families§r
• §lTurning§r (own recipes): 175 recipes
• §lMilling§r (former cnc mill): 15 recipes
• §lGrinding§r (former precision grinder): 23 recipes
• §lGear hobbing§r (former gear hobber): 45 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: vanadium steel plates and lubricant, duralumin plates. The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Industrial Saw
pages.text:
The §lIndustrial Saw§r (formerly the sawmill) saws wood (logs → planks, sticks and sawdust) and takes over the §6wafer slicing§r of the former wafer saw (silicon ingots and gem boules → wafers). The cutting table is removed: its blades are turned at the machining center, its wires are drawn, its meshes are woven at the rolling mill and its “block → 9 plates” moves to the rolling mill; a cutting table already placed becomes an Industrial Saw at the same tier.
§6Families§r
• §lSawing§r (own recipes): 17 recipes
• §lWafer slicing§r (former wafer saw): 8 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The Chemical Bath
pages.text:
The §lChemical Bath§r (formerly the surface treatment tank) treats surfaces in its baths: galvanizing, zinc, tin, nickel and copper plating, hard chrome, electroforming, silvering. It takes over the §lplasma spraying§r of the former booth (molten powder coatings: diamond discs, platings, rebuilt drill heads; up to six inputs) and the §6acid etching§r of the former etcher (exposed wafers → etched wafers, chips).
§6Families§r
• §lSurface baths§r (own recipes): 16 recipes
• §lPlasma spraying§r (former plasma sprayer): 10 recipes
• §lAcid etching§r (former acid etcher): 8 recipes
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The assembler
pages.text:
The §lAssembler§r builds parts and components. It takes over §6all§r the recipes of the former component assembler (frames, motors, bearings, pumps, circuits, computers, at the same tiers), the logistics parts bench copies of the former logistics assembler (rockets, spaceport, rail, harbors, robotics) and the §larc welding§r of the former welder (tanks, hulls, welded tubes, casings, under argon from MKII). Nine inputs, two outputs, one fluid and one gas tank.
§6Families§r
• §lAssembly§r (own recipes): 10 recipes
• §lComponents§r (former component assembler): 196 recipes
• §lLogistics parts§r (former logistics assembler): no recipe (its copies duplicated other machines)
• §lArc welding§r (former arc welder): 20 recipes
§6Same inputs§r: steel plates (armor or welded beam), steel plates, rods and screws (wrench or welded frame). The machine's own recipe (otherwise the most complete one) goes first; for the other one, lock it in the §lRecipes§r tab.
JEI: a single category, each recipe carries its family chip.

pages.title: The water generator
pages.text:
The §6water generator§r (MKI to MKIV) makes §lwater from nothing§r: power it, it fills its tank and §lejects through the sides§r you set (Sides tab), into a logistic cable or a tank.
• Flow per tier: MKI: 25 mB/t (pump: 200); MKII: 100 mB/t (pump: 800); MKIII: 400 mB/t (pump: 3,200); MKIV: 1,600 mB/t (pump: 16,000). It stays §lless efficient than the multiblock pump§r of the same tier (a quarter at most; here an eighth, a tenth at MKIV), but it fits in one block and works anywhere, with no water source below.
• It draws the power of any machine of its tier (1,024 FE/t at MKI, ×4 per tier), only while producing; with a full tank it waits.
• For a lot of water (cooling towers, industrial boilers), the §6multiblock pump§r remains the right machine.

pages.title: The rock generator
pages.text:
The §6rock generator§r (MKI to MKIV) endlessly remakes the rock of a §lsample§r: put a rock block in its §lreserved slot§r (gold edge, below the arrow), fill its two tanks with §l1,000 mB of water§r and §l1,000 mB of lava§r, power it: the same rock comes out, one every 2 / 1 / 0.5 / 0.25 s (MKI to MKIV).
• The sample is §lnever consumed§r; the water and lava are §lnever drained§r: they just have to be there.
• Rocks per tier: MKI stone, cobblestone, granite, diorite, andesite, sandstone; MKII those of MKI, tuff, calcite, dripstone, basalt, netherrack; MKIII those of MKII, deepslate, blackstone; MKIV those of MKIII, end stone, rocks of the celestial bodies (sample brought back from space).
• §lNever§r an ore or a rock worth a resource (obsidian, magma, glowstone, amethyst…): the slot refuses them and says why on hover (and which tier a deep rock needs).

pages.title: The component catalog
pages.text:
Pioneer's has §l383 components§r in 19 families: wood, glues, textiles, shapes, fasteners, structure, glass, motion, fluids, heat, electrical, semiconductors, electronics, computing, sensors, tooling, robotics, nuclear and space. Each one has §lan age§r (primitive, mechanical, bronze, MKI to MKIV, cosmic) and is made of subcomponents and materials of that age, never later ones.

They are sorted by family in the §lComponents§r creative tab. In JEI, R on a component shows its recipes, U what uses it: every one is used somewhere.

§6The tier material§r: steel at MKI, aluminum at MKII, titanium at MKIII, tungsten at MKIV (with cast iron, duralumin and magnesium, chromium and stainless steel, iridium and osmium). Frames, screws and bolts only exist in these four metals; before steel, you rivet with copper and nail with iron.

§6Two ways§r: up to MKI, most parts can also be made at a bench (base yield); a machine makes more of them. Beyond that, machines only.

Mechanical parts by tier
The projected blueprint
pages.text:
Every multiblock is built the same way:
1. Place the §6controller§r (made at the assembly bench).
2. §lShift + right-click the controller with an empty hand§r: the blueprint appears as ghost blocks. Again: next variant or size, then hide. Correctly placed blocks vanish from the blueprint; blocks in the way show in red.
3. Place the blocks; until the structure is complete, the controller screen says what to fix, §lwhere§r (“3 to the right, 1 down” from the controller) and the expected block; its §lStructure§r tab counts the blocks by role and shows the blueprint again (“Show the plan”, “Show in JEI”).
In creative, Shift + right-click while holding the controller builds everything.

A multiblock's §ltier§r is that of its weakest part (casing, glass, frame, sheet). §6Ports§r take the place of a wall part:
• industrial multiblocks: the wrench switches them between input and output; they sort what comes in and eject what goes out by themselves;
• space multiblocks (launch complex, stabilizer, simulator, greenhouse, garage…): the port is §lspecialized§r (wrench right-click: read; sneak + right-click: change): items, fluid, gas or data, as input or output.
A comparator against the controller reads the fill level, or 15 while the machine runs. Leave one block of space between two multiblocks.

pages.title: Industrial multiblocks
pages.text:
Every workshop machine has an §lindustrial§r counterpart, and each multiblock has its own §lstructure§r, designed block by block (1.0.4): §6casings§r, §6sheet metal§r, §6frames§r, §6industrial glass§r, §6firebox walls§r, §6heating coils§r, stackable blocks, cleanroom… The §6controller§r has §lits own spot§r in the structure (often in the middle of the front, at ground level); the §linner§r cells stay empty (air or water; no more work modules, except the data center's server racks).

§lShift + right-click the controller with an empty hand§r: the blueprint shows, block by block (each machine has a single size; the structure can be built in all four orientations). The tier is that of the §lweakest tiered part§r (casing, pane, sheet, frame, firebox wall, coil, stackable block); it alone sets the §lparallelism§r: 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 operations. An operation takes §l80% of the time§r and §l75% of the energy§r, and every byproduct comes out. Leave a one-block gap between two multiblocks.
§6Ports§r go in place of a §lcasing§r, a §lsheet§r (the port then takes its look, joined to the neighboring sheets) or a cleanroom casing, never a frame or a pane (“misplaced port”); the blueprint marks with a §lsmall orange frame§r the cells where a port is allowed. They are only set to §linput or output§r (wrench): as inputs they §lsort by themselves§r what comes in (each ingredient on its own stack, slots kept for the other ingredients, one tank per fluid or gas, water to the cooling of a machine that heats up first); as outputs they §leject by themselves§r every product to their neighbors.

pages.title: Structure blocks
Multiblock shapes
pages.text:
Since 1.0.4, the §l64 industrial multiblocks§r each follow the §6structure§r designed by Guillaume, with a §lsingle size§r: furnaces on their bed of fireboxes, distillation towers, sheet-metal vessels and tanks, glass halls for farms, cleanrooms, open-frame drills and pumps… The projected blueprint shows it block by block and the controller tooltips give its size.
These keep their §lprevious template§r: the §6offshore platform§r (free shape, its deck in the blueprint), the fission and fusion reactors, the §6cooling tower§r, the gravity compressor, the synthesizer, the propellant plant, the rail works and the shipyard.
A few structures are §ladjusted§r: a column of §6turbine rotors§r in the middle of the turbines, the §6centrifuge cascade§r bays left free (real centrifuges spin there). All the others are exactly the blueprints.
§lCleanroom§r machines (optical engraver, semiconductor fab, data center, quantum computer, which keeps its §6dilution refrigerator§r) have neither casing nor tier: their §lcapacity is fixed§r. Engraver and fab: §l16 operations at once§r, 15,360 FE/t each; data center: §l256 GOPS§r per rack (8,192 FE/t at full load); quantum computer: §l8 QOPS§r per array (16,384 FE/t). Their controller is §lwhite§r, blended into the wall, and their interface is light. Old shapes built in a world come apart cleanly (“Not formed”, contents kept): rebuild from the blueprint. Once formed, the multiblock takes its family's §llook§r and the machine comes alive inside: fit §6industrial glass§r to look inside.

pages.title: Built machines: frames and sheet metal
pages.text:
Structures are §lbuilt like the real thing§r: every block has a role, shown by the blueprint.
• §6frames§r (steel, aluminum, titanium, tungsten: one per tier): open rod frameworks of §ldrills§r, §lpumps§r, §lpresses§r, §lproduction lines§r and §lhalls§r;
• §6sheet metal§r (same metals): welded wall of §lcontainers§r: tanks, vessels, columns, bins; a pane or a port can take the place of a sheet (the port takes its look).
Cells outside the structure (between legs, around a tower) are free. Like a casing, the weakest frame or sheet sets the multiblock §ltier§r.

pages.title: Building blocks
Industrial chimney and item silo
Heat and cooling
pages.text:
A multiblock heats up with every operation (×1.5 per tier, up to 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 operations at once). It sheds some heat to the air: a §lslow§r machine (crusher, sifter, press…) runs without cooling at every tier, as do all of them at MKI and MKII; MKIII and MKIV §lfurnaces§r and big chemical plants need cooling:
• §6heat ports§r to logistic cables (heat channel) and §6radiators§r, or a §6cooling tower§r;
• a §6coolant§r in a fluid port: §lwater§r becomes §lsteam§r, a gas that leaves through a §6gas port§r (for the turbine), §lcoolant§r turns hot (boiler or cooling tower), §lliquid nitrogen§r boils off. The full loop is on the next page.
Above the casings' rating the machine §lslows down§r; at +20% it §lstops§r; at +35% a casing §lburns§r and the structure breaks.

pages.title: The water loop

pages.text:
On the left, the §lchannels§r; in the middle, the §lschematic§r: machines (with their icon) and junctions, joined by lines without length.
• A channel carries one type (items, fluids, gases, energy, heat, pressure, data) between the connected machines. 16 channels per network.
• Click a channel: it is colored in the diagram. Click again: its settings (type, filter, distribution, flow).
• Click a machine: its role in the chosen channel, the face used (independent of the one the cable touches), priority and limits.
• Wheel: zoom. Drag the background: scroll. Drag a machine: move it (for every player).
• Identical machines with the same settings: one ×N node, set at once. Shift + click: unfold or regroup.
• Copy / Paste (top): the whole configuration, settings stored by machine type.
• Shift + right-click a plug: diagram opened on that machine. Wrench: cut or restore a side.
• The weak link (cable of the lowest level) limits the whole network: click it to see it in the world.
Settings are drafts: nothing changes before §lConfirm§r. Viewing the diagram needs the right to interact in the territory; changing it, the right to use its machines.

pages.title: Channels
Points and faces
pages.text:
A §lpoint§r = a machine in a channel. Its role:
• §lInput§r (machine → cable): with “pull”, the cable empties the machine; without it, it only takes what the machine ejects;
• §lOutput§r (cable → machine); §lBoth§r; §lNone§r (a machine at “None” in every channel is §lunplugged§r: the cable removes its plug, it stays grayed out in the diagram).
The §laccess face§r is independent of the face the cable touches: you can §linject from the top§r even if the cable is plugged in at the bottom. The cube net shows what each face offers for the channel's type (green: accepts, red: gives, purple: both, gray: closed); the chosen face is ringed in gold. The machine's own side settings are respected.
Then: §lpriority§r (−99 to 99: the highest inputs empty first), §lweight§r (proportional distribution), §lkeep in stock§r (an input only gives the surplus), §lfill up to§r (an output receives no more), §lmax flow§r and §lown filter§r (5 slots, on top of the channel's).

pages.title: Distribution
Heat and pressure
The levels
The superconducting cable
Chutes and pipes
pages.text:
Before steel, logistics are made of wood: the §6wooden logistic cable§r (carpenter's bench, saw: 3 planks + 1 iron ring → 6) carries §litems§r (4 per second) and §lfluids§r (160 mB/t of water, creosote or brine), but §lno hot fluid§r (above 400 K: lava, molten metal).

It is the same cable as in the later ages (bronze, then MKI to MKIV): they all connect, and the network takes the level of the weakest. A machine drops its output into the plug; the §6noria§r fills a cable placed above or beside it; boilers, the beam engine and mills take from it. §lRight-click§r the cable: the network diagram, to choose who gives and who receives (“Logistics” chapter). Bronze Age steam travels in the §6bronze cable§r.

pages.title: Logistics: from wood to steel
Cables and tanks
pages.text:
§lCorrosives§r (strong acids, fluorine, chlorine, hydrogen chloride and fluoride…) and §lcryogenics§r (below 150 K: LNG, liquid oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and helium) only travel in the logistic cable §lMKII or better§r, lined with §6PTFE§r. A network containing a lower-level cable refuses them: no leak, no explosion, they stay in the machine.

The §6industrial storage tank§r (fluids) and the §6gas holder§r (gases) are multiblocks without modules: their capacity grows with their inner volume and tier (x4). Comparator: fill level. The §6bottler§r fills and empties buckets of every fluid.

pages.title: Buffers
The trash can
pages.text:
One block to get rid of clutter: the §6trash can§r destroys whatever is sent to it, through §lany side§r — §litems§r, §lfluids§r, §lgases§r (steam included) and §lenergy§r. It refuses §lheat§r, §lcompressed air§r (air is not a resource) and §ldata§r: cables do not connect to it on those channels.
It is made early, at the §lcoppersmith's bench§r with a hammer: 4 bronze sheets, 1 wooden hopper, 2 flint.
• Plug it at the end of a §6logistic cable§r (any level) and pick it as a destination in the diagram; or put it under a §lhopper§r, next to a §lbuffer§r that ejects, a multiblock port or a boiler: whatever goes in disappears.
• To get rid of §lheat§r, use a §6radiator§r; compressed air is kept in an air buffer.
• §lRight-click§r: its screen. §l“Throw away”§r slot: the stack you drop is destroyed; the last one can be §ltaken back§r while the screen is open (a new stack replaces it for good). §l“Empty”§r slot: a bucket, can, tank or battery is emptied at once, the container stays to take back.
Nothing is kept: the trash can has no storage and no setting, and costs the server nothing.

pages.title: A network with no distance limit
pages.text:
A §6logistic cable§r can cross the world: the network stays §lwhole§r even when sections are in §lunloaded§r chunks. The server keeps the layout of every cable (level, links, plugs): it never reads an unloaded chunk and never forces one to load.
• A machine whose chunk is not loaded is §lpaused§r: nothing leaves it, nothing enters it; it resumes as soon as its chunk loads. No item is ever “on its way” inside the cable: nothing is lost or duplicated when chunks unload.
• To keep a far site working while you are elsewhere, place a §6chunk loader§r there.
• In the diagram (right-click a cable), machines are grouped into §lsites§r: those at most §l48 blocks§r from one another form a site, drawn in its frame as before (“Site A”, number of machines, paused machines). Sites sit side by side in the order you see them; a §lline§r joins them and shows the §ltrue distance§r (as the crow flies, in blocks; the cable length is in its tooltip).
• “§lRearrange§r” at the top tidies the whole diagram; the button on a site's header tidies that site only. Paused machines are grayed out, with two orange bars.
In an older world, each chunk is surveyed the first time it loads: a network running through an area not reloaded since fills in as you travel.

pages.title: Unplugged machine: “None” everywhere
pages.text:
In a network with channels, a machine set to §l“None”§r in §levery§r channel is §lunplugged§r: the cable removes its arm and plug toward it, no more exchange (no pulling, no delivery, no ejecting into the cable, no digital network).
• It stays in the diagram, §lgrayed out§r, marked “unplugged” (red badge): give it a §lrole§r in a channel and the cable plugs back in at once. Its settings (face, priority, filters) are kept.
• A machine placed against a network with channels starts at “None” everywhere: it shows unplugged until you give it a role. In §lauto mode§r (a network never set up), everything stays plugged.
• §lShift + click§r on the cable side facing it opens the diagram on that machine. The §lwrench§r on that side §lcuts§r it: it then leaves the network and the diagram (wrench again: restored).

pages.title: The bag interface
pages.text:
The §6bag interface§r reads the bag put in its slot: its §lcontents§r become the block's inventory, on all §lsix faces§r. A §6logistic cable§r plugs into it like into a chest (channels, filters, priorities); a hopper stores or takes items there.
• §lBackpacks§r: their slots as they are. §lStorage bags§r (seeds, saplings, fishing basket): one slot per kind, shown as stacks of 64 (best genes first); only their kind goes in, up to their capacity.
• The contents §lstay in the bag§r: taking the bag out takes them along, nothing is copied, even in the middle of a transfer. The bag itself never leaves through a cable or a hopper.
• It is made at the §lcarpenter's bench§r with a saw: 4 treated wood, 1 wooden hopper, 2 leather, 2 iron nails.
The §6warehouse inlet§r also has a §lbag slot§r: put your full bag there, its contents leave as parcels for the crates; the empty bag stays in the slot.

pages.title: The warehouse crate
pages.text:
A big steel-hooped shipping crate, as a §lmultiblock§r: §l3 wide, 3 high§r, and §l3, 5 or 7 long§r (any horizontal direction). The §6crate frame§r (steel) goes on every edge, the §6panels§r (treated wood) on the faces, the inside stays empty. The §6hatch§r goes in the middle of the top: it is the heart and holds everything. Once formed, the crate gets boards, riveted angles, hoops and stencils (Shift + right-click the hatch, empty hand: the blueprint).

Capacity: §l256 item types§r per crate, whatever its length; the length sets the number of stacks for each type:
• §l3×3×3§r: 256 types × 32 stacks;
• §l3×5×3§r: 256 types × 64 stacks;
• §l3×7×3§r: 256 types × 128 stacks (over 2 million ingots).
These 256 types are §ltype slots§r: an item whose slot is full §loverflows§r into the free slots (a crate can hold a single item); taken out, it gives them back.
§lPlayers never open the crate§r: items go in and out through the §6ports§r (in place of a panel: hoppers, logistic cable) or through the §6counter§r. Looking at the crate shows its card (fill, types, most common items); a comparator reads the fill.
Breaking a part undoes the crate and loses nothing. Breaking the §lhatch§r carries all its contents: placed back in a crate, everything returns.

pages.title: Ropes, pulleys and counter
pages.text:
The §6warehouse network§r is everything the ropes link together. Put a §6small pulley§r with a §lvertical axis§r §labove the hatch§r of each crate and §labove the counter§r (placed on it, or higher in the line: next page); link them with the mod's ropes (§6fiber rope§r, tarred rope, leather belt: click a pulley, then another; a green or red line shows the rope before the second click). Pulleys must be §lat the same height§r, 24 blocks apart at most, with no solid block between them; up to §l4 ropes§r per pulley (junctions along the aisles), if everything turns the same way.

§lThe ropes must turn§r: a shaft above or below a pulley, driven by a windmill, a horse mill, a steam engine… Rotation passes from pulley to pulley through the ropes. Parcel speed = rope speed (a small pulley at 40 rpm: 1.3 blocks/s). §lWithout rotation, nothing moves§r and the counter says so.

At the §6counter§r, like at a terminal: §lthe whole warehouse in a grid§r (search, sort by count, by name or by mod). §lClicking an item puts it in the cart§r, nothing leaves yet: click = one stack, Shift + click = one item, Ctrl + click = one parcel (4 stacks), right-click = one stack less; the §lCart§r button opens the cart panel (− / + / × and the mouse wheel adjust each line). Then §l“Order”§r (or Enter): the whole cart leaves at once; whatever can’t leave (stock gone in the meantime, queue full) stays in the cart and the counter says why. The cart is kept, even with the screen closed. For each type, a §lsmall crate§r rises from the hatch holding the most of the item, hangs from the rope, goes around the wheels, comes down onto the counter and opens: the items drop into the §loutput§r (3×3; a hopper below empties it). Then the empty crate goes back. 24 parcels on the way at most; requests wait their turn (“On the way”: the queue, the parcels, “Cancel queue”).
The other way: a hopper or a cable §lon the side§r of the counter fills its send slots, and each stack leaves as a parcel for a crate with room.

pages.title: Relays and a counter on the ground
pages.text:
§lThe counter goes on the ground§r, under the line: the §6small pulley§r right above it, §lup to 8 blocks higher§r, serves it if §lnothing is in between§r (no block, no water). The parcel leaves the rope at the wheel and §lcomes down on its line§r (the carriage’s winch unwinds) onto the counter top, then goes back up. To place it without scaffolding: §lShift + right-click the top of the counter§r with the small pulley, it goes by itself to the height of the nearby line (gold outline before clicking). The same goes for crates: a line can run higher than their hatches. Looking at the pulley tells what it serves (“Counter station (2-block drop)”) or why it doesn’t (block in the column, too high, pulley too big). With a rope in hand, the drop column is outlined in gold. The old way (a pulley placed on the counter) still works.

All §6pulleys§r (small, medium, large) placed with a §lvertical axis§r work as §lrelays§r, at the same height; only the §lsmall§r one is also a §lstation§r (its rim passes right above the hatch or the counter tray; its wheel sits a little higher in its block). Parcels go around the wheels, just under the rim: nothing solid below, except the shaft carrying the wheel (a relay can stand on an upright shaft). Rotation passes both ways, at the size ratio: the rope has the same speed everywhere and parcels follow it. A pulley with a horizontal axis carries no parcels (they hang under the rope).

pages.title: Warehouse inlet and outlet
pages.text:
Two more §lstations§r on the line, set up like the counter: a §6small pulley§r above (up to 8 blocks higher, clear column), tied by the ropes; same diagnosis in the Info tab.
The §6warehouse inlet§r: §leverything put in its 9 slots leaves as parcels§r for the crate that already holds the item, otherwise one with room: hopper, cable, conveyor or by hand. Crates full: the slots stay full and nothing more comes in (nothing is lost, the card says “Crates full”). A hopper can't take anything back out.
The §6warehouse outlet§r: §lreceives parcels§r and keeps them in its 9 slots. Two ways to fill it:
• §l“Keep in stock”§r: up to 6 rules (drop an item, or drag it from JEI; − / + / wheel for the amount): the outlet asks for what is missing by itself;
• at the counter, §l“Deliver to”§r (cart panel): pick the outlet, the order arrives there instead of the counter.
Placed §lagainst a machine or a chest§r (click its face), its chute faces it and pushes the items in: a machine always fed. A hopper or a cable below empties it too.
The counter keeps its send slots: a hopper on its side still sends to the crates. The crates' ports stay too: a hopper against the crate itself, without a rope.

pages.title: The counter and JEI
pages.text:
The counter is narrow so the §lJEI list§r stays visible next to it. With the counter open, open a recipe in JEI (R on an item): its §l“+”§r button asks the warehouse for the ingredients.
• §l“+”§r: the recipe once §linto the cart§r;
• §lShift + “+”§r: as many times as the stock allows (64 at most);
• §lCtrl + “+”§r: into the cart, then §l“Order”§r right away (to the destination picked in the cart).
The §lrequested recipe§r shows at the top of the cart: product, number of crafts and ingredients. §lMouse wheel§r on the recipe: ±1 craft (§lShift§r: ±10), the ingredients follow; §l×§r removes it with its ingredients.
§lMissing§r slots are §lred§r in JEI, with the missing count; the button's tooltip says what leaves and what is missing. For a slot with several possible items (all planks, an ingot tag), the counter takes §lthe ones it has most of§r, and mixes them if one isn't enough. Vanilla recipes, benches and the mod's machines: anything that asks for items (fluids are not requested). Nothing of the recipe in the warehouse, or counter not linked: the button is grayed out, with the reason.
The §l“On the way”§r card says why an order waits (rope stopped, output full, 24 parcels out, column blocked); a click opens the details and “Cancel queue”.

pages.title: The counter can’t see the crate?
Several ropes per pulley
pages.text:
A pulley takes up to §l4 ropes§r, whatever its axis: one coming in, three going out, or a warehouse junction. Ropes sit in §ltwo grooves§r (low, high) in turn and cross without touching. Each rope is a drive: all linked pulleys share the same speed (at the size ratio), and each rope adds its losses (rope efficiency): the load adds up.

§lCondition: everything must turn the same way.§r If the two systems already turn against each other at the rope's ratio, the rope is refused, with the reason (cross it with Sneak, or lay it straight). If the two pulleys are already linked by another drive at another ratio, it is refused too: it would jam the whole network. The green or red preview line says so before the second click.
§6Warehouse posts§r and the §6warehouse pulley§r are gone: pulleys hold by themselves, like shafts; an old warehouse pulley has become a small pulley, ropes kept.

pages.title: Caravans
pages.text:
Before the railroad, goods travel on animals’ backs. A §6caravan§r is a §llead animal§r and up to §l5 followers§r in single file, going by themselves from §6relay§r to relay: they §lload§r at one, §lunload§r at another, and eat along the way.
§6The pack saddle§r (tanner: 4 leather, 2 planks, 2 fiber ropes, 2 bronze rings): right-click a tamed horse, a donkey, a mule, a camel or a dromedary, adult, with no saddle or chest. Its §lslots§r depend on the animal’s §lpack load§r (one slot per 9 kg):
• §lCamel§r: pack 220-260 kg → 24-27 slots
• §lDromedary§r: pack 190-230 kg → 21-26 slots
• §lPercheron§r: pack 140-170 kg → 16-19 slots
• §lMule§r: pack 130-160 kg → 14-18 slots
• §lProvence Donkey§r: pack 90-110 kg → 10-12 slots
• §lThoroughbred§r: pack 70-90 kg → 8-10 slots
• §lPony§r: pack 45-60 kg → 5-7 slots
Bags (horse), baskets (donkey, mule) or crates (camels) §lfill up visibly§r. Sneak empty-handed: open them; shears: take the pack off (its contents stay inside). Loaded, a caravan goes up to 25% slower, except §lcamels in the desert§r (hot and dry biome), which also eat half as much there.
The §6camel§r (Bactrian, two humps, woolly) lives in badlands, windswept hills and snowy plains; the §6dromedary§r (one hump, light sand, a bit faster) in deserts and savannas. Both like cactus, hay and wheat.

pages.title: Relays and route sheet
Lighting: lights and switches
pages.text:
§lLight fixtures§r from bronze to electric: §6oil sconce§r (wall), §6bronze lantern§r (floor, or hanging from the ceiling), §6bronze chandelier§r (ceiling), then §6electric wall lamp§r (wall), §6ceiling lamp§r (ceiling) and §6industrial cage lamp§r (floor, wall or ceiling). §lOn its own, a light stays lit§r, like a torch.
To control them, a §lswitch§r: §6wooden lever§r (mechanical age, carpenter), §6bronze lever§r (metalworker), §6electric switch§r (redstone bench). It goes on like a lever, on a wall, the floor or the ceiling.

§lLinking§r (empty hand or §6wrench§r in hand):
1. §lsneak + right-click§r the switch: it is remembered (5 minutes);
2. §lsneak + right-click§r each light: it gets linked (or unlinked if it was); the message gives the number of linked lights. §l32 blocks§r at most from the switch, §l64 lights§r per switch; a light has only one switch (linking it elsewhere detaches it);
3. sneak-click the switch again: linking done.
§lWith a wrench in hand§r (main hand or off hand), looking at a switch or a linked light, a §lline§r joins the switch to each of its lights (amber when on, gray when off); without the wrench, no lines (link with the wrench in your off hand and an empty main hand to see the lines while you work).

§lRight-click§r the switch: §leverything turns on or off§r, even the lights of an unloaded chunk (when it loads). The switch also gives a §lredstone signal§r when on; a linked light still lights up from redstone (linked to a switch left off, it only obeys redstone). Breaking the switch frees its lights (lit).

pages.title: Every source of energy
Power
How much each generator makes
Bulk power
Living fuels
pages.text:
Solids (solid combustion generator, boiler, furnace): §lwood pellets§r 1,200 burn ticks, §lbiochar§r 1,600 (like coal), press cake and miscanthus 300, chips and bagasse 200. One burn tick is worth 1,024 FE.
Liquids (liquid combustion generator): §lrenewable diesel§r is worth as much as diesel, §lbio-kerosene§r as much as kerosene; turpentine, bio-oil, animal fat and wood tar burn too. The mixer turns renewable diesel into diesel, and cuts fuel oil with bio-oil.
Gases: §lwood gas§r, pyrolysis gas, biogas and §lmethane§r in the gas turbine (compact or multiblock); wood gas and methane also in the boiler.

pages.title: The solar panel
The wind turbine
The dam
pages.text:
The §6dam turbine§r goes §lin the wall of a reservoir§r: its §lwater intake§r (the grating, at the back) touches the reservoir water, its §loutlet§r (at the front) opens downstream, free. The water is not used up. Up to §l512 / 2,048 / 8,192 / 32,768 FE/t§r.
1. Dam a valley or a lake: a watertight wall, water on one side only.
2. Put the turbines at the foot of the wall, downstream side facing you.
3. §lHead§r: the reservoir surface above the turbine, full at 16 blocks.
4. §lVolume§r: 128 / 512 / 2,048 / 8,192 water sources per turbine; turbines on the same reservoir share it.
If the water in front joins the reservoir, there is no head: nothing. The interface says what is missing.

pages.title: The geothermal plant
The microbial fuel cell
pages.text:
§lLiving energy§r without burning anything: bacteria digest organic matter between two electrodes. Up to §l256 / 1,024 / 4,096 / 16,384 FE/t§r while it has food.
It eats §lanything compostable§r (seeds, leaves, saplings, crops, dishes) and §lliving-world leftovers§r: wood chips, bagasse, press cake, miscanthus, microalgae, meals… An item is worth its composting chance × §l12,000 / 24,000 / 48,000 / 96,000 FE§r: a melon (65%) gives 7,800 at MKI.
Hook it to the end of a farm: a hopper or a logistic cable feeds it through any side.

pages.title: Heat and pressure
pages.text:
Two resources you already had become §lworking materials§r.
• §6Heat§r is no longer just something to get rid of: it heats a multiblock instead of electricity, is stored in a buffer and keeps greenhouses at the right temperature; the §6radiator§r gives the surplus back to the air.
• §6Compressed air§r runs tools, tubes you ride in a cabin at full speed, pressurized machines, and is stored in buffers.
Both meet: compressing air §lheats it§r, and that heat can be recovered in a heat buffer.

pages.title: From hot to cold
pages.text:
One rule: heat §lonly flows from hot to cold§r, and its §ltemperature§r matters as much as its quantity. A body at 900 K can heat a pyrolysis oven; the same number of joules at 350 K only heat a greenhouse.
The logistic cable (heat channel, one body shared by the whole network) and heat buffers carry heat; their conductance rises with the tier: §l64 / 256 / 1,024 / 4,096 J/t per kelvin§r of difference.
Anything hot loses a little to the ambient air (300 K). The §6radiator§r gets rid of heat; the §6heat port§r set to input and the heat buffer §lrecover§r it.

pages.title: The heat cascade
pages.text:
The §6industrial heat port§r is set with the wrench: as an §loutput§r it removes the multiblock's heat, as an §linput§r it draws heat in from neighboring logistic cables (heat channel), if they are hotter.
A heating multiblock (furnace, pyrolysis, dryer, distillation…) above its §lworking temperature§r then uses the heat received instead of electricity: §l1 joule replaces 1 FE§r, up to §l75%§r of the operation's energy. The interface shows heat received and energy saved.
Build a cascade: a blast furnace's output port feeds a pyrolysis oven's input port, whose leftover heat dries wood, then warms a greenhouse. Each stage takes what is still hot enough for it.

pages.title: The radiator
pages.text:
The §6radiator§r gives a multiblock's heat back to the air. Place it against a §lheat port set to output§r (or a cable carrying heat): several radiators add up, one per free face of the port.
• Loss to air: §l24 / 96 / 384 / 1,536 J/t per kelvin§r above 300 K (MKI to MKIV), conductance to the port 120 / 480 / 1,920 / 7,680 J/t per kelvin, capacity 8,000 J/K.
• Against a multiblock of its tier at its rated temperature, it removes about §l8.6 k / 55 k / 330 k / 2 M J/t§r (800 / 1,100 / 1,500 / 2,100 K), as much as 21 / 137 / 823 / 4,937 mB/t of water, consuming nothing.
• One MKI is enough for the hottest MKI multiblock at full load (arc furnace: ~5.8 kJ/t). Against an MKI multiblock a stronger radiator does no better: the MKI body limits the exchange (60 J/t per kelvin).
Water, on the other hand, makes useful steam: keep radiators for heat you have no use for. Exact numbers: tooltip and JEI (Radiators category).

pages.title: Storing heat
pages.text:
The §6heat buffer§r keeps heat and gives it back later to colder neighboring bodies: §l4,000 / 16,000 / 64,000 / 256,000 J/K§r from MKI to MKIV. Its faces are set like every buffer's (input, output), its window glows with temperature (330 / 500 / 800 / 1,300 K) and a §lcomparator§r reads it.
Charge it from waste heat (a furnace's output port, an air compressor) or an electric heater, and drain it into a heat port set to input: a cascade, a greenhouse.

pages.title: Farm climate
pages.text:
Farms (hydroponic farm, tree plantation, aquaculture farm) take the §ltemperature of their biome§r: cold in the snow, hot in the desert.
Their comfort zone is §l285 to 310 K§r. Outside it they run at §l50%§r, never stopped; the interface says “too cold” or “too hot”.
• Too cold: a heat port set to §linput§r, fed by waste heat, a heat buffer or an electric heater.
• Too hot: a heat port set to §loutput§r toward §6radiators§r.

pages.title: Compressed air
pages.text:
The electric §6air compressor§r makes compressed air: §l400 FE/t → 40 L/t§r, 500 L reserve, up to 10 bar; it also gives §l25 J of heat per liter§r to neighbors that accept heat.
The logistic cable (pressure channel) and pressure buffers hold §l5 / 10 / 20 / 40 bar§r by tier. A volume's pressure = air ÷ volume.

pages.title: Pneumatic tools
pages.text:
Each tool has its own §lair tank§r (the bar shows the fill). To refill it: §lShift + right-click§r a block holding compressed air (compressor, buffer, station…), except a pipe.
• §6Jackhammer§r (2,000 L): digs the targeted face in §l3×3§r, 50 L per block, so 40 blocks per charge; while sneaking, a single block.
• §6Impact wrench§r (1,000 L): a wrench that also §ldismantles a mod machine in one click§r (20 L).
• §6Air blower§r (1,500 L): clears leaves, snow, grass and flowers in a 6-block cone (3 L per block, 2 L per puff).
• §6Sandblaster§r (1,500 L): strips (25 L and 1 sand per block): oxidized copper, mossy or cracked bricks, mossy stone.
• §6Diving tank§r (2,400 L): in the inventory, it gives you air back underwater; 12 L per second, about 3 min 20.

pages.title: Hypertubes
pages.text:
An air-powered subway: you travel §lseated in a cabin§r racing at §l25 blocks per second§r through a §lturquoise glass§r tube ringed in yellow-orange: you watch the landscape go by.
1. Start from a §6station§r, a tube end or a free block. With the §6hypertube§r in hand: §lright-click the start, right-click the end§r (station side, tube end or free block: the tube stops there, no support needed). The tube §lrounds itself§r and §lbends a little around an obstacle§r (3 blocks at most); the end becomes the next start, so you draw the line click after click (Shift + right-click: stop). One tube per block of length, 96 blocks at most per link, bends of 0.9 block radius at least. To dismantle: §laim at a tube§r (it gets outlined) and §lleft-click§r, whatever you hold: its tubes come back to you.
2. Open each station (right-click) and §lgive it a name§r: that is its stop. Only named stations show up as destinations.
3. Supply the departure station with air (at least §l1 bar§r; it holds 800 L, up to 8 bar). A trip costs §l60 L + 3 L per block§r, taken at departure.
4. Right-click a station: pick the destination in the list (distance, duration, air needed). The cabin speeds up, takes the shortest path, brakes and sets you down in front of the arrival station's mouth.
On the way there is no getting out (Shift does nothing) and no damage. If a hypertube is broken during the trip, the cabin takes you back to the departure station or sets you down at the nearest safe spot; if you disconnect, you resume at the arrival station.

pages.title: Process pressure
pages.text:
The §6industrial pressure port§r lets compressed air into a multiblock.
• §lPressurized recipes§r: Haber-Bosch and reforming in the industrial chemical reactor (Haber-Bosch), industrial cracker (hydrocracking), autoclave, polyethylene, industrial chemical reactor (steam reforming), Fischer-Tropsch. Above their minimum pressure they use a little air and run at full speed; without pressure they run at §l50%§r, never blocked. JEI shows the pressure and air required.
• §lGas lift§r: in a well, injected air raises the deposit's pressure, like water.
• §lAeration§r: the aquaculture farm and the hydroponic farm (microalgae) are aerated with compressed air instead of oxygen.

pages.title: Taps and resin
pages.text:
A §6resin tap§r goes on the §lside of a trunk§r (right-click the side face of a log). It needs §lno energy§r: sap drips into its cup on its own.
1. Pick a §lliving tree§r: at least 3 identical logs stacked, with natural leaves at the top (a plank tree or a bare trunk does not flow).
2. §lSpruce§r → §6raw resin§r; §ljungle§r → §6raw latex§r. Other woods give nothing.
3. The §ltaller§r the trunk, the faster the sap (up to 8 logs counted). Several taps on one trunk §lshare§r the flow.
4. Right-click with an empty hand: you take the contents; the message also gives the delay per drop, or why nothing flows. A comparator reads the fill level.
The §6wooden resin tap§r (carpenter's bench) holds 4 units; the §6bronze resin tap§r (coppersmith's bench) flows §ltwice as fast§r, holds 16 and pushes into a chest or cable placed §lbelow§r. Logistic cables can also pull from both taps.

pages.title: Rosin and primitive plastic
pages.text:
Everything is done §lwithout electricity§r, in the §6pottery kiln§r and at the benches:
1. §6Raw resin§r in the kiln (200 °C, 10 s) → §6rosin§r.
2. Mason's bench, with a mortar: 2 rosin + 2 sawdust + 2 plant fibers → 2 §6primitive plastic mix§r (or 1 hemp fiber instead of the plant fibers: 3 mixes).
3. Mix in the kiln (160 °C, 12 s) → §6primitive plastic§r.
Primitive plastic is the §linsulator§r of the §lMKI circuit§r (in the middle, between copper and solder wires) and of §lbasic energy cables§r: have some before electricity.
§6Raw latex§r, in the §lsteam extractor§r (1 → 1, machine only; MKI dryer: smoked), gives §6natural rubber§r: the sheath of the MKI logistic cable, conveyor belts (rolling mill (calendering)). §lGaskets§r are still made of synthetic rubber.
Later, the chemical reactor steam-distills resin (4 resin → 3 rosin + 250 mB of §6turpentine§r), the mixer makes the mix and the press the plate. Resin or rosin with a stick also makes §ltorches§r.

pages.title: Industrial crops
pages.text:
Rapeseed, hemp and corn are Agriculture 2.0 crops (genetic seeds, climate: see the "Mechanics: Farming and cooking" chapter); their wild seeds come from §lgrass§r in biomes of their climate:
• §6Rapeseed§r: 4 seeds → 300 mB oil at the press.
• §6Hemp§r: stalks give §lhemp fiber§r (knife at the carpenter's bench, or crusher): string, ropes, canvas, primitive plastic.
• §6Corn§r: edible, gives §lstarch§r (crusher (fine grinding) with water), ethanol, a little oil and meal.
• §6Miscanthus§r (3% from grass): grows only in a §lhydroponic farm§r; it is the most generous biomass (4 per cycle).
The §6hydroponic farm§r grows every seed of the mod.

pages.title: Biomass
pages.text:
• §6Crusher§r (compact or multiblock; it took over the old wood chipper's recipes): 1 log → 8 chips (and sawdust); leaves, sticks, bamboo, miscanthus → chips and fibers; hemp stalk → 2 fibers; cane → bagasse and sugar. The by-product goes to its 2nd output slot.
• §6Compactor§r (it took over the old pellet mill's recipes): 4 chips → 4 §lwood pellets§r; sawdust, bagasse and miscanthus too. It also makes §lfish feed§r and animal feed (the 2nd ingredient goes in the binder slot: fish meal + starch, press cake + wheat, press cake + corn, microalgae + press cake).
• §6Fermenter (anaerobic digestion)§r: wet waste (leaves, flesh, saplings, kelp, press cake, bagasse, microalgae, wheat, vinasse, glycerol) + a little water → §lbiogas§r and §ldigestate§r, sometimes fertilizer. Slow (30 s) but it eats anything.
The §6fermenter§r keeps sugars and starches: ethanol, §lvinasse§r (back to the digester) and CO₂.

pages.title: Oils
pages.text:
The §6extractor (oil pressing)§r crushes seeds (rapeseed, hemp, wheat, pumpkin, melon, sunflower, corn): §lplant oil§r + §lpress cake§r. Fish yield §lfish oil§r and fish meal, microalgae §lalgae oil§r, cane and beetroot §lmolasses§r and bagasse.
• §lSolvent§r: 4 press cakes + 100 mB naphtha in an extractor (leaching) → 200 mB more oil.
• §lAnimal fat§r: raw meat or rotten flesh rendered in the cracker.
• §lSoap§r: fat or oil + caustic soda (and glycerol), or rosin + caustic soda; with turpentine it makes flotation reagent.
• §lBiodiesel§r: any oil + methanol + caustic soda in the chemical reactor.
• §lRenewable diesel§r and §lbio-kerosene§r (advanced tier): oil + hydrogen + nickel in the industrial cracker (hydrocracking).
• §lLubricant§r from the basic tier: 1,000 mB plant oil → 700 mB in the mixer (600 from fish oil).

pages.title: Pyrolysis
pages.text:
Pyrolysis happens in the §lcoke oven battery§r (the multiblock; not the compact coke oven): it heats matter §lwithout air§r: it does not burn, it breaks down. Each recipe has its §lregime§r, set in advance (nothing to tune):
• §lSlow§r (basic tier, 10 s): a log → charcoal, tar, wood vinegar and §lwood gas§r; chips, pellets, bagasse, press cake, miscanthus, hemp, bamboo → §6biochar§r. It is the charcoal pit of the Industrial Age.
• §lFast§r (advanced tier, 6 s): 8 chips → 400 mB §6bio-oil§r + biochar + pyrolysis gas.
• §lRecycling§r (advanced tier): plastic sheets, pipes, casings, foam and pellets → §lnaphtha§r (about half the matter comes back); PVC → naphtha and hydrogen chloride; rubbers → carbon black and fuel oil; conveyor belt → the same, plus its steel.
• Oil sludge → fuel oil; tar sand (advanced) → synthetic crude; coal → coke, coal tar and coke oven gas.
Byproducts: wood vinegar → methanol, acetic acid and tar (distillation column (rectification)); tar → pitch and creosote; pyrolysis gas → syngas and methane (gas separator); biochar → fertilizer, activated carbon, fuel.

pages.title: The industrial chemical reactor (gasification)
pages.text:
The §6industrial chemical reactor (gasification)§r (multiblock) barely burns: a little §loxygen§r (250 mB) and §lsteam§r (500 mB) turn a solid fuel into §lsyngas§r (hydrogen + carbon monoxide), with a little ash.
• 8 chips or 4 pellets → 2,000 mB; 2 biochar → 1,600; 1 coal → 1,600; 1 coke or petroleum coke → 1,800; miscanthus, bagasse, press cake too.
Syngas is the gateway to §lmethanol§r, §lhydrogen§r (membranes, PSA), §lmethane§r (methanation) and §lFischer-Tropsch§r. Oxygen comes from the industrial gas separator (air separation).

pages.title: Natural gas
pages.text:
Well gas is a §lmixture§r. The §6industrial gas separator (gas processing)§r (multiblock) splits it:
• 10,000 mB natural gas + 100 mB §6amine solution§r → 7,600 mB §lmethane§r, 800 ethane, 10 helium, 120 LPG, 100 condensate; 90 mB amine comes back.
• Sour gas also gives §lhydrogen sulfide§r (to the Claus process and sulfur); refinery gas gives methane and ethane.
• At the advanced tier it also upgrades §lbiogas§r: methane and CO₂.
Amine solution is made in the chemical reactor (water, liquid ammonia, ethylene); it also sweetens sour gas in the distillation column (stripping).
§lMethane§r burns better than natural gas (turbine, boiler), liquefies into LNG, and replaces natural gas at the industrial chemical reactor (Haber-Bosch) (900 mB instead of 1,000).

pages.title: Biomethane and methanation
pages.text:
Methane §lwithout a field§r, at the advanced tier:
• §lBiomethane§r: 1,000 mB biogas → 580 mB methane + 400 CO₂ in the gas separator (600 + 380 in the Gas Separator (PSA adsorption), molecular sieve).
• §lMethanation§r (Sabatier): 1,000 mB CO₂ + 4,000 hydrogen → 1,000 mB methane and water, in the chemical reactor (catalysis) (nickel); 2,000 mB syngas → 500 methane.
• Pyrolysis gas splits into syngas and methane.
§lCO₂§r is no longer waste: it goes to methanation, to urea, or enriches the farms' air.

pages.title: Reformer and Fischer-Tropsch
pages.text:
The §6industrial chemical reactor (steam reforming)§r (multiblock) makes §lhydrogen in bulk§r: 1,000 mB methane + 2,000 steam → 3,400 mB hydrogen + 900 CO₂ (natural gas: 3,000; 2,000 biogas: 2,800; pyrolysis gas, ethanol and methanol too). The nickel catalyst barely wears out (1%).
The §6Industrial Chemical Reactor (Fischer-Tropsch)§r (multiblock, advanced tier) turns 4,000 mB syngas into §ldiesel§r (300 mB), §lkerosene§r (150), water, tail gas and a paraffin wax, on a §6cobalt catalyst§r (made in the chemical reactor: cobalt dust, alumina, nitric acid) or on iron (a little less).
§lWhy not 100% oil-free?§r These routes give §lfuels§r, waxes, methanol, methane, hydrogen — no naphtha or ethylene. §lPlastic sheets§r (advanced frame) and §lgaskets§r (advanced casings and kits) still come from oil and field gas.

pages.title: The hydroponic farm
pages.text:
The §6hydroponic farm§r is a §lglass-roofed hall§r multiblock (glass walls and a gabled glass roof), controller in the middle of the front, ports, and built-in §6grow beds§r (the inside stays empty); the tier sets the number of crops in parallel (4/8/16/32).
1. An §litem§r input port: the seeds (wheat, potato, carrot, beetroot, cane, berries, melon, pumpkin, rapeseed, hemp, corn, miscanthus).
