2. A §lfluid§r port: water (500 mB per cycle, base yield) or §6nutrient solution§r (250 mB: §l×1.5§r).
3. A §lgas§r port: with nutrient solution, 200 mB §lCO₂§r gives §l×2§r.
4. An item output port: harvests and seeds. A cycle lasts 15 s at the basic tier.
Nutrient solution is made in the mixer: 1 fertilizer + 1,000 mB water → 1,000 mB (the most efficient); 500 mB digestate + 500 water → 600; 1 fish meal → 400; 2 bone meal → 300.

pages.title: The tree plantation
pages.text:
The §6tree plantation§r (multiblock, §6tree plots§r inside) grows trees in 30 s at the basic tier: one sapling + 1,000 mB water → 6 logs, the sapling, 2 sticks and an extra; with 500 mB nutrient solution → 9 logs and 3 sticks.
Extras: oak and dark oak, apples; §lspruce§r, raw resin; §ljungle§r, raw latex; cherry, petals; mangrove, roots. Bamboo multiplies too (9 for 1).
It is the source of wood, resin and latex in bulk, without taps.

pages.title: Aquaculture and microalgae
pages.text:
The §6aquaculture farm§r (multiblock, built-in §6fish tanks§r) replaces fishing:
• 2 cod (or salmon, tropical fish; 1 pufferfish) + 1 §lfish feed§r + 1,000 mB water + 200 mB §loxygen§r → 5 fish (3 puffers) and sometimes bone meal;
• kelp → 6 kelp and §lshells§r; sea pickles + feed → 3 pickles and 2 shells; seagrass.
Crushed shells → §lquicklime§r (industrial furnace (roasting), pottery kiln). Dried kelp gives iodine and soda ash.
The §6hydroponic farm (microalgae)§r (workshop machine) isolates a §lmicroalgae§r strain (4 kelp + water), then grows it: 1 microalgae + water + 500 mB CO₂ → 3, and 400 mB oxygen; with nutrient solution → 5, 600 mB oxygen and a little algae oil. Microalgae give oil, biogas, feed and bio-oil.

pages.title: The living world
pages.text:
Since 1.0.5, the world is §6alive§r: it changes with the seasons, its animals stay, breed and can be hunted. This chapter gathers everything, in the order you discover it while playing:
• §lSeasons§r: a calendar of 4 seasons of 10 days; climate, colors and weather change, and so does what you can sow.
• §lThe greenhouse§r: a closed room of greenhouse panes and its regulator; ideal climate in every season.
• §lWildlife§r: animals no longer despawn; each 128-block zone repopulates away from players.
• §lDogs and cats§r: breeds, owner by name tag, kennel and basket, modes, Recall key (§lG§r).
• §lGame§r, §lpredators and small wildlife§r, §lsavanna and jungle§r, §lsea and shores§r: 32 wild species, each with its own habits.
• §lHunting§r: herds, tracking dog, Hunting skill, musket, revolver, harpoon, trophies.
• §lGame cooking§r: smoking, dishes, lamp oil.
• §lServer settings§r: what the administrator can adjust.
The links below lead to the first page of each part.

pages.title: The seasons
pages.text:
The world follows a §6calendar§r: 4 seasons of 10 days (server setting), one date for the whole server; sleeping moves the calendar forward. The §lminimap§r shows the season and the day on the climate line. The §lcalendar§r (carpenter's bench, saw: 3 paper, 1 lath, 1 plank, 1 peg) tells the date in hand; hung on a wall, its page follows the season and a §lcomparator§r reads it (1 spring, 2 summer, 3 fall, 4 winter).
• §lClimate§r: each season shifts the temperature (summer / winter): temperate (plains, forests) +8 / -14 °C, cold (taiga, mountains) +6 / -12 °C, dry (desert, badlands) +6 / -8 °C, tropical +3 / -3 °C, oceans +3 / -4 °C, snowy +4 / -6 °C; humidity rises in spring and fall. The change is smooth over the last 2 days of a season and the first 2 of the next.
• §lWeather§r: spring, frequent short rains; summer, dry weather, rare but violent storms; fall, long rains and morning mist; winter, §lreal snow§r in temperate and cold biomes (it does not put out fires, does not get you wet, fills cauldrons with powder snow and does not water fields), but with no snow layer or ice where it does not usually snow. Desert and badlands: never anything. Savanna: rain in spring and summer.
• §lColors§r: grass and leaves change color: light green in spring, deep green in summer, broadleaf trees yellow, orange then red in the fall (birches yellow), dull brownish green in winter; conifers and jungle barely change, savanna and desert turn straw yellow in the dry season.
• §lCrops§r: out of its climate, a plant stops growing at once and §lwithers after a whole day§r out of climate. The look card tells until when it grows (“Ideal climate until the end of summer”) or how long before it withers. Fruit trees never die: their fruit just waits.
• §lUnderground§r (no sky, below layer 50): fixed climate of 8 °C, humidity 0.5, no seasons, mushrooms included. Above layer 50, a cellar follows the outside climate. A greenhouse (a closed room of greenhouse blocks, with a regulator) stays ideal in every season.

pages.title: What to sow each season
pages.text:
Number of crops in their §lideal climate§r in the middle of each season (irrigated soil, ordinary seed), and in parentheses those that become ideal (they were not in the season before: time to sow them):
• §lPlains§r: spring 35 (wheat, amaranth, corn); summer 25 (rice, cotton, sweet potato); fall 35 (wheat, barley, oats); winter 16 (rye, kale, leek)
• §lForest§r: spring 32 (wheat, amaranth, corn); summer 36 (rice, cotton, sunflower); fall 32 (barley, oats, rapeseed); winter 16 (rye, kale, leek)
• §lTaiga§r: spring 16 (barley, oats, rapeseed); summer 29 (wheat, flax, hemp); fall 16; winter 7
• §lSavanna§r: spring 20 (rice, starfruit, coffee); summer 20; fall 17; winter 17
• §lDesert§r: spring 17; summer 17; fall 17; winter 17
A “difficult” plant still grows, slowed down; good Resistance widens the margin. Out of season, a greenhouse or a cellar below layer 50 (8 °C) takes over.

pages.title: Building a greenhouse
pages.text:
A §6greenhouse§r is a §lclosed room§r whose walls and roof are all §lgreenhouse blocks§r: §6greenhouse glass§r (wired glass in a frame; neighboring panes form a single glazed wall), §6greenhouse frames§r (posts and corners, along the axis you choose) and glazed §6greenhouse vents§r (open or closed, they count as wall). §lAny door§r is allowed, open or closed. The §lfloor§r is any solid block (dirt, farmland, substrate, stone…), and a one-block low wall under the panes also counts as floor.
• §lTreated wood§r from the bronze age, §liron§r later (sturdier): agricultural workbench, saw and hammer. Both materials can be mixed.
• §lSize§r: 8 to 4,096 air blocks inside, at most 32 × 32 × 16 (width, length, height).
• The §6greenhouse regulator§r goes §linto a wall§r (it counts as wall), front facing outside: it surveys the room from the inside and declares it formed (green light). Its interface shows the volume, the crops and the climate; so does its look card.
• §lInside§r: an §lideal climate for every crop, in every season§r, with no minimum light; nothing falls inside, neither rain nor snow. Fruit trees bear fruit all year round.
• Example: 5 × 5 on the ground, 3-block walls, flat roof, frames on the edges, a door, a vent in the middle of the roof (Shift + right-click on a placed regulator: the plan of this example; in creative, holding the regulator builds it).

pages.title: Greenhouse: common mistakes
pages.text:
When the greenhouse is not formed, the interface, the look card and the red banner say §lwhat§r and §lwhere§r (exact block coordinates). §lShift + right-click§r on the regulator: the §lfault plan§r shows the leak (a see-through pane to plug) or the faulty blocks (in red); again for the example greenhouse, then to hide it.
• §lThe greenhouse leaks§r: a block is missing from a wall, the roof or the floor (a slab, a fence or a thin glass pane also let the air through). Corners and edges do not count: only the faces that touch the inside must be closed.
• §lFaulty block§r: a solid block that is not a greenhouse block in a wall or the roof (ordinary glass, stone, log…). A stone pillar in the middle of the greenhouse is faulty too (only its top can hold a raised bed).
• §lToo small§r (under 8 air blocks), §ltoo big§r (over 4,096 blocks or 32 × 32 × 16, or a greenhouse open onto a cave).
• §lAlready regulated§r: two regulators in the same greenhouse; only one keeps it. Two neighboring greenhouses may share a wall: each has its own regulator.
• The greenhouse is surveyed again when a block of its wall is placed or broken, and at least once a minute.
• §lWorlds from before 1.0.5§r: glass above crops no longer makes a greenhouse on Earth (a message says so once). Those crops follow the outside climate, with a day of grace before withering out of season: close the room with greenhouse blocks and add a regulator. On other worlds, the old glass greenhouse is unchanged.

pages.title: Wildlife
pages.text:
Since 1.0.5, animals §lno longer despawn§r and §lno longer spawn at random§r around you: they are born with the world, when a piece of terrain is created, and stay where they live. This applies to grazing animals, predators, birds, marine life and fish (the mod's fish and the vanilla fish already present). Night monsters and bats do not change.
• The world is split into §6128 × 128 block zones§r. Each zone remembers its §lstarting population§r for five groups: §lgame, predators, birds, marine life, fish§r.
• Every §l10 minutes§r, if a group of a zone drops §lbelow a quarter§r of its starting population (hunting, fishing…), a small group of animals of the biome and season comes back, §lmore than 64 blocks§r from any player and §lout of sight§r.
• Between a quarter and the starting population, animals §lslowly have young§r (out of sight, more than 32 blocks from any player): a zone left alone gets its population back within a few days (1.0.5, lot 6).
• Never back §linside a clan claim§r nor §lwithin 48 blocks of a village§r: your livestock is not counted and never topped up.
• §lBirds§r are more numerous in spring and summer. Each zone has a §lcap§r per group: nature never overflows.
• §6Crows§r stay in the area: when full, they land and rest for a day. A zone with fields attracts more crows; the §6scarecrow§r keeps its effects.
• Worlds from before 1.0.5: animals already there stay; zones already explored are repopulated gently (one group per pass).
• Admins: settings in the “fauna” section of the server configuration; §l/pioneer fauna zone§r and §l/pioneer fauna map§r show the state of the zones.

flow.label: Returns far and out of sight

pages.title: Dogs and cats
pages.text:
The wolf has become the §6wild dog§r: a shaggy mongrel. Tame it with bones as before: it instantly becomes a §ldog of a random breed§r.
• §l8 dog breeds§r: German Shepherd, Labrador, Border Collie, Husky, Beagle, Saint Bernard, Pointer, Dachshund. Each has its own silhouette and §laptitudes§r: §lnose§r (tracking range when hunting, 24 to 64 blocks), §lspeed§r, §lstrength§r (16 to 30 health and bite), §lcold endurance§r (a chilly dog slows down in the cold, the Husky never does).
• §l8 cat breeds§r: European Tabby, Siamese, Persian, Maine Coon, Chartreux, Bengal, Norwegian Forest Cat, Sphynx. Village strays take the breed of their coat. Aptitudes: §lfishing§r, §lrat hunting§r, §lindependence§r (an independent cat comes to see you less often).
• Two parents of the same breed have puppies or kittens of that breed; of different breeds, one of the two.
• Your old tamed wolves have become breed dogs: same owner, same collar, same name.

pages.title: Owner and adoption
pages.text:
To be an animal's §6owner§r, you must §lgive it a name with a name tag§r. This applies to dogs, cats and §lmounts§r (horses, donkeys, mules, llamas, camels, dromedaries).
• Without a name, a tamed animal obeys whoever tamed it, but §lhas no owner§r: no recall, no protection.
• An animal with an owner §lcannot be hurt by other players§r, unless your clans are at §lopen war§r. Nobody else can rename it.
• To §lgive it away§r: in its interface, tick §l“Let others adopt it”§r. The next player who renames it with a name tag becomes its owner, and the box unticks.
• Animals tamed and named before 1.0.5: you already are their owner.

pages.title: Kennel, basket and territory
pages.text:
The §6kennel§r (dog) and the §6basket§r (cat) are made at the §lAgricultural Bench§r with a saw, in every furniture wood. Bring your animal §lon a lead§r and right-click the block (or “Link” in its interface): it switches to §lAutonomous§r mode.
• It lives in a §l30-block territory§r around its home and never leaves it. §lAt night§r, and sometimes during the day, it goes home to sleep: lying in front of its kennel, §lcurled up§r in its basket.
• Now and then it §lcomes to see you§r if you are in or near the territory, stays a few minutes by your side, then leaves.
• §lThe dog§r barks at monsters and predators entering the territory and §ldefends livestock§r: it rushes at once (in under a second) at wild dogs, foxes and real wolves. In §lFollow§r or §lHunt§r mode it also defends you: a wolf or a predator within 16 blocks of you or of it.
• §lThe cat§r hunts the territory's rats. In the daytime, every 3 to 8 minutes, it goes §lfishing§r in the water closest to its basket (a pond will do) and §lbrings the fish back into its basket§r (3 slots). Right-click the basket with an empty hand, or put a hopper below, to collect them.
• If the kennel or the basket is broken, the animal follows you again.

pages.title: Modes and interface
pages.text:
§lShift + right-click with an empty hand§r on your animal opens its §6interface§r: name and breed, owner, health, linked kennel or basket (coordinates), aptitudes, mode, adoption box. For a mount: breed, owner, adoption and an §lInventory§r button (or Packs if it carries a pack saddle).
• §lAutonomous§r: around its home (it needs a kennel or a basket).
• §lFollow§r: as before, it follows you and catches up in a leap.
• §lSit§r: it no longer moves (a plain right-click also makes it sit or stand).
• §lHunt§r (dog): it may leave its territory, §ltracks the nearest game§r within reach of its nose and guides you to it: it moves ahead, stops to wait for you, then points and §lbarks toward the animal§r. It stops hunting when you recall it.

pages.title: Recalling
pages.text:
The §6Recall§r key (§lG§r by default, configurable in Options › Controls, Pioneer's category) recalls §levery animal you own§r: dogs, cats and mounts. They are §lteleported next to you§r, on safe ground, §lwith no distance limit§r, even from another dimension.
• An animal left in an unloaded area is found at its last known place: its area is loaded for the time of the recall.
• §lHold§r the key: a §lwheel§r shows each of your animals (name, distance or dimension); release on one of them to recall only that one.
• A recalled animal switches to §lFollow§r mode (it stands up if it was sitting, stops hunting). A mount ridden by another player, or tied into a caravan, is not recalled.
• A delay of a few seconds separates two recalls (server setting).
• The gear modules key moves to §lR§r.

pages.title: Game
pages.text:
Five §6game§r species live in forests and plains. They are born with the world and come back through repopulation, like other animals; they share the room of game (the world does not hold more).
• §lWild boar§r (forests, dark forests, taiga): it flees at 8 blocks, but §lcharges§r if you get §lwithin 4 blocks§r or wound it. Tusked boar, sow, striped boarlets. When hungry, it sometimes §lroots up and destroys a few crops§r: a field surrounded by §lfences, walls or fence gates§r, or inside a claim, is safe.
• §lStag and hind§r (forests, birch forests, meadows): §lherds of 3 to 6§r, very shy (16 blocks); the whole herd flees together, §lin leaps§r. The stag wears antlers; spotted fawns.
• §lWild turkey§r (forests, meadows): groups of 3 to 6; in spring, the tom §lfans its tail§r.
• §lHare§r (plains, meadows, snow): bigger than a rabbit, very fast, it §lzigzags§r as it flees; §lwhite in winter§r.
• §lBison§r (plains, savanna plateaus): §lherds of 4 to 10§r, peaceful; but §lthe whole herd fights back§r if you attack one of them.
• Approach §lcrouching§r: animals let you come twice as close. A dog in §lHunt§r mode tracks them.
• They can be fed and bred like livestock (two sexes): carrots and potatoes (boar), wheat and apples (deer), seeds (turkey), carrots and dandelions (hare), wheat (bison).

pages.title: Game through the seasons
pages.text:
Game lives to the rhythm of the §6seasons§r.
• The §lstag sheds its antlers§r between late autumn and midwinter (each at its own time); they §lgrow back in spring§r. At shedding time, a §6deer antler§r sometimes stays on the ground: look for it in forests. A stag wearing its antlers drops one (sometimes two).
• The §lhare§r turns §lwhite in winter§r; in a snowy biome, it is white all year long.
• The turkey mostly struts in §lspring§r; the stag mostly bellows in §lautumn§r.
• Births in your livestock pens stay §lfree in every season§r.
• §6Wild breeding§r: a hunted but not emptied zone (between a quarter and its starting population) slowly refills by itself: now and then a young one is born near an adult, §lout of sight and more than 32 blocks§r from any player, never in a claim nor beyond the starting population. A forest left alone gets its game back §lwithin a few days§r.

pages.title: Game meat
pages.text:
Game gives its own §6meats§r: §lvenison§r (deer), §lboar meat§r, §lbison meat§r (the most filling), §lturkey§r; the hare gives rabbit meat and hide. Boars, deer and bison also give §lleather§r, turkeys give §lfeathers§r. Young ones give nothing.
• They §lcook§r in a furnace, a smoker and on a campfire, like livestock meat; an animal that burns drops its meat already cooked.
• Like any raw poultry, raw turkey may cause hunger.
• They count as §lraw meat§r for baskets and farm storage. Smoking, minced meat and game dishes: see the “Game cooking” page.

pages.title: Predators
pages.text:
Three wild animals are §6dangerous§r.
• §lGray wolf§r (taiga, snowy forests, mountains): not to be confused with the §lwild dog§r. It lives in §lpacks of 3 to 5§r; §lat night§r, it attacks §llivestock§r and §llone players§r (no other player within 24 blocks); by day, it only attacks a lone player who comes within 6 blocks. The whole pack follows the prey. It §lfears fire§r: a §6torch§r or lantern in hand keeps it at bay (10 blocks), and so does a lit campfire. It cannot be tamed. An autonomous §ldog§r defends livestock against it. Gray, white (snow) or black; leather and bones.
• §lBear§r (forests, taiga, wooded mountains): §lvery dangerous§r, it charges anyone who comes §lwithin 6 blocks§r; a sow with cubs charges at 12 blocks. It is drawn to the mod's §6apiaries§r, which it §lbreaks§r to feast; inside a §lclaim§r, it rears up and roars to threaten, but breaks nothing. It stays active in winter. Lots of meat and leather; a dog in Hunt mode tracks it.
• §lSnake§r (plains, forests, savanna, jungle, desert): it §lhunts rats§r and §lbites§r if you come §lwithin 2 blocks§r or attack it: §lmild poison§r. Its coat depends on the biome (grass snake, sand viper, green tree snake, banded snake). Slimeball.

pages.title: Small wildlife
pages.text:
• §lGreen woodpecker§r (forests): it flies from tree to tree, §lclings to trunks§r and §ldrums§r: you can hear it from far away. The male has a red moustache, the female a black one. Feathers.
• §lPigeon§r (everywhere, drawn to buildings): in flocks, it §lperches on rooftops§r, pecks and §lcoos§r with a puffed-up chest. Feathers, sometimes a pigeon to roast.
• Woodpeckers and pigeons are §lfewer in winter§r; they fly off when approached (crouching: twice as close).
• §lRat§r (everywhere, mostly §lnear buildings§r): now and then it §lsteals an item§r (food first) from an §lunprotected chest or barrel§r — never from a §6warehouse crate§r, a machine, a locked chest or a clan claim — and carries it off: kill it to get it back. It §lslowly breeds§r near food stores. Counter it with a §6rat trap§r, a §lcat§r (it hunts rats) and a §lsnake§r. The server can turn theft off (setting §lfauna.ratTheft§r).
• Rats and pigeons also come back near villages and in claims: that is where they live.

pages.title: Rat trap and bird house
pages.text:
• The §6rat trap§r (farming bench, saw: a plank, two copper wires, a peg): §lbait§r it with §lseeds§r or §lcheese§r by right-clicking. Once set, it §llures rats within 8 blocks§r and §lcatches the first one§r that touches the bait. One rat per bait: §lright-click to empty it§r, then set it again.
• The §6bird house§r (farming bench, saw: three planks, a lath, a peg; one per wood): place it §lagainst a wall§r or §lon a post§r (fence, wall, log). It §ldraws pigeons and woodpeckers§r: when there are few around, a bird arrives from afar and settles near it. Now and then, a §lfeather falls below§r.
• Not to be confused with the §6nesting box§r (the hens' former "nest box"), where hens come to lay.

pages.title: The savanna
pages.text:
Four large animals roam the §6savannas§r.
• §lGiraffe§r (savannas and plateaus): peaceful, it §lbrowses the tops of acacias§r, neck stretched up to the leaves (nothing is broken). It flees if you come within 10 blocks; §lstruck up close, it kicks§r (a hoof blow that knocks you back), then runs off. Big game meat.
• §lLion and lioness§r: §llazy§r, lying down most of the time. If you §llinger within 6 blocks§r, the lion gets up and §lgrowls§r; stay longer and it §lattacks§r. Back away and it goes back to rest. The §llioness hunts§r savanna game (wild horses, donkeys and llamas, bison, giraffe calves) from late afternoon to dawn, once a day, with the other lionesses. Meat.
• §lRhinoceros§r: it §lcharges anything it sees within 8 blocks§r; a wall hides you. Very §ltough§r (armored hide), its blow §lsends you flying§r. Lots of bones, meat.
• §lElephant§r: §lfamily herds§r. Do not come within 5 blocks of a §lcalf§r, and never strike an elephant: §lthe whole herd charges§r. It only gives §lbones§r: no ivory.
• Large animals step up one block without jumping and never break blocks. Giraffe, rhinoceros and elephant are §lgame§r (a dog in Hunt mode tracks them); lions are §lpredators§r.

pages.title: The jungle
pages.text:
• §lMonkey§r (jungles, sparse jungles, bamboo jungles): it lives in troops, §lclimbs trees§r and §lpicks ripe bananas§r from the mod's §6banana trees§r (the branch goes back to rest); in the wild jungle, it finds some in the canopy. Sitting down, it §lpeels§r its banana, §leats§r it and §ltosses the peel§r, which soon vanishes. Beware: it §lsometimes steals the banana in your hand§r — just one, never anything else. The server can turn theft off (setting §lfauna.monkeyTheft§r). A banana in hand draws it in; feed it some to breed it. Bananas. A hunting dog does not track it.
• §lTiger§r (jungles): solitary, it §lhunts players on sight§r. §lLying in wait§r, crouched in tall grass, it creeps closer, then §lpounces§r from 5 blocks. Like the wolf, it §lfears fire§r: a §6torch§r or lantern in hand keeps it 6 blocks away, and so does a lit campfire. Bengal tiger, rarely white. Leather, big game meat.
• §lBig game meat§r roasts in a furnace, a smoker or on a campfire.

pages.title: The sea
pages.text:
The §6oceans§r have their giants. They are born in open, deep water, never in rivers.
• §lWhales§r: the §lblue whale§r (nearly 15 blocks, deep and cold oceans), the §lhumpback whale§r (long white flippers), the §lsperm whale§r (huge square head, deep oceans; very rarely white). They §lsurface to breathe§r and §lblow a spout of spray§r, then dive again (the humpback shows its tail). Peaceful and §lvery long to bring down§r; the sperm whale rams whoever attacks it. Lots of §lblubber§r and §lwhale meat§r.
• §lOrca§r (cold and frozen oceans): hunts §lseals, sea lions, penguins, razorbills and sharks§r in pods; it leaves players alone unless attacked.
• §lSharks§r: the §lgreat white§r and the §ltiger shark§r attack swimmers within 16 blocks; the §lhammerhead§r and the §lgray reef shark§r only attack if you are §lbleeding§r (under half health, or hurt less than 10 seconds ago); the §lwhale shark§r, a spotted giant of warm seas, is harmless. Sharks also hunt fish, never in a claim nor the ones you released. Shark meat.
• §lManta ray§r (warm seas): glides in schools, harmless. Ray wings.
• Stay in a boat above sharks: they only go after swimmers.

pages.title: Shores and pack ice
pages.text:
• §lSeal§r (rocky and snowy shores, pack ice) and §lsea lion§r (beaches and rocky shores): they §lbask§r on rocks, sand and ice (the sea lion props itself up and barks), and §ldive as soon as you come near§r (sneak up to see them closer). They swim, surface to breathe and come back ashore. Seal meat, leather (and a little blubber). The seal pup is pure white.
• §lSeagull§r (beaches, shores, harbors): it also settles near coastal buildings. Cheeky, it §lsometimes steals a food item from your hotbar§r — never the item in your hand nor your armor. It keeps its loot in its beak: shoot it down to get it back. The server can turn theft off (setting §lfauna.seagullTheft§r). Feathers.
• §lPenguin§r (frozen oceans, pack ice, snowy beaches) and §lrazorbill§r (cold, rocky coasts): they live in §lcolonies§r, waddle, slide on their bellies, call each other. Now and then they §ldive to fish§r and come back with §la fish in their beak§r, which they swallow a little later. Fish.
• Seals, sea lions, penguins and razorbills are §lorca prey§r when they swim.
• Sea meats (whale, shark, ray, seal) cook in a furnace, a smoker or on a campfire; whale blubber gives lamp oil (see the “Game cooking” page).

pages.title: Herds and tracking dogs
pages.text:
Now and then (at most once every §l3 to 6 game days§r), a §6herd§r of §l4 to 10 animals§r arrives near you, §l48 to 96 blocks§r away, out of your sight, never in a village or a claim. Its species follows the biome and the season: §ldeer§r in forests and taigas, §lbison§r on plains, §lboars§r in dark forests and taigas, §lturkeys§r in meadows, §lhares§r in winter, §lgiraffes§r and §lelephants§r in savannas.
• §lSigns§r: §ltracks§r on the ground lead to the herd, you hear §ldistant calls§r.
• §lThe dog§r: autonomous near its kennel, it §lgrowls§r then §lcomes to fetch you§r. Shift + right-click on it: the §lHunt§r button glows §lonly when a herd is within its scent range§r (otherwise it is grayed: “No hunt in range”). In Hunt mode it leaves its territory, follows the herd's §ltrail§r (up to twice its scent range), waits for you, points and barks toward the animal. It goes back to autonomous mode when the herd is over.
• If nobody comes near within §lone game day§r, the herd §lscatters and disappears§r. Once found (a player within 24 blocks), it stays; a day later, the survivors leave when nobody is near them anymore. Herd animals do not count for repopulation and do not breed.
• §lHunting skill§r (17th in the Notebook): XP for each game animal killed (§ldouble§r from afar, 24 blocks or more, and double again for a dangerous animal), for a herd found, and for §lskinning§r (each hide or leather in the loot). At level 10: §l+30%§r meat and leather, trophies §l5% → 10%§r, reloading §l−25%§r, spread §l−30%§r, dog scent §l+50%§r. The §lScout§r has Hunting as an affinity, on top of Combat and Salvage.

pages.title: Firearms
pages.text:
• §6Musket§r (bronze and steam age, Metalworker's Bench): hold §lright-click for 3 seconds§r then release to §lload§r it with §l1 lead ball and 1 gunpowder§r (the muzzle comes up, the ramrod rams the charge). Loaded, a right-click fires §lone very powerful shot§r (20 damage, §l64-block§r range): smoke, recoil. It must be reloaded after every shot.
• §6Revolver§r (MKI, Metalworker's Bench): §l6 shots§r with §lcartridges§r; sneak and hold right-click to reload §lone cartridge at a time§r. Weaker per shot (8 damage, 40-block range) but much faster.
• §lLead balls§r: 8 per lead ingot at the Metalworker's Bench, or 16 per ingot at the §lfoundry§r (sand mold). §lCartridges§r: a brass plate, 4 balls and 2 gunpowder make 4 cartridges (Metalworker's Bench).
• Aim is not perfect: shots §lspread§r a little (less with the Hunting skill). §lNever underwater§r: the powder gets wet.
• A gunshot §lscares game away§r within 32 blocks: sneak up and fire only once.
• Against a player, damage is §lhalved§r (server setting §lhunt.firearmPvpFactor§r); clan allies and animals in protected claims stay untouchable.

pages.title: Harpoon, gun rack and trophies
pages.text:
• §6Harpoon§r (bronze age, Metalworker's Bench): hold right-click then release to §lthrow§r it, §leven underwater§r. It stays §ltied to a rope§r (32 blocks): the harpooned animal is §lslowed§r and §lpulled toward you§r when the rope tightens (sea giants, too big, are only slowed). Right-click: you §lreel the rope in§r and the harpoon comes back to your hand. Damage §l×2.5 against sea creatures§r: the weapon for whales and sharks (you can aim at a whale's head or tail).
• §6Gun rack§r (11 woods, Carpenter's Bench): a wall board with §lthree rows§r. Right-click with a musket, a revolver or a harpoon: the weapon goes up, lying on its pegs; empty hand: take it back.
• §6Trophies§r: §l5%§r chance (10% at Hunting level 10) when you kill a §lstag carrying its antlers§r (wall-mounted deer head), a §lbear§r (bear rug on the floor) or a §lshark§r (wall-mounted shark, not the whale shark). They are real mounted animals: same model and coat as the animal.

pages.title: Game cooking
pages.text:
Hunting loot goes through the mod's §6kitchen stations§r, like livestock.
• §lSmoking§r: any raw game meat (venison, boar, bison, bear, big game, whale, seal, turkey, pigeon) dries on the §ldrying rack§r (dried game meat), then goes into the §lsmokehouse§r: §lsmoked game meat§r, filling and long-lasting. §lShark§r meat and §lray§r wings are fish: fillets, dried then smoked fish, fish soups and skewers.
• §lMinced meat§r: red game meat can be minced on the cutting board; chili, lasagna, stuffed peppers and sausages take it.
• §lDishes§r: §lgame stew§r (cooking pot: 2 meats, mushrooms, onion, carrot, wine), §lgame skewers§r (mixing bowl then frying pan), §lstuffed turkey§r (mixing bowl: turkey, bread, onion, cranberries, butter; then bread oven), §lpigeon with peas§r and §lskate wing with butter§r (cooking pot), §lgame pâté§r in a jar (preserve).
• §lLamp oil§r: 2 whale blubbers in the §lfruit press§r give 250 mB of fish oil; an §lempty bottle§r in the press's “Fill” slot fills it. It fuels the §loil sconce§r and the §loil lantern§r (instead of beeswax) and burns in a furnace.
• §lTallow candles§r: whale blubber + string → 2 candles (Carpenter's Bench, knife).
• §lDeer antler§r: ground at the millstone (4 bone meal) or in a mortar (2); it also makes a §lknife handle§r instead of a stick.
• Cooked and smoked meats and dishes §lsell§r to villagers like livestock products.

pages.title: Server settings
pages.text:
The living world is set in the server's §6common configuration§r (§lpioneers-common.toml§r), sections §lseasons§r, §lfauna§r, §lpets§r and §lhunt§r. Every setting is commented and bounded.
• §lseasons§r: length of a season (1 to 30 days, 10 by default), seasonal weather.
• §lfauna§r: persistent wildlife (on / off), repopulation period (10 min), threshold (25%), distances to players (64) and villages (48), lighter AI beyond 48 blocks, wild breeding, thieves (§lratTheft§r, §lmonkeyTheft§r, §lseagullTheft§r), herds (every 1 to 2 days, 48 to 96 blocks, 4 to 10 animals) and §lcaps per zone§r of 128 × 128 blocks: game 48, predators 8, birds 24, sea creatures 16, fish 48.
• §lpets§r: recall cooldown, territory radius, protection of animals that have an owner, cat fishing.
• §lhunt§r: firearm damage against players (§lfirearmPvpFactor§r, 0.5).
Budget: at most §l144 wild animals per zone§r, plus one herd of at most 10 animals per player or group of nearby players; far from players, animals make decisions 4 times less often. Operator commands: §l/pioneer season§r, §l/pioneer fauna§r, §l/pioneer hunt§r.

pages.title: Finding oil
pages.text:
Oil and gas fields lie only under §ldeserts§r and §loceans§r; brine, anywhere. They are both §lreal§r and §lvirtual§r: above the field, the desert hides §6oil pools§r rimmed with §6tar sand§r, and the ocean floor §6seeps§r; below, a reserve of millions of mB that only wells can reach.

The §6seismograph§r (right-click) listens to the ground: under your feet it gives the field, its reserve and its pressure; otherwise the direction and distance of the nearest one (160 blocks). Tar sand, washed with steam in the §6centrifuge (decanting)§r, gives §lbitumen§r.

pages.title: Wells and pressure
pages.text:
The §6pumpjack§r draws oil, natural gas and brine (and lithium brine) from the field under its chunk: it is a §lmultiblock only§r (no compact version; Shift + right-click the controller for the blueprint), whose tier sets the number of parallel operations. The §6fluid pump§r (a multiblock too) sucks up fluid blocks below it (water never runs out).

The more a field is drained, the lower its §lpressure§r (25% when dry). Put §lwater§r in the well: it is injected and brings pressure back to 100% (0.5 mB per mB drawn); §6drilling mud§r does twice as well. Associated gas comes out through a gas tank (helium from a gas field through the second one); a gas field also yields a little §lcondensate§r.

At higher tiers the pumpjack runs more operations at once (4 / 8 / 16 / 32): enough to drain a large field quickly.

pages.title: The offshore platform
pages.text:
The §6offshore platform§r has §lno fixed shape§r: a deck of casings (glass, ports) in one piece, up to §l64 × 64§r blocks. §lController, ports and risers wherever you like§r. The controller blueprint shows a square deck, as an example.

Each §6riser§r is a §6column pump§r (any tier) set in the deck; it needs §lwater below§r (at least 3 blocks) down to the seabed. You have nothing to lower: the platform §llowers its own tubing§r, one §6production tubing§r per block of water, under an animated heave compensator. It §lrequests§r it: bring it through an item port, or let the robotic network deliver it. A riser produces once it reaches the seabed (wellhead, crude rising up the tubing), is worth 2 operations and draws the field of §lits own chunk§r.

Controller broken: the tubing comes back up and drops nearby.

pages.title: Distillation
pages.text:
The §6distillation column§r cuts crude into §lsix fractions§r, top to bottom: LPG, naphtha, kerosene, diesel, fuel oil, atmospheric residue (plus refinery gas). Cuts are §lfixed§r for each crude (light, desalted, heavy, synthetic, condensate): nothing to tune.

Each fraction leaves through an output §6fluid port§r at §lits own height§r: the highest port gives LPG, the next one naphtha, and so on (ports at the same height share a fraction; the lowest also takes the rest). The §6distillation column (vacuum)§r takes the residue: vacuum gas oil, base oil, fuel oil, vacuum residue, paraffin wax.

Need §la single§r fraction? The §6compact distillery§r (MKI to MKIV, no multiblock) takes the same inputs as each column recipe and keeps §lonly one§r output, chosen with the §lrecipe selector§r (naphtha only, diesel only, refinery gas only…). The other fractions are lost and it is §l1.5 times slower§r: the column stays the high-yield route, the distillery is the small-workshop one.

pages.title: Conversion
Catalysts
pages.text:
Five catalysts, made in the §6mixer§r on an alumina support: §lplatinum§r (reforming, nitric acid, hydrogen peroxide), §lnickel§r (hydrogenation, methanol, syngas), §lzeolite§r (cracking, polymers, Claus), §liron§r (ammonia), §lvanadium§r (sulfur trioxide).

A catalyst almost always §lcomes back§r (95% or better); otherwise it comes out §lspent§r. Four spent catalysts go back into the §6cracker§r with oxygen to make three fresh ones.

pages.title: Air, gases and cold
pages.text:
The §6industrial gas separator (air separation)§r (multiblock) draws in air: §lnitrogen, oxygen, argon§r; at advanced tier the same as liquids, and the rare gases (§lneon, krypton, xenon§r). The §6cryogenic unit§r also draws air and §lliquefies§r gases: §l8 mB of gas for 1 mB of liquid§r (LPG, LNG, liquid oxygen, argon and nitrogen; liquid hydrogen and helium at elite tier). The §6cryogenic unit (heat exchange)§r vaporizes them again.

Helium is drawn from natural gas in the §6gas separator§r; the §6cryogenic unit (refrigeration)§r liquefies chlorine and butane, makes dry ice and dewaxes oil.

pages.title: Heavy chemistry
Plastics and rubber
pages.text:
The §6chemical reactor (polymerization)§r (zeolite) makes pellets: §lpolyethylene§r (ethylene), §lpolypropylene§r, §lPVC§r (vinyl chloride), §lpolystyrene§r, §lPTFE§r (tetrafluoroethylene, from refrigerant in the cracker). The §6extruder§r turns them into sheets and pipes; the §6casting machine (injection molding)§r into casings and components.

Rubber: the basic route vulcanizes §lnatural rubber§r (3 + 1 sulfur → 1, in the autoclave); the petrochemical route, more profitable: butadiene → §6latex§r → synthetic rubber (autoclave) → 2 synthetic + 1 sulfur → §l2§r vulcanized, or §6mixer§r (carbon black, sulfur, aniline) → §6autoclave (vulcanization)§r → §6rolling mill (calendering)§r: sheets, §lgaskets§r, belts. §lSulfur§r comes from coke oven gas passed over iron dust (§6chemical reactor§r), from lazurite or from the Claus process.

The §ladvanced tier§r: frames need plastic, casings and kits gaskets.

pages.title: Electronics
Isotopes
Extraction and yellowcake
pages.text:
1. §lLeaching§r (extractor (leaching)): 2 pitchblende concentrates + 500 mB sulfuric acid → 1,000 mB §6uranium solution§r.
2. §lSolvent§r (mixer): 900 mB kerosene + 100 mB amine solution → 1,000 mB §6extraction solvent§r.
3. §6Extractor (solvent extraction)§r: 1,000 mB solution + 100 mB solvent → 100 mB §6loaded solvent§r and 1,000 mB §6acid raffinate§r.
4. Same machine, §lstripping§r: loaded solvent + 100 mB ammonia → §6ammonium diuranate§r; 95% of the solvent comes back.
5. §lCalcination§r (industrial furnace (roasting)): diuranate → §6yellowcake§r (and a little ammonia).
The raffinate is neutralized with quicklime in the mixer: water and §6uranium tailings§r, which the cracker heats to release §lradon§r.

pages.title: Conversion
pages.text:
The §6chemical reactor (fluidized bed)§r does all the conversion; the powder floats in the gas flowing through it.
1. Yellowcake + 500 mB nitric acid (extractor (leaching)) → §6uranyl nitrate§r.
2. §lDenitration§r: uranyl nitrate → §6uranium trioxide§r (orange), nitrogen dioxide and water.
3. §lReduction§r: UO₃ + 500 mB hydrogen → §6uranium dioxide§r (brown).
4. §lHydrofluorination§r: UO₂ + 1,000 mB hydrogen fluoride → §6uranium tetrafluoride§r, the "green salt".
5. §lFluorination§r: UF₄ + 500 mB fluorine → 1,000 mB §6uranium hexafluoride§r (UF₆), the only uranium compound that is a gas.
UF₆ and uranyl nitrate are §lcorrosive§r: you need advanced cables.

pages.title: Enrichment
pages.text:
Natural uranium contains only 0.7% uranium-235. The §6centrifuge cascade§r (multiblock only, low hall) raises it to 4%:
1,000 mB natural UF₆ → 100 mB §6enriched UF₆§r + 900 mB §6depleted UF₆§r, in 20 s per operation.
The §6gas centrifuges§r are built into the hall (a real cascade has dozens of rotors); as with every multiblock, the §ltier§r sets the number of parallel operations.
§lDepleted UF₆§r is not waste: in the fluidized bed (with hydrogen) it turns back into tetrafluoride, which the industrial furnace (reduction) turns with magnesium into §6depleted uranium§r metal. Rolled into plates, very dense, it goes into the reactor's controller; the §6magnesium fluoride§r gives its fluorine back to sulfuric acid.

pages.title: Fuel
pages.text:
1. §lDeconversion§r (fluidized bed): 1,000 mB enriched UF₆ + 500 mB hydrogen + 250 mB steam → §6enriched uranium dioxide§r; the hydrogen fluoride goes back to hydrofluorination.
2. §lPressing§r (press): 1 enriched UO₂ → 4 §6green fuel pellets§r.
3. §lSintering§r under hydrogen (industrial furnace (sintering), 20 s) → 4 §6fuel pellets§r.
4. §lCladding§r (extruder, with a tube die): 1 zircaloy ingot → 4 §6zircaloy cladding tubes§r.
5. §lRod§r (assembler (arc welding), under helium): 1 tube + 4 pellets → 1 §6fuel rod§r.
6. §lAssembly§r (assembler): 9 rods + 2 §6spacer grids§r (bender, zircaloy plate) + 2 stainless plates → 1 §6fuel assembly§r.
§6Control rod clusters§r: 4 boron carbide (arc furnace: boron-10 + graphite) + 4 tubes + 1 stainless plate.

pages.title: The Generation I fission reactor
pages.text:
The reactor is a §lround vessel§r built like the real thing (Shift + right-click the controller for the blueprint): casing base (controller, ports), §6sheet metal§r wall with glass strips, casing lid.
• Inside: staggered columns of §6fuel channels§r; each channel takes §lone assembly§r. The rest of the vessel stays §lempty§r: water comes in through the ports and shows through the glass.
• Lid: all casings; the §6control rods§r are §lbuilt in§r, one above each column, and are driven from the interface.
• Shell: an item port in (fresh assemblies) and one out (spent assemblies), a fluid port in (water or coolant), a gas port out for the §lsteam§r (a gas) and a fluid port out for the hot coolant.
• The §lcasings§r set the nominal temperature: basic 800 K, advanced 1,100, elite 1,500, ultimate 2,100. The higher it is, the more margin you have.
An assembly heats at §l40,000 J/t§r at full power and lasts §lone hour§r of play; it comes out hot and must go to the pool.

pages.title: Operating the reactor
pages.text:
The controller's screen shows §lpower§r, §ltemperature§r and its limits, the assemblies and their burnup, and what keeps power from rising (no fuel, no water, steam not removed…).
• §6Autopilot§r (“Autopilot” button, on by default): it withdraws the rods slowly and holds the core at its operating temperature; power settles on the water received and the steam removed. So the reactor starts §lby itself§r once fueled. It re-arms a heat shutdown by itself.
• §6Control rods§r: from 0 (withdrawn, full power) to 100 (inserted, core smothered). Setting them by hand (−10 … +10) switches to §lmanual§r mode.
• Power follows the rods with a little lag. As the vessel heats, the reaction slows by itself (§lnegative feedback§r), but never below 30%: without water, it keeps heating.
• §6Emergency shutdown§r: rods fully in and locked. It trips by itself at 90% of nominal (can be disabled, at your own risk), by the button, or by a §lredstone signal§r on the controller. Reset once the temperature has dropped.
• After a shutdown, §ldecay heat§r goes on: 6 % of the power, fading over a minute. Keep the water flowing!
• A comparator reads the power percentage; the PLC can set the rods.

pages.title: Runaway and radiation
pages.text:
Above 105% of nominal, the alarm sounds. The core starts melting: through the glass you see the §6corium§r (translucent flowing magma) rise at the bottom of the vessel. Above §l125% for 10 s§r, the core §6melts down§r:
• the inside and shell vanish, the bottom fills with glowing §6corium§r;
• an explosion digs a crater of §l15 blocks + 1 per assembly§r (25 at most);
• a §6contaminated zone§r twice as wide settles in; it halves every 3 game days; grass dies in it.
§lRadiation§r builds up in you (dose in sieverts): nausea above 1 Sv, weakness above 2, wither above 4. It drops slowly once you move away. Hot spent assemblies and corium also irradiate from your inventory.
The §6dosimeter§r shows rate and dose. A full §6hazmat suit§r stops 95% of the radiation.
Corium cools into §6cooled corium§r after about a day; with a diamond pickaxe it gives §6corium chunks§r, to be stored.

pages.title: Pool and storage
pages.text:
A spent assembly comes out §6hot§r: it still heats and irradiates strongly.
The §6spent fuel pool§r (multiblock only, deep basin) keeps it under water for 2 minutes (1,000 mB of water evaporated): it comes out as a cold §6spent fuel assembly§r. The §6spent fuel racks§r are built into the basin; the tier sets how many assemblies are handled at once. The pool heats up: plan for cooling.
Spent assemblies go to §lreprocessing§r (recovered uranium and plutonium, see "Reprocessing"); the ones you keep and corium chunks are sealed in a §6dry storage cask§r (concrete and steel) that you place like a block.

pages.title: Thorium and higher enrichment
pages.text:
§6Monazite§r is found in beach and river sand deposits. Ground, then run over the ore separator (shaking table), it gives a concentrate that caustic soda attacks (chemical reactor): §6thorium hydroxide§r. Nitric acid pulls out §6thorium nitrate§r and §6rare earth oxides§r (for lasers); the extractor (solvent extraction) gives §6thorium dioxide§r.
4% enriched UF₆ goes back into the cascade: §lHALEU§r (20%), then §lHEU§r (90%), for the fragment reactor.
The §6centrifuge cascade (laser)§r does the same §lwithout a cascade§r, faster and with a better yield (12% enriched instead of 10%). At elite tier, the fluidized bed also does §ldry conversion§r: yellowcake → UF₄ in one pass.

pages.title: Targets and hot cell
pages.text:
Generation I and II fission reactors take §6targets§r next to the fuel (at most half the slots): the core's heat irradiates them (200 MJ each), then they come out through the output port.
• §6Lithium-6 target§r → in the §6hot cell§r: §ltritium§r and a little §lhelium-3§r (fusion fuels).
• §6Neptunium target§r (neptunium comes from reprocessing) → §6plutonium-238§r.
Plutonium-238 clad in iridium makes a §6heat source§r that powers a §6radioisotope thermoelectric generator§r: 4,096 FE/t with no upkeep, for many game days (−1% per day). Right-click to insert the source, Shift + empty-hand click to take it back.
The hot cell also makes the americium-beryllium §6neutron source§r that starts Generation II and III reactors.

pages.title: Reprocessing
pages.text:
The §6hot cell (reprocessing)§r (tower, pulsed columns, stack) runs the §lPUREX§r process:
1. §lShearing and dissolution§r: spent assembly + nitric acid → §6dissolved fuel§r, §6cladding hulls§r and a little krypton.
2. §lExtraction§r: dissolved fuel + solvent → §6uranyl nitrate§r (uranium goes back to conversion), §6plutonium nitrate§r, §6high-level waste§r, sometimes §6neptunium-237§r.
3. The fluidized bed turns plutonium nitrate into §6plutonium dioxide§r (or, with fluorine, into plutonium gas for stellar cores).
The hot cell also separates §6americium-241§r from the waste and opens irradiated thorium blankets (§6uranium-233§r). Hulls are compacted in the press.

pages.title: Generation II fast neutron reactor
pages.text:
A sodium-cooled §lbreeder§r, inspired by Superphénix: a round sheet-metal §lpool vessel§r (glass strips), the §6fast channel§r §lcore§r at the bottom, and a §lslab§r carrying the machinery.
• The slab, all casings, carries the §lbuilt-in§r machinery: the §6control rods§r in the center, above the core, 2 primary pumps and 2 intermediate heat exchangers.
• Fuel: §6MOX assemblies§r (120,000 J/t each, three times Generation I). Around them: depleted uranium or thorium §6blankets§r, which become plutonium or uranium-233: it makes §l1.2 times§r what it burns.
• Sodium (molten-salt electrolysis, Downs process) comes in through a port and fills the vessel, where you can see it ripple: 1,000 mB per channel, never consumed. Water turns to steam through the exchangers (+25% steam).
• ⚠ §lPositive void coefficient§r: if sodium is missing, the reaction §lspeeds up§r. Never drain a running Generation II reactor.

pages.title: Generation III fission fragment reactor
pages.text:
The age's most advanced reactor: a §lsphere§r where a §6dusty plasma§r of highly enriched uranium floats in a magnetic field. The fission fragments, flying fast, are slowed by an electric field: they make §lelectricity directly§r (80%), with no water or turbine.
• Build: a §lslab§r at the bottom and one on top, a round glass wall between them, and in the middle the §lglazed sphere§r (§6diamond reflector§r ribs) held by four §6frame§r columns. A ring of §6confinement coils§r circles it at the equator; a §6fragment collector§r sits in the center of each slab.
• Materials from §lUranus and Neptune§r: §6rain diamond lattice§r, §6veronite superconductor§r (Miranda), §6messinite ceramic§r (Titania), §6ruachite crystal grid§r (Triton).
• Fuel: §6fragment cartridges§r (HEU nanopowder in a diamond shell), 600,000 J/t each.
• §lIgnition§r: the field charges from the energy reserve (energy input port), then keeps 10% of the output. If power fails, the field drops: above 50% power, the plasma §ldisperses§r: an explosion and wider contamination than a meltdown.

pages.title: Waste and deep storage
pages.text:
§6High-level waste§r is §lvitrified§r: hot cell (vitrification), borosilicate frit (sand, soda, boron) and a stainless canister → §6vitrified waste canister§r.
4 vitrified canisters (or 8 compacted hulls), steel and copper make a §6waste package§r. Left in the open, it irradiates (2 Sv/h).
§lDeep storage§r: bury the package §lbelow level 0§r, surrounded on all 6 sides by rock (stone, deepslate, tuff, clay, granite, diorite, andesite, calcite): it stops irradiating entirely. Dig a deep gallery, line up the packages, backfill.

pages.title: Fusion
pages.text:
Two fusion reactors built like the real thing: a §llarge thin ring§r on a round base, a glazed §6vacuum chamber§r showing the plasma, its lower half lined (§6blankets§r or §6converters§r), and the coils around it. Each reactor has a single size (the blueprint's).
Cycle: §lfield ramp-up§r (superconducting coils, cooled with liquid helium) → §lheating§r (Heat button: built-in neutral beam injection and gyrotron, a lot of energy taken from the input ports) → §lignition§r → the plasma burns by itself and heating stops.
• Each coil drinks 1 mB/t of §6liquid helium§r (16 for a tokamak); boiled-off helium comes out as gas, to be reliquefied.
• §lDisruption§r: if the field drops below 50% (missing helium or power), or if the tokamak runs out of fuel or overheats, the plasma dies at once: an explosion without crater, 2 casings scorched, a small tritium leak. No meltdown.
• STOP shuts down cleanly (no more fuel, quench without damage).

pages.title: Tokamak (Generation I)
pages.text:
§lDeuterium-tritium§r fusion, peak reactivity near 150 million degrees.
• Build: §l16 D-shaped toroidal field coils§r around the chamber, the §6central solenoid§r as a column in the middle of the ring (neutral beam injection is built in), the lower half of the chamber in §6breeding blankets§r.
• Gases: deuterium (heavy water) and tritium; the plasma is full when each gas has 1,000 mB in store. The ash leaves as helium.
• The heat boils water (coolant port): up to 4 MJ/t for a large torus.
• §6Breeding blankets§r: neutrons turn §6lithium ceramic pebbles§r into tritium (ratio 1.1); with enough blankets, the tokamak breeds its own tritium.

pages.title: Heliotron (Generation II)
pages.text:
§lDeuterium-helium-3§r fusion, neutron-free: no blankets, no radioactivity, and §l70% of the power as direct electricity§r (direct converters: up to 90%), up to 10 MFE/t.
• Two continuous §6helical coils§r wind around the chamber (5 turns around the ring) and twist the plasma into a ribbon: no solenoid, no disruption as long as liquid helium does not run out. The lower half of the chamber is made of §6direct converters§r.
• The helical coils need §6sulcite HTS tape§r: sulcite from §lGanymede§r, the only moon with its own magnetic field.
• §6Helium-3§r comes from §llunar regolith§r: 16 moon sand in the cracker → 25 mB (the solar wind has been laying it down for billions of years).

pages.title: Machines that compute
pages.text:
Computing begins in the Industrial Age with §lsimple, low-power§r machines: they watch over and control your factories.
• The §6data link tool§r links machines: §lShift + right-click§r a machine to remember it, then §lright-click§r a cabinet, a PLC or a screen (same dimension, 64 blocks at most).
• The §6relay cabinet§r (electromechanical relays) applies §l4 rules§r every second to 2 linked machines.
• The §6programmable logic controller§r or PLC (chips) applies §l16 rules§r 4 times a second to 4 machines, with timers, counters and latches.
• The §6supervision screen§r shows a linked machine's state and a value's curve; put several side by side for a big screen (a rectangle of up to 6 × 4, a single frame, text sized to the screen; an assembly that is not a rectangle is split into rectangular screens, the largest first).
Next (following pages): real programmable computers, data centers and AI.

pages.title: Writing rules
pages.text:
A rule reads: §lIF§r [linked machine].[value] [comparison] [threshold] §lTHEN§r [action].
• Values: status, temperature, energy %, progress, tank fill; for a reactor: power %, temperature, rods, fuel.
• Comparisons: >, <, =, ≥, ≤, ≠.
• Actions: §lredstone§r output on a face (level 0 to 15), or a §lcommand§r to a linked machine: for a reactor, rods = n, emergency shutdown, reset, auto shutdown.
Example: IF reactor.temperature > 1,200 THEN rods = 80; IF reactor.temperature < 1,000 THEN rods = 20: the plant regulates itself.

pages.title: The computer
pages.text:
The §6computer§r (workstation) is programmed in §lPioScript§r, a simplified Python. Right-click: the terminal opens, with an editor (line numbers, colors), a console and the file list.
• Internal disk §lc:§r (32 KB) and two drives §la:§r / §lb:§r for §6floppy disks§r (64 KB): right-click with a disk in hand to insert it.
• §lCtrl + S§r saves, §lF5§r runs, the Stop button interrupts. Errors give the line.
• Link up to 4 machines with the data link tool: §llink(1)§r to §llink(4)§r in the program.
• A program restarts from the top when the world is reloaded.
The §6examples disk§r (disk + book) holds commented programs (bonjour.py, clignotant.py, compteur.py, tableau.py, reacteur.py, vol.py, rail.py, journal.py) and §lfonctions.txt§r, the full language reference.

pages.title: PioScript
pages.text:
Like Python: numbers, strings, f-strings §lf"{x:.2f}"§r, lists, dictionaries, §lif / elif / else§r, §lwhile§r, §lfor x in range(10)§r, §ldef§r, recursion. No classes, imports or exceptions.
• §lprint(…)§r, §linput(…)§r, §lsleep(seconds)§r (§lsleep(0.05)§r = 1 tick), §ltime()§r.
• §lredstone.get("north")§r, §lredstone.set("up", 15)§r.
• §lm = link(1)§r; §lm.value("temperature")§r, §lm.values()§r, §lm.command("rods", 40)§r, §lm.command("scram")§r.
• §lscreen.print(text)§r, §lscreen.write(line, text)§r: on linked supervision screens.
• §lfs.write(name, text)§r, §lfs.read(name)§r, §lfs.list()§r.
Example: a loop that reads the reactor temperature every second and trims the rods to hold it at 1,100 K.

pages.title: PioScript: built-in help
PioScript: the library (1/2)
pages.text:
• §lBuilt-in functions§r: print, input, help, len, type, isinstance, str, int, float, bool, repr, format, range, enumerate, zip, list, dict, sorted, reversed, min, max, sum, any, all, abs, round, divmod, chr, ord, hex, bin, random, randint, sleep, time
• §lMaths (math)§r: math.pi, math.e, math.tau, math.inf, math.sqrt, math.pow, math.floor, math.ceil, math.trunc, math.sign, math.clamp, math.lerp, math.sin, math.cos, math.tan, math.asin, math.acos, math.atan, math.atan2, math.degrees, math.radians, math.hypot, math.exp, math.log, math.log10, math.gcd, math.mean, math.median, math.isnan
• §lText (str methods)§r: upper, lower, title, capitalize, strip, split, splitlines, partition, join, replace, startswith, endswith, find, rfind, count, isdigit, isalpha, isalnum, isspace, isupper, zfill, ljust, rjust, center
• §lLists (list methods)§r: append, extend, insert, pop, remove, index, count, sort, reverse, clear, copy
• §lDictionaries (dict methods)§r: keys, values, items, get, setdefault, pop, update, clear, copy
• §lJSON (json)§r: json.dumps, json.loads

pages.title: PioScript: the library (2/2)
pages.text:
• §lRedstone (redstone)§r: redstone.get, redstone.set, redstone.output, redstone.inputs, redstone.all
• §lLinked machines (link)§r: link, links, connected, name, keys, value, values, commands, command, lockRecipe, unlockRecipe, lockedRecipe
• §lDigital network (network)§r: network.connected, network.data, network.stored, network.capacity, network.compute, network.machines, network.machine, network.find
• §lSupervision screens (screen)§r: screen.print, screen.write, screen.clear, screen.rows, screen.cols, screen.center, screen.bar
• §lFiles (fs)§r: fs.list, fs.read, fs.write, fs.append, fs.lines, fs.exists, fs.size, fs.delete, fs.rename, fs.copy, fs.free
• §lWorld and time (world)§r: world.time, world.clock, world.day, world.is_day, world.moon, world.weather, world.dimension, world.biome
• §lThe computer (computer)§r: computer.position, computer.energy, computer.energy_max, computer.program, computer.beep
• §lComputing network (compute)§r: compute.available, compute.quantum, compute.request, compute.total
• §lFlight computers (flight)§r: flight.check, flight.flash
• §lRailroad (rail)§r: rail.trains, rail.train, rail.send, rail.stations, rail.station, rail.set_limit, rail.signal, rail.get_signal, rail.weigh, rail.deliveries
• §lShipping (naval)§r: naval.ships, naval.ship, naval.send, naval.ports

pages.title: Data centers
pages.text:
§6Computing power§r becomes a resource, measured in §lGOPS§r. The §6data center§r (a plain box) produces it: each §6server rack§r gives §l256 GOPS§r and draws 8,192 FE/t at full load (10% idle).
• Computation (and telemetry) leaves through §llogistic cables MKI or better§r, plugged into a wall §6data port§r (or touching the structure anywhere): a network's supply is shared among demands every second.
• Racks heat up (2 J per FE): above 1,500 K, computation is throttled. The controller carries its §6cryogenic unit (refrigeration) units§r (fans to the air, powered by the racks' energy); add water, coolant or liquid nitrogen for big halls.
• It also produces §6telemetry§r (a data type) used to train AIs.
• Consumers: AI lab, §lresearch lab§r (up to ×4 faster), PioScript programs (§lcompute.request(n)§r).

pages.title: Quantum computer
pages.text:
Under its dome hangs the §6dilution refrigerator§r, a gilded chandelier of stepped plates that goes down to a few §lmillikelvin§r. Its §6qubit arrays§r (Josephson junction chips) give quantum computation, in §lQOPS§r: 8 each, for 16,384 FE/t.
• It drinks §6helium-3§r (1 mB/s) and §6liquid helium§r (5 mB/s); it takes 60 s to reach coherence.
• Without fluid, it warms up in 10 s: §ldecoherence§r, no more computation.
• Only the most advanced AI model needs it: this is where fusion (helium-3), cryogenics and computing meet.

pages.title: Artificial intelligence
pages.text:
The §6AI lab§r trains a §6blank neural chip§r with §ldata§r (logistic cables MKI or better) and §lcomputation§r:
• §6Expert system§r: 5,000 data units, 20,000 GOPS·s.
• §6Neural network§r: an expert system + 20,000 data including telemetry, 200,000 GOPS·s.
• §6Foundation model§r: a network + 100,000 data, 2,000,000 GOPS·s and 2,000 QOPS·s (quantum computer).
§lUses§r: right-click a multiblock's controller with a chip: it installs (Shift + empty-hand click to take it back). Expert −10% energy; neural −20% and +20% speed; foundation −30% and +40%. The §6AI upgrade card§r for robotic hubs makes units faster and longer-lasting.

pages.title: The factory AI core
pages.text:
The §6factory AI core§r is an AI that §lruns your factory§r. Put a neural network (16 machines) or foundation model (64 machines) in it, then link machines to it with the data link tool.
• It gives its chip's bonus to every linked multiblock.
• It §lregulates reactors§r: for fission, it inserts the rods above 85% power and shuts down preventively before the limit; for fusion, it cuts heating and quenches cleanly when a disruption looms.
• It §ltalks§r: failures, records, interventions and a few jokes, in nearby players' chat and on linked supervision screens. The neural network is called §lNOVA§r, the foundation model §lPROMETHEUS§r.

pages.title: One cable, three services
Data
pages.text:
1. §lProduce§r: the §6receiving antenna§r collects data from probes and satellites; the geo-spectrometer, bio-sequencer, asteroid crusher and biome analyzer get theirs from samples. Each pours it into the cable through its output faces.
2. §lCarry§r: the cable carries it on its Data channel; in auto mode, to the connected machines that accept it; in the network diagram, a Data channel can filter by type.
3. §lStore§r: a §6data bank§r keeps one type; the network adds up all its banks: that is the §lnetwork stock§r.
4. §lUse§r: the §6research lab§r and the §6AI lab§r §ldraw on their own§r from the network's banks whatever they lack: no need to set a bank to output any more. The synthesizer gets its own through its data ports.

pages.title: Shared computing
pages.text:
Computing is §lnot data§r: it fills nothing and does not travel. A §6data center§r (GOPS) or a §6quantum computer§r (QOPS) offers power; everything touching the same network (by cable, through a structure's §6data port§r, or placed against it) shares it.
• Every second, supply is split §lin proportion to demand§r: if demand exceeds supply, everyone gets a share and everything slows down.
• Users: research lab (faster, then required in advanced eras), AI lab, computers.
• The terminal shows supply and demand; a red bar = not enough computing.

pages.title: Supervision
The network terminal
Where to start?
pages.text:
1. An MKI §6logistic cable§r and a §6network terminal§r.
2. A §6data bank§r on the cable: without it nothing is kept.
3. A source: §6antenna§r (probes), or an analyzer.
4. A §6research lab§r on the same cable; start a research (K key): it draws from the banks.
5. Later, a §6data center§r linked to the cable through a data port: research speeds up, AI becomes possible.
6. To automate: a controller or computer on the cable.
At every step, the terminal's “What next?” tab says what is missing.

pages.title: The cable, the network medium
pages.text:
Since 1.11, the §6logistic cable§r §lMKI or better§r carries §ldata§r, a resource type of its own (neither item, fluid nor gas), measured in MB: 2,000 / 16,000 / 128,000 / 1,024,000 MB/t per channel from MKI to MKIV (wood and bronze do not carry it; a mixed network runs at the level of the weakest).
• A data machine connects like any other: the plug shows on a side open to data (“Data” channel of the sides panel); it ejects according to its sides, the network delivers to the others (auto mode) or according to the data channel set in the diagram.
• Every MKI-or-better network §lis§r the digital network: §lcomputing§r and §lsupervision§r need no channel, touching the cable is enough.
• Old optical fibers became logistic cables of the same level.

pages.title: Antenna and banks
pages.text:
§6Antenna§r: its dish picks up the data of all your probes (64,000 MB buffer) and sends it through its output sides.

§6Data banks§r: one data type each, they keep their contents when broken.
• MKI: 1 M MB, 2,000 MB/t;  MKII: 4 M, 8,000;
• MKIII: 16 M, 32,000;  MKIV: 64 M, 128,000.
• Creative (creative only): endless source of one data type; one variant per type in the Logistics tab.
By default they receive from the back and sides and give from the bottom; the front gauge shows how full they are.

pages.title: Research lab
pages.text:
The lab has a memory of §l16 tanks of 100,000 MB§r, each able to take any type (one type per tank); store the surplus in banks. It spends that data to advance the §6research tree§r: new worlds, rocket blueprints, probes, suits, machines...

"Research" page: the tree, with the active research and the queue. "Memory" page: the data on hand and, at the bottom, the 4 §lanalysis data§r tanks, turned into samples for the research they feed. The "Quantum labs" research doubles computing speed. Research is shared by everyone (server-wide).

When a recipe requires research, a §lwarning tab§r appears on the right of the GUI: hover it to see which one.

pages.title: Milestones and computing
Mastering worlds
pages.text:
Each world is mastered in 4 steps: §lorbit§r (probe data), §lsurface§r (surface scanner, biome cells read by the biome analyzer), §lgeology§r (asteroid crusher, spectrometer) and §lbiology§r (sequencer).

The crusher, spectrometer and sequencer do not research by themselves: they produce analysis data of a precise type (one per asteroid family; geology or biology of the world of origin: lunarium ore gives Moon geology), to be sent through logistic cables (MKI or better; back side by default) to a research lab. §l1 GB = 1 sample§r.

The §6biome analyzer§r reads up to 9 biome cells (not consumed) and produces 25 MB/t of each biome's data for 200 FE/t per cell. Only space biomes give a cell. The lab spends 10,000 MB of a biome's data to validate its exploration.

Mastering a world's orbit allows landing there. The next steps improve drilling, yields and farming on site.

pages.title: Leaving Earth
Propellants
pages.text:
The §6propellant plant§r (4-tier workshop or cryogenic sphere multiblock) doses and subcools propellants:
1. §lRP-1§r (industrial cracker (hydrocracking)): 1,000 mB kerosene + 100 mB hydrogen → 950 mB.
2. §6Kerolox§r (advanced tier): 300 mB RP-1 + 700 mB liquid oxygen → 1,000 mB. Rockets §lT1-T2§r.
3. §6Hydrolox§r (elite tier): 750 mB liquid hydrogen + 250 mB liquid oxygen. Rockets §lT1-T7§r.
4. Pure §6liquid hydrogen§r: the nuclear thermal propulsion of §lT8-T10§r heats it in a reactor.
5. §6D-³He fusion propellant§r (ultimate tier): deuterium + lunar helium-3 + liquid helium. Rockets §lT11-T13§r.
The launch pad refuses to fill a rocket with a propellant that does not suit it ("Wrong propellant"). Propellants are cryogenic: advanced cables.

pages.title: The flight computer
pages.text:
The §6flight computer§r is the avionics of every probe and every rocket nose cone. It comes §lblank§r out of the assembly bench.
Put it in a §6computer§r drive (right-click, the whole stack at once) then run a PioScript program:
§lflight.flash("a")§r programs the whole stack in drive A (§lflight.flash("a", "Lunar probe")§r gives it a mission name);
§lflight.check("a")§r answers "none", "blank" or "programmed".
The §lvol.py§r program on the examples disk programs them continuously.
The probe module and the nose cones of every rocket need a programmed flight computer.

pages.title: Rockets built by the ages
Space feeds your factories
pages.text:
The §lultimate tier goes through space§r:
• §6Lunar alloy§r (industrial crucible (vacuum)): 2 titanium aluminide + 1 lunarium → 2 ingots; ultimate frame and kit, ultimate item, energy and pressure cables.
• §6Tharsium magnet§r (Mars): ultimate electric motors.
• §6Venusium liner§r: ultimate centrifugal pumps and MKIV logistic cables.
• §6Mercurium heat spreader§r: ultimate heat exchangers and MKIV logistic cables.
• §6Platinum-group concentrate§r (Vesta, Pallas, Hygiea, Ceres dust): osmiridium and platinum through aqua regia.
• §6Valhallite shielding§r (Callisto): nuclear propulsion.
And already: lunar helium-3 (Generation II fusion), Ganymede sulcite (heliotron), Uranus and Neptune materials (Generation III fission).

pages.title: Four stations
pages.text:
Assembly is split across four stations, each with its own recipes:
• §6Rocket integration hall§r (9×15×9 multiblock): T1 to T13 rockets and the orbital station kit.
• §6Module assembly table§r: rocket modules.
• §6Robotic assembly bay§r (7×6×9 multiblock): every robotic unit, MKI to MKIV.
• §6Equipment assembly table§r: life support unit and space suits.

Pick the recipe with the arrows. The grid shows the shape to fill (ghost items), the required blueprint and research. "Build" starts the job, "Repeat" keeps building copies while ingredients arrive.

Both multiblocks are built around their §lcontroller§r (Shift + right-click empty-handed: projected blueprint), in industrial casings, frames, sheet metal and glass (the weakest gives the tier and color). The bay needs a §6charge pad§r in the middle of the floor: four articulated arms build the unit there from the parts the conveyor brings in. The hall needs 3×3 §6launch pad§r plates in the middle of the floor: the rocket is assembled standing up, bottom to top, beside the service tower, under two overhead cranes. While the structure is incomplete, the screen tells which block to fix.

pages.title: Automation and recipes
pages.text:
One-block tables accept energy and items through their (configurable) sides. Both multiblocks use §6industrial ports§r placed in the floor, plinth or sheets: energy port, item port set to input (each part goes to its grid slot), item port set to output (the finished product is pushed to neighbors; wrench: switch direction). Grid slots only accept the expected ingredient and never give anything back to automation.

Recipes are §bpioneers:assembly§r JSON files: station, pattern (5 rows of 10), keys, result, energy, duration, optional blueprint and research. Add or change them with datapacks or KubeJS.

pages.title: Thirteen tiers
Modules
pages.text:
A rocket has §l3 to 9 module slots§r depending on its tier (shown in its tooltip). §6Sneak + right-click§r the placed rocket to open its menu: install modules and see its cargo.

• §6Crew cabin§r: required to board (without it, you cannot get in).
• §6Probe§r: probe missions to a world.
• §6Cargo bays§r for items, fluids, gas, data: each bay module enlarges the matching storage of the rocket.
• §6Efficiency§r, §6Speed§r, §6Shield§r: less fuel, shorter flights, protection.

A module can only be removed if the bay it carries is empty. A rocket broken and placed again keeps its modules and cargo.

pages.title: Building the complex
pages.text:
A disc of plates around the §lcore§r, and a tower standing on the edge, in the middle of one side:
• §6MKI§r (small): 5×5 disc, 5-block tower — T1 to T3 rockets, 100 mB/t fueling.
• §6MKII§r (medium): 7×7, 9-block tower — T4 to T7, 250 mB/t.
• §6MKIII§r (large): 9×9, 13-block tower — T8 to T10, 500 mB/t.
• §6MKIV§r (heavy): 11×11, 17-block tower — T11 to T13, 1,000 mB/t.

Once formed, the complex takes the §lcolor of its tier§r, the one of cables and buffers (green, blue, red, burgundy): plate joints, disc frame and tower collars. The disc is rounded. A tower that is too short downgrades the complex. §6Launch ports§r can replace any plate. Each one is specialized with the wrench (sneak + right-click): items, fluid, gas or data, as input or output. They give access to the rocket's propellant and hold.

pages.title: Missions
pages.text:
The pad only §lplans§r missions: the rocket keeps its own modules. Fill the tank with a §lpropellant suited§r to the rocket's tier (kerolox, hydrolox, liquid hydrogen or fusion propellant: the pad refuses the others), place the rocket on the core, pick a mission:
• §6Manned§r: board, press Space to lift off, pick the destination on the map.
• §6Probe§r: the rocket flies alone to the chosen world; its data reaches the antenna.
• §6Logistics§r: automatic shuttle to another station of the cargo network (departure rule: ASAP, half, full, timer, redstone).
• §6Receive§r: welcomes shuttles from other stations.

Loading goes through the dock: the rocket takes whatever fits in its bays.

pages.title: Travel
pages.text:
Once aboard, press §lSpace§r: countdown, ascent, then the §6system map§r opens in orbit. Pick the world, "Depart": the transit begins, and you end up at the controls of the descent capsule.

The whole sequence (transit, piloted descent, parachute, autopilot, landing) is explained in the §6Space travel§r pages that follow.

The map key (M by default) also opens it on the ground, for browsing.

pages.title: Lift-off
pages.text:
Aboard a fueled rocket standing on its pad, press §lSpace§r.

1. §6Countdown§r: 10 seconds, shown on screen; the engines light up during the last 3.
2. §6Ascent§r: 14 seconds. The camera shakes, the sky turns deep blue then black, and stars come out. Halfway up, the §lfirst stage detaches§r and falls back; the upper stage goes on alone (except the single-stage T1 rocket).
3. §6Orbit§r: the map opens and stays open until you pick a destination. Escape opens the pause menu; the map comes back afterward.

The §6Abort mission§r button (bottom left, two clicks to confirm) brings you back down by capsule above the launch pad.

pages.title: Transit
pages.text:
The §6transit§r screen shows the trip: a scrolling starfield, the departure world shrinking away, the destination growing, an info bar (destination, distance, progress) and flight tips.

• Within one system: 6 to 21 seconds depending on the distance between orbits.
• To another star: 28 seconds, with a §lwarp jump§r (flash, stretched stars).

When the transit ends, you are in the capsule, above your landing point.

pages.title: Piloted descent
pages.text:
The capsule arrives about 230 blocks above the ground and falls according to the world's §lgravity§r; the atmosphere slows it more or less (thick on Venus, Titan, the giants; thin on Mars; none on the Moon).

§6Controls§r (rebindable in Controls):
• §lSpace§r: retro-rockets (they burn the capsule's fuel).
• §lW A S D§r: side thrusters, in the direction you look.
• §lB§r: parachute. Only with an atmosphere; it tears above about 27 m/s.
• §lV§r: autopilot (on or off).

The dashboard shows altitude, vertical and horizontal speed, fuel and parachute state. You cannot leave the capsule before touchdown.

pages.title: Landing
Oxygen and gravity
pages.text:
Away from Earth the air is not breathable. Without a full suit (helmet included) and an oxygen reserve, you suffocate. The O₂ indicator (above the air bar) shows your reserve and the environment.

Each world has its own §6gravity§r: Moon and Mars are light, asteroids almost weightless (you jump very high and fall slowly). Values come from the §bpioneers/environments§r files: gravity, atmosphere, required suit, hazard, nitrogen, temperature.

pages.title: Space suits
pages.text:
Four suits, assembled at the equipment assembly table, each one from the previous:
• §6Space suit§r (research "Space suit"): vacuum. The Moon.
• §6Thermal suit§r (unlocked by studying lunar geology): extreme cold and heat. Mars, Phobos, Deimos.
• §6Acid-proof suit§r (unlocked by Martian geology): Venus, Mercury and the whole outer system.
• §6Atmospheric suit§r (research "Atmospheric suit"): crushing pressures. Gas giants and Toliman b; it lets you §lfly§r in the clouds.

The chestplate holds the oxygen reserve (12,000, 18,000, 24,000, 36,000 mB): 20 mB/s. A suit too weak for the world slowly hurts you.

pages.title: Pressurized bases
pages.text:
§6Oxygen diffuser§r: fills the closed room it stands in with oxygen, 2 mB per block, up to §l1,024 blocks at MKI§r, 2,048 at MKII, 4,096 at MKIII and 8,192 at MKIV (flow doubled at each tier). In a pressurized room you breathe without a helmet and your suit's reserve refills.

A room is sealed only if it is enclosed by full blocks. A regular door leaks: use the §6airlock door§r, which closes by itself. When open it depressurizes the room: build an §lairlock§r (two airlock doors with a small chamber between them).

pages.title: Oxygen and nitrogen for a base
pages.text:
A base's §loxygen§r comes from ordinary machines: the §6electrolysis cell§r splits water into oxygen and hydrogen (hydrogen is a propellant), anywhere, even without an atmosphere.

Where the world has a nitrogen atmosphere (Earth, Titan...), the §6industrial gas separator (air separation)§r extracts §lnitrogen§r and oxygen from it; without an atmosphere it has no recipe.

pages.title: Small space machines
Restless skies
pages.text:
When players are around, a world may go through a few-minute §6event§r. A chime and a banner announce it.
• §6Meteor shower§r (worlds without a thick atmosphere, Mars): burning meteors crash around you and dig a §lcrater§r; about one in three stays buried at the bottom: a §lmeteorite§r to dig out.
• §6Dust storm§r (Mars): ochre fog, you can barely see.
• §6Aurora§r (Earth, Ganymede, Titan, Toliman b, Proxima b, TRAPPIST-1e and f): curtains of light in the sky. Under the open sky they bring §lluck§r: +1 while they last (better loot).
• §6Superstorm§r (gas giants): lightning everywhere, and rich pockets become three times as common.

Dangerous events follow the §6local difficulty§r, like monsters: rare on peaceful or in freshly explored areas, more frequent on hard and where you have lived for a long time.

pages.title: Solar flares
pages.text:
A §6flare§r hits a whole star system at once (the sky turns golden). Out in the open, its radiation hurts, the more so the closer the world is to the star.

On a world with an atmosphere, it also sets §lfire§r to flammable blocks under the open sky.

Protection: stay under a roof, in a pressurized room or under a force field; a suit reduces the dose (acid-proof or better: almost nothing). The "Flare shielding" research halves it. On Earth the magnetosphere protects you: just aurorae.

Flares have an upside: a §6solar absorber§r orbiting the star produces up to §lthree times as much§r while it lasts (and heats up as much).

For admins: §b/pioneers event start <type> [seconds]§r and §b/pioneers event stop§r.

pages.title: Force field
pages.text:
The §6force field generator§r (tharsium, elite circuits) projects a §lbubble§r from 4 blocks in radius up to its maximum (− / + buttons): 16 at MKI, 24 at MKII, 36 at MKIII, 48 at MKIV.

• It §lshatters meteors§r entering it: each impact costs a large energy spike (400,000 FE by default, depending on the meteor's size). If the buffer is not enough, the field §lcollapses§r for 10 seconds and lets the meteor through.
• It shields what it covers from flare §lradiation§r and §lfires§r.
• Constant upkeep depending on the radius (radius 16: 2,048 FE/t), doubled during a flare. Can be switched off by redstone if configured so.

Keep an energy buffer next to it: impacts are what drain the generator.

pages.title: Lightning rod
pages.text:
A §6lightning rod§r harvests the energy of lightning. Place a §llightning collector§r, stack §l4 to 24 conductors§r on it, and top the mast with a copper §llightning rod§r (pointing up), under open sky.

• During a §lthunderstorm§r, lightning strikes the tip and charges the collector. The taller the mast, the more often and harder it strikes.
• On a §lgas giant§r, lightning falls even in calm weather, and during a §lsuperstorm§r it pours, each strike stronger: that is where the rod pays off most.
• Energy comes out of the collector's sides and bottom. The collector's §ltier§r caps the useful mast (8, 12, 18 then 24 conductors from MKI to MKIV) and the output (250 k, 500 k, 1 M, 2 M FE/t).

The interface shows the mast height, the weather, the energy per strike and the average output.

pages.title: One station per world
pages.text:
After the "Orbital stations" research you may set up a station around every world. It brings nothing but itself: a very expensive prestige project.

1. Assemble an §6orbital station kit§r (rocket integration hall).
2. Carry it in your inventory or in the hold of a crewed rocket.
3. In orbit, on the map, select the world and choose §l"Orbital station"§r.

Every world can host one except the asteroid belt; around a §lstar§r (Sun at T11, Alpha Centauri, Proxima, TRAPPIST-1), the "Stellar absorption" research is required.

The station deploys: round deck, small launch pad (full tank for the way back), airlock and habitat module with an oxygen diffuser. Afterwards, the same button takes you back there.

pages.title: Building
pages.text:
A real greenhouse: a §lround base§r of industrial casings, §6hydroponic substrate trays§r set in the floor in rows (the aisles stay casing for the robot), a §lcharging pad§r in the middle and an §lindustrial glass dome§r held by 4 ribs of §6structure frames§r. The controller sits in the edge of the base. Shift + right-click the controller empty-handed: the blueprint, in §l4 sizes§r (9 to 15 across).
