The §ltier§r is that of the weakest part (casings, frames): MKI ×1, MKII ×1.5, MKIII ×2, MKIV ×3 growth. A §6robotic turtle§r (placed in the controller; the higher its tier, the faster it works) plants, tends and harvests every tray. Greenhouse ports, set in the base (input / output mode with the wrench), relay energy and items.

pages.title: Space seeds
pages.text:
Space plant seeds carry the same §6genes§r as Earth seeds, rated 1 to 10 (stars after the name, gauges in the tooltip):
• §lGrowth§r: speed in the greenhouse (5 = the usual speed). §lYield§r: harvest (5 = 1.7 on average).
• §lFertility§r: seeds returned at harvest, which §lmutate§r as on Earth. Wild seeds (plants broken on the surface) have weak genes.
• §lResistance§r: temperature margin around the §lhome world's climate§r (±2 °C to ±11 °C). On its home world the plant grows best; on another world whose mean temperature is within the margin, it grows at less than half speed; elsewhere, nothing.

pages.title: Rover garage
pages.text:
A real §lgarage§r: a slab of industrial casings, posts and beams of §6structure frames§r, cladding and roof of §6structure sheet metal§r, §lone door and one dock per bay§r, and a frame mast carrying the §6prospecting radar§r on the roof. The controller is on the left gable; mining ports replace any sheet or casing. Shift + right-click the controller empty-handed: the blueprint, from §l1 to 4 bays§r.

Each bay holds one rover: put several (same model) in the controller and they leave §las a convoy§r and drill side by side (cargo, battery and drilling multiplied). The garage §ltier§r (weakest part) speeds up drilling: MKI ×1 to MKIV ×2. The radar finds deposits of the 17 exotic metals; pick one on the GUI map.

pages.title: The rover
pages.text:
A §6robotic rover§r placed in the controller becomes the mining rover: it gets its drill arm, leaves its dock, digs its way to the deposit and brings the ore back. Its §ltier§r sets battery, cargo, speed and drilling (MKIV: far more efficient). Deposits are §lvirtual§r: the rover doesn't damage the terrain. Fit it with a drill head suited to the metal and with modules (battery, cargo, scanner, overclock, refinery).

Give it a §lname§r in the GUI field: it is shown above it. Mining ports (input / output with the wrench) take the ore out and bring energy and parts.

pages.title: Interplanetary logistics
pages.text:
Every named launch complex becomes a §6station§r of the network. On a §lLogistics§r mission an unmanned rocket shuttles to the target station: it loads at the dock, flies, lands, is unloaded and comes back. The arrival station must run a §lReceive§r mission.

The map's "Logistics" window (L key) shows the flights in progress. A §6space chunk loader§r keeps your bases loaded while you are away (radius 1 chunk at MKI up to 4 at MKIV); its "Preview" button draws the loaded area in the world.

pages.title: Inner system
pages.text:
• §6Moon§r (T1): vacuum, -20 °C, gravity 0.17. Lunarium, ice in polar craters. Space suit.
• §6Mars§r (T2): cold, -63 °C, gravity 0.38, a little nitrogen. Marsium, tharsium, hematite, dry ice. Thermal suit.
• §6Phobos, Deimos§r (T2): tiny moons, almost weightless. Thermal suit.
• §6Venus§r (T3): acid, 464 °C. Venusium, sulfur. Acid-proof suit.
• §6Mercury§r (T4): heat, 167 °C. Mercurium, polar ice. Acid-proof suit.

pages.title: Outer system
pages.text:
All of them require the acid-proof suit.
• §6Belt§r (T5): Ceres, Vesta, Pallas, Hygiea.
• §6Jupiter§r (T6): Io (radiation, lava), Europa (ocean under the ice), Ganymede, Callisto.
• §6Saturn§r (T7): Enceladus (geysers), Titan (hydrocarbon lakes, rich in nitrogen).
• §6Uranus§r (T8): Miranda, Titania.
• §6Neptune§r (T9): Triton.
• §6Pluto, Charon§r (T10).
Gas giants (T11) have no surface: you descend to the aerostats (“Gas giants” pages, right after). The Sun can be visited from a station (“Endgame” chapter).

pages.title: Into the clouds
Flying and settling
pages.text:
Inside a giant, the atmospheric suit §6glides§r: you sink slowly and take no fall damage. §lJump§r fires the back thrusters (climb), §lSneak§r dives, movement keys steer.

The §6aerostat kit§r (research "Aerostats") deploys a 9×9 platform under your feet: 3×3 landing pad in the middle, railings, glowing buoyancy cells and a keel. It only deploys in clouds or open air. Every aerostat becomes an arrival point for capsules.

This is where you build your base: drone bay, tanks, and a pressurized room if you want to take the helmet off.

pages.title: Gas pockets
Drone bay
pages.text:
The bay is §lbuilt§r on the aerostat: a casing deck edged with frames, one §6landing pad§r (2×2 tiles) and one sheet-metal tank per drone, and a glazed cabin (frames, sheets, glass) holding the controller with a radar on its roof. Shift + right-click the controller empty-handed: the blueprint, from 1 to 4 pads. The §ltier§r (weakest part) cuts flight costs: MKI ×1 to MKIV ×0.35.

The §6drone bay§r (research "Gas harvesting") launches up to §l4 robotic drones§r at once (one pad per drone; the higher their tier, the faster they fly, the harder they pull and the more they carry) toward pockets within 80 blocks. Each trip brings back 1,000 mB of gas or 4 crystals. Energy: 5 kFE per launch, 15 FE/t per drone in flight.

• §6Mode§r: Auto (marked first, then rich, then close) or Marked (only those tagged with the scanner).
• §6Filter§r: one button per content, to skip what you do not need.
• §6Recall§r: every drone comes home.
• 4 gas tanks of 64,000 mB (output set in the sides panel), 2 crystal slots. The radar shows drones and pockets.

Unarmored drones avoid storms; one that ventures there is struck by lightning. §6Drone armor plating§r ("Storm drones", one per drone) opens the storm layer and carries 1,500 mB or 6 crystals.

pages.title: What to do with the harvest?
pages.text:
• §6Helium-3§r: with deuterium and liquid helium, the §lfusion propellant§r of T11-T13 rockets (propellant plant); it also feeds the Generation II fusion reactor and the quantum computer.
• §6Methane§r: a fuel, for the gas turbine (compact or multiblock) and the boiler.
• §6Ammonia§r: a §lcoolant§r; it cools the solar absorber and comes out hot.
• §6Metallic hydrogen§r: T12 and T13 rocket parts, singularity cell.
• §6Rain diamonds§r: in the crystallizer, the §lrain diamond lattice§r of the Generation III fission reactor.

The §6singularity cell§r (Gravity Compressor: metallic hydrogen, 100 mB of Void Singularity, 2,000 mB of solar plasma, 1 GFE) is the key to T13 rockets and to the rift projectors of the Space Simulator.

pages.title: The galaxy map
pages.text:
On the map, the §lG§r key (or the "Galaxy" button) switches to the §6galactic view§r: our system, §6Alpha Centauri§r (4.37 light-years, T12 rocket) and §6TRAPPIST-1§r (40 light-years, T13 rocket). Click a system to open it; G or right-click to go back.

A system only shows up once §lsurveyed§r by research ("Alpha Centauri survey", "TRAPPIST-1 survey"). Getting there takes "Interstellar propulsion" (T12) and "Void drive" (T13).

Each exoplanet follows the same mastery as the solar system worlds: orbit, surface, geology, biology. An §lMKIV§r (heavy) launch complex is needed.

pages.title: Alpha Centauri
pages.text:
Two golden suns (Rigil Kentaurus and Toliman) and a red dwarf, Proxima. §6T12§r rocket.
• §6Toliman b§r: green super-Earth, gravity 1.25, 38 °C, crushing pressure: §latmospheric suit§r. Lowlands, bloom-stone forests, shallows under two suns. Tolimanite, Toliman twinleaf.
• §6Proxima b§r: tidally locked; one side scorched, one side frozen, and the §ltwilight band§r in between. -12 °C, radiation: acid-proof suit. Terminite, twilight lily. Aurorae.
• §6Proxima d§r: small scorching world (360 °C, gravity 0.45), molten seas and flare fields. Flarium crystals, flare thorn.

Proxima is a §lflare§r star: see the “Survival in space” chapter.

pages.title: TRAPPIST-1
pages.text:
A red dwarf and seven tightly packed planets; four can be visited with a §6T13§r rocket. The sun stays still in the sky there.
• §6TRAPPIST-1b§r: volcanic hell, 400 °C. Lava rivers, glassy plains. Pyrrhite, cinder cactus.
• §6TRAPPIST-1d§r: ocean planet, 12 °C, thermal suit. Archipelagos and tidal flats. Thalassite, tide kelp.
• §6TRAPPIST-1e§r: the friendliest, -3 °C, a plain space suit is enough. Glowcap forests, violet meadows, crimson lakes. Edenite, Eden berry bush.
• §6TRAPPIST-1f§r: ice world, -62 °C. Ice sheet, frozen sea, cryovolcanoes. Borealite, frost bell.

pages.title: Exotic resources
pages.text:
The seven new materials are processed like the others (raw ore, dust, ingot) and each one has its use:
• §6Tolimanite§r, §6terminite§r, §6flarium§r: tanks, nose cones, wings and boosters of the §lT13§r rocket. So you must mine Alpha Centauri to reach TRAPPIST-1.
• §6Pyrrhite§r, §6thalassite§r: rift projector of the Space Simulator.
• All four TRAPPIST-1 minerals go into the plating of §6Singularity§r gear.

Each exoplanet's veins count for geology, its plants (in a greenhouse, on site) for biology, as in the solar system.

§6Building§r: every rock and ice of every world now has its variants, at the stonecutter: rocks as cobbled, polished, smooth, bricks, cracked and chiseled bricks; ices as packed, polished, bricks and chiseled; with stairs, slabs and walls.

pages.title: Space Stabilizer
pages.text:
An 11×11×11 globe holding a captive star. What it stabilizes depends on the §6core§r placed at the exact center of the globe.

§6Building§r: casing around the edge of each face, glass or ports elsewhere. In the middle of all 6 faces (sides, top and bottom): a power port with a field emitter right behind it, inside. The rest of the inside stays empty. The §6controller§r goes §lat the bottom center of a side face§r: it checks the structure (lit = valid); its interface has a §lcore slot§r: it places the core in the chamber itself (and replaces a spent one). "Open Chamber" button: the stabilizer interface.

pages.title: The two cores
pages.text:
• §6Singularity Core§r: a black hole turns §lwater§r (placeholder until balancing) into §6Void Singularity§r: 500 mB for 1 mB, 1 mB/t per rate point (1 to 100), 250 kFE/t of field per point.
• §6Stellar Core§r: a star burns §llava§r into §6solar plasma§r: 500 mB for 1 mB, 10 mB/t per point, 150 kFE/t per point.

Ports are set with a wrench: input (water or lava) or output (the product flows out to neighboring pipes on its own).

pages.title: Ignition and operation
pages.text:
1. With the 6 emitters powered and fuel, the shared reserve of the §lpower ports§r (200 MFE each, 6 required, as many more as you like in the wall) must hold §61 GFE§r.
2. All-or-nothing ignition: the GFE is taken at once, the §6core is consumed§r and the star is born in its place; the ignition sequence lasts 10 s.
3. Stable: every tick, fuel is consumed and product made. Full output: the star stays lit (the field still draws power) and production resumes as soon as there is room.

An emitter running dry, a SCRAM, fuel running out or a broken block: §6collapse§r. To re-ignite: a new core in the controller (another core switches the regime).

pages.title: Gravity Compressor
pages.text:
A §lmultiblock§r: a 9-block sphere of industrial casings, its §6graviton coils§r built in, with the controller in the shell (Shift + right-click shows the plan). Inside, six pylons aimed at a pulsing core, three spinning gyroscopic rings and matter drawn in on a spiral. Recipes at tier §lMKIV§r (MKIII for the Stellar Core), with a §ltotal energy§r cost: the reserve holds 4 GFE.

• §6Stellar Core§r: 100,000 mB each of plutonium, deuterium and tritium, 100 MFE.
• §6Singularity core§r: one Stellar Core + 100,000 mB of solar plasma, 400 MFE: the first black hole.
• §6Singularity cell§r: metallic hydrogen + Void Singularity + solar plasma, 1 GFE.
• §6Compacted planetary matter§r: 64 of the planet's rocks + a block of its metal (or a giant's gases, ice and core), 200 MFE: the first step of a simulated planet (see the “Endgame” chapter).

pages.title: A planet in four steps
pages.text:
A simulated planet (the eight planets only) is made in §lfour steps§r, with two multiblocks:
1. §6Compact§r (Gravity Compressor): 64 of the planet's rocks + a block of its metal (Earth: stones and iron; giants: their gases, ice and core) → §lcompacted planetary matter§r, 200 MFE.
2. §6Enrich with data§r (Synthesizer): the matter + millions of MB of surveys → an §lempty miniature planet§r. Mars: 4 M Martian + 1 M sidereal, 50 MFE; Jupiter: 6 M Jovian + 2 M sidereal, 100 MFE.
3. §6Add the atmosphere§r (Synthesizer): three gases in the proportions of the real one → a §lprotoplanet§r. Earth: 7,800 nitrogen, 2,100 oxygen, 100 argon; Mars: 9,500 CO₂, 300 nitrogen, 200 argon; Jupiter: 9,000 hydrogen, 1,000 helium, 100 ammonia. 20 MFE.
4. §6Convert§r (Synthesizer): the protoplanet + 4,000 mB of solar plasma → a §lsimulated planet§r, 500 MFE (1 GFE for a giant).

pages.title: Synthesizer
pages.text:
The §6Synthesizer§r is a §lmultiblock§r: a 7-block dome of industrial casings, its §6synthesis matrices§r built in, with the controller in the wall. Inside, a clawed cradle, a ring of six projectors and a ceiling projector shape a miniature planet spinning in its atmosphere, under data packets and three satellites.

§lData§r comes in through a §6data port§r (or an MKI-or-better logistic cable plugged into the structure): three 64 M MB tanks, one type each; gases through the gas ports. Recipes at tier §lMKIV§r, with a total energy cost (4 GFE reserve). Research "Planet synthesis". Plan for ultimate banks.

pages.title: Space Simulator
pages.text:
The ultimate multiblock, which looks like a planet: a §lperfectly round globe 25 blocks§r across, girdled by a ring like Saturn.

§6Building§r: the shell (the outer layer of the globe) in casing, glass or ports; a §6space rift projector§r at the center of §leach of the six faces§r; hollow inside; the §6controller§r in the shell, §lat the bottom center of a side face§r (8 blocks below the center), front facing out. §6Ribs§r: the equator and both face meridians in casing (reinforced sphere); glass anywhere else to see inside. At the equator, a §6ring of supreme space coils§r (radius 16 to 17) linked to the globe by §lfour spokes§r of coils, at the center of the side faces. Shift + right-click on the controller shows it all.

§6Mode§r: chosen at the controller (Sol. / Gal. buttons), no core is needed: solar mode simulates a §lsolar system§r, galaxy mode a §lgalaxy§r (Big Bang: “Simulated galaxies” pages, at the end of this chapter).
Solar system §6ignition§r: §l50 GFE§r and §l4,000 mB§r of solar plasma; §6upkeep§r: §l40 MFE/t§r and §l1 mB/t§r. If anything runs short, the simulation collapses.

While running, a §6torrent of energy§r engulfs the coils: it §lkills instantly§r, whatever the armor. Research "Solar simulation".

pages.title: Output
A power plant around a star
pages.text:
The §6solar absorber§r (research "Stellar absorption") only works §lin orbit of a star§r: set up a station around the Sun (T11 rocket), Alpha Centauri A or B, Proxima or TRAPPIST-1, and build it on its deck.

§6Building§r: a hollow box from 5×3×5 to 13×5×13. Edges in §lcasing§r; the whole top face (except edges) in §lcollectors§r, and collectors nowhere else; casing or §lports§r on the sides and bottom; a §lcontroller§r in a side wall (not on an edge), facing outward: it checks the structure and opens the interface. Nothing may hide the sky above.

Shift + right-click on the controller shows the three sizes.

pages.title: Output and heat
pages.text:
Each collector makes §62 MFE/t§r around the Sun (242 MFE/t for the largest absorber, 121 collectors), times the star's luminosity: Alpha Centauri A ×1.5, B ×0.5, Proxima ×0.15, TRAPPIST-1 ×0.05. A flare multiplies everything by up to 3. Energy comes out of every port.

All this light §lheats§r. The coolant (§lammonia§r from the giants) goes in through a port set to input (wrench) and comes out §lsuperheated§r through an output port. Without coolant the temperature rises; at 1,600 °C the §6emergency shutters§r close until it drops below 600 °C.

The "Shutters" button in the GUI closes the absorber by hand.

pages.title: Galaxy mode
pages.text:
The top of the progression (research "Universe simulation"): give birth to a whole galaxy in the §6Space Simulator§r (building: see the planetary simulation chapter).

Choose §lgalaxy mode§r at the controller (Gal. button), then the galaxy with the arrows in the GUI. No core is needed: the §lVoid Singularity Cell§r goes into the rift projectors.

Ports bring in energy and solar plasma, and take out the products.

pages.title: Big Bang
pages.text:
The §6Big Bang§r button starts the simulation. It consumes:
• §l250 GFE§r of stored energy (capacity 1 TFE);
• §l16,000 mB§r of solar plasma (128,000 mB tank).

Then the chosen galaxy draws its energy and plasma every tick. If either runs short, the simulation §6collapses§r: a new Big Bang is needed. Switching galaxy resets the current cycle, without collapse.

pages.title: Galaxies
pages.text:
• §6Spiral§r: 30 s, 60 MFE/t, 2 mB/t of plasma. 8 stardust; 15%: dark matter.
• §6Elliptical§r: 45 s, 80 MFE/t, 3 mB/t. 4 stardust, 1 neutronium ingot; 20%: one more neutronium.
• §6Irregular§r: 60 s, 80 MFE/t, 3 mB/t. 6 stardust, 1 dark matter; 35%: 6 more stardust.
• §6Quasar§r: 2 min, 150 MFE/t, 6 mB/t. 1 quasar crystal, 2 dark matter, 2 neutronium; 10%: one more crystal.

§6Uses§r: stardust, neutronium and dark matter blocks; §lquasar lamp§r (decorative light); §lneutronium drill head§r, the fastest drill head for mining rovers. JEI details every galaxy.

pages.title: Four kinds of units
pages.text:
Robotic units run the base, §lwithout teleportation or wireless§r: they actually go, carry and deliver. You don't configure them one by one: you put §6logistic points§r on chests and machines, draw §6areas§r and give §6orders§r from the §6logistic map§r (§lO§r key) — the base then runs itself, as in Factorio.
• §6Drone§r: the fastest, flies over everything, but carries little and works slowly. Perfect for small deliveries.
• §6Robot§r: the worker. It harvests, fells, mines and digs §lthree times faster§r than the others.
• §6Rover§r: slow, but a §lcolossal cargo bay§r (54 stacks, 512,000 mB): bulk transport.
• §6Turtle§r: slow, but §lvery energy-efficient§r, quick at work and roomy; the only one able to §lsleep on its area§r (rest mode): ideal for fields and herds.

They are all built at the §6robotic assembly bay§r, from the lunar research §lRobotics§r: one blueprint per kind, only the materials change from one tier to the next (lunarium, venusium, krakenite, sputnikite, and the tier's §lelectric motor§r). Their parts (arms, wheels, cores, chassis, rover parts) are built at the §6assembly bench§r with industrial components: motors, pistons, bearings, planetary gearsets, oscillators, relays.

pages.title: The robotic hub
pages.text:
Units live in a §6hub§r: a compact multiblock, a §l3 × 3 × 3 cube§r.
• The eight corners are §6robotic casings§r;
• the rest is casings, §6glass§r (plain or structural), §6ports§r (energy, and pipe access to the buffer) and at least one §6bay door§r, on a side (or in the middle of the roof, for drones).
In its interface, you pick the §lkind of units housed§r: drones, robots, rovers or turtles (empty hub). Docked units spin in the cradle, under the dome.

A hub houses §l5 units§r, plus 5 per §6bay extension module§r (3 at most: 20 units), recharges the docked ones and takes §l4 upgrades§r. Its range depends on the best tier inside: it is the start of the §6logistic network§r.

pages.title: The logistic network
pages.text:
A §6network§r is the area covered by hubs and §6robotic relays§r that touch: every point, stock and unit inside works together.
• A §6relay§r covers §l24 blocks§r around it (more with the range upgrade) and draws a little energy.
• Each unit has a §lbattery§r: it drains on the way and at work. Below 20%, the unit goes to recharge at the nearest relay (or hub) — §la few seconds§r are enough — then resumes its mission.
• A unit with nothing to do goes back into its hub (it comes out as soon as there is work): relays are never waiting spots.
• §lProvider → requester: nothing more to do§r. The network delivers on its own, with the best-suited unit (real throughput: a drone for a small parcel, a rover for a big volume). A delivery waiting too long for a free unit is reported (alert).
• §6Dedicated lines§r are only for needs markers don't cover (machine → machine, reserved shuttle); a blocked line never stops the network from delivering.
• An area §lnever gets more units than requested§r: the unit already there chains the sub-tasks. Supplies (food, saplings, materials) come from the §lnearest provider§r, then from storage.
• The §6robotic road§r (joins, turns, crossings) makes ground units drive §l50% faster§r (rovers: 80%), and they §lprefer§r it for their trips.

pages.title: Logistic points
Who carries what?
The logistic map
Dedicated lines
The 3D planner
pages.text:
Areas and works are set in §lfree view§r, on the real world: a detached camera (WASD, space and Shift to fly, right-click to look, wheel to move forward, Ctrl + wheel: speed). Open it from the map (Area and Works tools), with the §6zone planner§r (right-click in the air) or by editing an area.
• §lSelection§r (V): drag on the terrain, or §lclick two opposite corners§r; heights follow the terrain and the task.
• Then §lstretch each face§r with the colored handles; the yellow handle moves everything (Shift: vertically). Bounds can also be fine-tuned block by block in the panel.
• A §lname§r of your choice for the area (shown on the map and in the orders).
• §lTop§r (T), §lFrame§r (F), Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Y, Enter saves, Esc cancels.
• §lCtrl + C / Ctrl + V§r: copy an area and place copies with a click; click another area's name to switch to it.
On the right: the task (keys 1 to 6), its settings, §lwhat the area contains§r (ripe crops, trees, hives, animals… highlighted) and the units.

pages.title: Work areas
Works
pages.text:
The §6works planner§r (map: Works tool) builds a job §lstep by step§r, and the §lpreview§r shows the result each time: red for what gets removed, ghosts for what will be placed (H: hide).
• §lClear§r (Delete): everything in the selection is removed.
• §lRoad§r (R): click the §lstart§r then the §lend§r (right-click a point: remove it), and fine-tune their coordinates in the panel (rise and slope shown). The §lgentlest route§r is computed — max slope of your choice (1/1 to 1/4), minimal earthwork, §lwide curves§r with no knots, and §lswitchbacks§r when the height to gain is too much for the distance — then shown as ghosts before you confirm. Surface of your choice (§6robotic road§r, path, gravel, stone… or any block), width 1 or 3, clearance above, and a §lFill§r option: the space below filled down to the terrain with the block you want.
• §lCopy / paste§r (Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V): the selection as it will be after the planned steps — a farm, a building… X to rotate; the §lreal blocks§r show as ghosts before placing. The copy can be §ledited§r: eraser (E: click or drag over ghost blocks, Shift: a whole type), remove or replace a material, trim, no air, no settings or areas (Ctrl + Z undoes).
• §lBlueprints§r (B): a copy can be saved to the §6blueprint library§r, shared by all your worlds (thumbnail, name, materials); pick a blueprint there to paste it, rename, duplicate, update or delete it. The files can be shared (pioneers/plans folder). Units can turn dirt into §lpath or farmland§r: dirt in the network is all they need.
Example: clear some land, draw a road on it, paste a farm: the final preview shows, you start it. Units then do everything §lin the right order§r: removals top to bottom, then placements bottom to top, with §lmaterials taken from the network§r (the list is in the panel). The order disappears once the job is done.

pages.title: Upgrades
Movement
Tiers and energy
pages.text:
Four §6tiers§r, each made from the metal of a farther world: §lMKI§r lunarium (Moon), §lMKII§r venusium (Venus), §lMKIII§r krakenite (Titan, Saturn), §lMKIV§r sputnikite (Pluto). Each tier is built directly, with its metal, a circuit and the electric motor of the same tier (Electric Motor MKI … MKIV).

A higher tier moves faster, carries more, works better and extends the hub's range, but its battery drains §lmuch faster§r. Hubs and relays pay for every recharge; the more units around one hub, the higher the cost.

pages.title: Farm and kitchen
pages.text:
§6Agriculture 2.0§r replaces Minecraft farming: §l51 crops§r with genetic seeds, §l12 fruit trees§r, animated §lkitchen stations§r (no interface: everything is done by clicking the station), §l25 breeds§r of male and female animals, §l54 fish§r and §6tension fishing§r.

Minecraft's seeds and dishes are no longer used: your vanilla seeds become the mod's, bread, soups and cooked meats become the mod's dishes. Vanilla harvests (wheat, carrot, potato…) stay the same items.

Look at a crop, a station or an animal: a §lcard§r appears next to the crosshair; sneaking shows more (genes, food, water…).

pages.title: Seeds and genetics
pages.text:
Each seed carries four §6genes§r rated 1 to 10: §lyield§r (bigger harvest), §lgrowth§r (grows faster), §lresistance§r (copes with a less suitable climate), §lfertility§r (more seeds, and more often favourable mutations).
You do not cross seeds: at each harvest, the returned seeds §lmutate§r a little, rather upwards when fertility is good. Keep the best (the §lstars§r in the name sum up the genes) and replant them: generation after generation, the line improves.
Wild seeds come from §lgrass§r: each biome gives crops of its climate, with weak genes. Farmer robots always replant the best harvested seed.

pages.title: Climate and greenhouses
pages.text:
Each crop has a climate: the biome §ltemperature§r (colder at altitude) and its §lhumidity§r (irrigated soil counts as wetter).
• §lIdeal§r: full speed. §lTolerable§r: less than half. §lHostile§r: the plant ends up §lwithering§r (resistance delays it).
• A §6greenhouse§r: a closed room of greenhouse blocks with a regulator (page “Building a greenhouse”). Inside, everything grows as in an ideal climate, in every season. On other worlds, where nothing grows in the open, a glass block (greenhouse glass tag) above the crop, up to 12 blocks higher, still does.
• §6Rice§r is a paddy crop: its soil needs water all around.
The look card gives the climate of the targeted crop, and the seed tells it in its tooltip before planting.

pages.title: Hydroponic substrate
pages.text:
§6Hydroponic substrate§r is a water-soaked soil: §l4 dirt + 2 compost + 1 beeswax§r make 4 blocks at the §lagricultural workbench§r (the assembler makes it too).
• Placed, it is §lpacked§r: till it with a hoe (the farmer robot does it too).
• Tilled, it takes §levery seed§r like always-moist farmland, paddies included, and the crop grows §l×1.5 faster§r.
• It does §lnot change the climate§r: biome temperature and humidity, resistance margin and greenhouse count exactly as on irrigated farmland. A plant hostile to the biome still withers.
It is also the floor of the §6space greenhouse§r trays.

pages.title: Fruit trees
pages.text:
Twelve trees: apple, pear, cherry, apricot, peach, plum, orange, lemon, pomegranate, mango, banana, olive. Their §6saplings§r rarely drop from vanilla leaves and are sold by the wandering trader.
The leaves of a grown tree go through §lblossom§r, §lgreen§r fruit, then §lripe§r: right-click to pick, the cycle starts again. Climate counts as for crops.
Fruits make juice (press), jams (jar), pies, dried fruit (drying rack) and salads; olives give oil.

pages.title: Kitchen stations
pages.text:
Stations are made at the benches (farming bench for the wooden ones, coppersmith, metalworker, mason) and open with a §lright-click§r: each has its own §lscreen§r (input and output slots, gauges, arrow, status screen; Recipes, Sides and Info tabs). Stations worked by hand have a button (“Cut”, “Whisk”, “Turn the screw”…); §lShift + right-click with an empty hand§r also does one stroke. Liquids go through two slot pairs: “§lEmpty§r” (a full bucket or bottle pours into the tank, the empty container comes back) and “§lFill§r” (an empty bottle, mug or bucket fills from the tank). Hoppers and pipes work too, side by side (sides tab).
• §6Cutting board§r: the food, a §lknife§r in its slot, then “Cut”.
• §6Kitchen stove§r: fuel; it heats the station placed §lon top§r. A campfire, fire, lava or magma also heat.
• §6Cooking pot§r: on heat, add §lexactly§r the recipe's ingredients and liquid; serve with the requested container (bowl, cup…).
• §6Frying pan§r: four places, each at its own pace. §6Bread oven§r: its own fire, four places. §6Mixing bowl§r: ingredients (milk or water through the “Empty” slot) then “Whisk”. §6Drying rack§r: four spots in the open air; placed §lover a campfire§r (right-click the fire with the rack), it dries twice as fast. The §6smokehouse§r then smokes dried meat and fish (page "Drying and smoking").

pages.title: From wheat to bread
pages.text:
1. Grain at the §6millstone§r (or the mortar, at the farming bench) → §6flour§r. Barley, rye and wheat give it; oats make flakes, corn makes meal.
2. §6Yeast§r: 2 flour + a fruit + water, in the §lvat§r (5 min).
3. §6Dough§r: 3 flour + yeast + salt + water, in the §lmixing bowl§r (8 whisk strokes) → 2 dough.
4. Dough in the §6bread oven§r → §6bread§r. Bread makes toasts, sandwiches, burgers, fishing bait.
Same path for pastry (butter), fresh pasta (eggs), batter and cake batter.

pages.title: Milk, butter and cheese
pages.text:
• §6Butter churn§r: a bucket of milk in the “Empty” slot (1,000 mB), then “Churn” → 2 §6cream§r; 2 creams churned → §6butter§r.
• §6Curd§r: in the cooking pot, milk with vinegar or a lemon → 3 curds.
• §6Cheese press§r: 4 curds, “Tighten the press” (8 turns) → a §6fresh cheese wheel§r.
• §6Ripening§r: place the wheel §lin the dark§r (a cellar). It slowly turns golden and becomes an §6aged cheese wheel§r. Cut on the board: 8 cheese (4 for a fresh wheel).
Only §lfemales§r give milk, when it is ready (see husbandry).

pages.title: Jars and cans
pages.text:
• §6Preserves jar§r: 3 fruits + sugar → §6jam§r; 3 vegetables + vinegar + salt → §6pickles§r. The product keeps the fruit or vegetable name ("Strawberry Jam"). The jar §lseals§r itself when the recipe is complete and works without you (3 to 4 min).
• Sturgeon roe + salt → §6caviar§r.
• §6Can sealer§r: a §ltin can§r and a dish, “Seal” three times → §6canned food§r of that dish. It stacks to 16, feeds and gives §lexactly the same effects§r as the dish: the astronaut's ideal ration.

pages.title: Beer, wine and spirits
pages.text:
The process is realistic: each step has its station.
• §6Beer§r: barley steeped in the vat → §6green malt§r; dried → §6malt§r; milled → §6crushed malt§r. In the §6brew kettle§r (on heat): malt + water → §6wort§r; + hops → §6hopped wort§r. In the §6fermenting vat§r with yeast (10 min) → beer (and the yeast multiplies).
• §6Wine§r: grapes in the §6fruit press§r → §6grape must§r; vat → wine; §6barrel§r → §6aged wine§r. Cider (apple juice), perry, mead likewise; a cider forgotten in the barrel turns to §6vinegar§r.
• §6Spirits§r: in the §6copper still§r (on heat): wine → brandy, beer → new make spirit (aged in the barrel: §lwhisky§r), potato wash → vodka, cane wash → rum.
Bottling: an §lempty bottle§r (glassware from the potter's bench, not the glass bottle) or an §lempty mug§r for beer, in the “Fill” slot of the vat or the barrel.
These are §llarge stations§r placed in one go: 2 × 2 vat, 1 × 2 kettle (with its hood), 2 × 2 still (pot, swan neck, worm in its water tub), 1 × 2 barrel (a cask lying on its rack, one block tall: casks line up and stack into a cellar). They need free room (they extend to the right, the back and up); fill them through any of their blocks, hoppers and pipes included; breaking one block breaks the station. The kettle and the still are heated through the block you placed.

pages.title: Champagne and sparkling cider
pages.text:
Two §lsparkling§r drinks, fermented a second time §lin the bottle§r:
• §6tirage§r in the §6mixing bowl§r: an §lempty bottle§r, sugar, §lyeast§r and 250 mB of §lyoung wine§r (the base wine: grapes in the press → must → vat) or §lcider§r (apples in the press → apple juice → vat), 3 whisks → a §6tirage bottle§r;
• §6second fermentation§r: §l4 tirage bottles§r in the §6fermenting vat§r (no liquid) → §l4 bottles§r of §6champagne§r in 10 min, or of §6sparkling cider§r in 8 min.
Champagne: regeneration and jump boost; sparkling cider: speed and jump boost. Plain cider is still drawn from the vat with an empty bottle.

pages.title: Mushrooms
pages.text:
Three mushrooms are grown like the other plants (genes, stages, climate, harvest by click, successive flushes): the §6brown mushroom§r, the §6red mushroom§r and the §6button mushroom§r.
• §lSpores§r: at the §6cutting board§r, one mushroom → 2 spores; a wild mushroom picked (small or huge, without shears) sometimes gives some; the button mushroom comes from §lcompost§r: a ripe compost bin puts some in its spawn slot, one time in four.
• §lGround§r: §6mushroom substrate§r (agricultural bench: 2 compost, 2 wheat for straw, 1 sawdust → 4), always moist, grows ×1.25; §lmycelium§r or §lpodzol§r ×0.75; tilled hydroponic substrate ×1.5. Never farmland.
• §lShade§r: they only grow at a light level of §l12 or less§r (cave, woodland, under a roof, at night); in broad daylight they wait without withering. The look card says so.
Hydroponic farms grow them too. Dishes: soup, risotto, §6chicken with mushrooms§r, §6royal omelette§r (mixing bowl then pan), §6stuffed mushrooms§r, §6mushroom pie§r, §6sautéed mushrooms§r.

pages.title: Drying and smoking
pages.text:
Meat and fish are §ldried first§r, then §lsmoked§r.
• §6Drying rack§r: right-click a §lcampfire§r with the rack: it settles over the fire on two forked stakes. Lit, the fire dries §ltwice as fast§r (even in the rain); §6beef jerky§r only dries over the fire. Fish fillet → §6dried fillet§r, salmon → §6cured salmon§r, pork chop → §6dry-cured ham§r, bacon → §6dry-cured bacon§r, raw sausage → §6dry sausage§r.
• §6Smokehouse§r: a wooden cabinet over a brick firebox. Put §lwood§r, §lchips§r, sawdust or §lcharcoal§r (no coal) in the firebox, then hang four dried pieces on the hooks: dried fillet → §6smoked fish§r, cured salmon → 2 §6smoked salmon§r, dry-cured ham → §6ham§r, dry-cured bacon → §6smoked bacon§r, dry sausage → §6smoked sausage§r. Smoke rises from the chimney.
• It replaces Minecraft's smoker (no longer craftable): anything without a smokehouse recipe cooks as in the old one (crustaceans, potatoes…), four times slower.
Dry-cured ham, dry sausage and beef jerky can also be eaten as they are.

pages.title: Food effects
pages.text:
Dishes feed more than their ingredients, and give effects:
• §6Well Fed§r: big dishes (stews, cakes, pizzas…) §lstop hunger§r from dropping for a long while.
• §6Caffeine§r (coffee, tea, chocolate): speed and attack speed; too much coffee in a row gives §ljitters§r (weakness).
• §6Tipsy§r: alcohol builds up and slowly wears off. A little brings luck; too much brings §lnausea§r in waves, and far too much makes you stagger and blurs your sight.
• Salads: regeneration; meats: strength; stews: resistance; spicy dishes: fire resistance; sushi: water breathing; caviar: luck…
Some dishes are placed (cake, pies, pizza, quiche) and eaten slice by slice.

pages.title: Breeds and breeding
pages.text:
Cows, sheep, pigs, chickens and goats each have §lfive breeds§r, and each breed is §lan animal in its own right§r: its name, model, size, coat, yields and §6spawn egg§r. Breeds spawn according to the biome climate: Highland and Ouessant like the cold, Duroc and Boer the heat.
• §lMilk§r: Holstein, Saanen; §lmeat§r: Charolais, Piétrain, Boer; §lwool§r: Merino (thicker fleece, regrows faster); §leggs§r: Leghorn; the §lAngora§r goat can be shorn (mohair).
• Only females give milk and eggs; milk has its timer (the card says when it is ready). The male is a little taller.
• Breeding takes §la male and a female§r of the same species, neither starving nor thirsty; two breeds can be crossed: the young takes the breed of §lone of the two parents, a one-in-two chance§r.
Animals also eat the mod's feeds (barley, oats, §6compound feed§r…); §lchickens follow any seed§r (vanilla, mod, other worlds) and §lcats and ocelots every mod fish§r (taming, healing, breeding: like cod).

pages.title: The breeds in detail
pages.text:
§lCows§r (height at the withers; chickens: of the head)
• §lHolstein§r: 1.45 m · Tall, black pied, short horns
• §lJersey§r: 1.22 m · Small and fine, fawn, dark mask
• §lCharolais§r: 1.42 m · Massive, cream, pale horns
• §lHighland§r: 1.15 m · Low, long hair, wide horns
• §lAngus§r: 1.32 m · Black, polled, stocky
§lSheep§r
• §lMerino§r: 0.78 m · Thick fleece up to the eyes, horned ram
• §lSuffolk§r: 0.86 m · Tall, black head and legs
• §lTexel§r: 0.82 m · Muscular, bare white face
• §lOuessant§r: 0.50 m · The smallest breed, black, horned ram
• §lJacob§r: 0.76 m · Piebald, four horns
§lPigs§r
• §lLarge White§r: 0.90 m · Long, pinkish white, prick ears
• §lGascon§r: 0.80 m · Black, ears over the eyes
• §lDuroc§r: 0.88 m · Red, arched back
• §lPiétrain§r: 0.82 m · Heavily muscled, black spots
• §lKunekune§r: 0.58 m · Small and round, wattles under the chin
§lChickens§r
• §lLeghorn§r: 0.50 m · Slim and white, large comb
• §lMarans§r: 0.54 m · Copper black, feathered legs
• §lBrahma§r: 0.68 m · Giant, black hackles, feathered legs
• §lGolden Gaulish§r: 0.50 m · Golden, black tail
• §lSilkie§r: 0.36 m · Bantam, down feathers, crest
§lGoats§r
• §lAlpine§r: 0.80 m · Chamois with a dorsal stripe, sabre horns
• §lSaanen§r: 0.86 m · Tall, white, polled
• §lBoer§r: 0.76 m · Stocky, red head, drooping ears
• §lAngora§r: 0.62 m · Small, curly mohair, spiral horns
• §lPoitevine§r: 0.76 m · Dark, white face stripes

pages.title: Feeders and troughs
pages.text:
A §ldomestic§r animal (born on the farm, hand-fed or led on a lead) gets §6hungry§r and §6thirsty§r. It goes on its own to the nearest §6feeder§r or §6water trough§r (16 blocks), or drinks from water in the world; grazers also eat grass.
• Feeder: grain, hay, vegetables or compound feed depending on the species. Trough: water buckets (“Empty” slot of its screen), pipes, or rain. An animal only heads for a feeder or trough it can §lreach§r: the one in the next pen, behind the fence, is set aside.
• Low food or water: §lyield drops§r (milk, eggs, wool, meat) in proportion, down to §l10%§r when empty. An animal never dies of hunger or thirst: it §lwastes away§r (smoke) and barely produces.
• Wild animals have no needs, but produce half as much.
Sneaking in front of an animal, the card shows its food, water, production and yield.

pages.title: Watering and composting
pages.text:
A §6sprinkler§r keeps the soil moist and speeds up growth: §l9 × 9 blocks§r in bronze (growth ×1.5), §l15 × 15§r in steel (×2). It needs water: pipes, buckets or rain — or place it §lon the field's water hole§r: it pumps by itself. It stops in the rain and with a redstone signal.
The §6compost bin§r replaces Minecraft's composter: it takes anything compostable, each item with its own chance to add a layer. At §l7 layers§r, it closes and §lferments§r for 2 minutes, steaming, then gives §l4 compost§r. Hoppers: waste on top or the sides, compost below; a comparator reads its level. Minecraft composters already placed (villages included) become Pioneer's compost bins, and farmers work at them.
§6Compost§r grows a crop by one stage and §lfeeds§r it: harvest ×1.25 and seeds improve more often. Industrial §6fertilizer§r does the same, with two stages. Put in a steel sprinkler, compost or fertilizer feeds the whole field while watering.

pages.title: Scarecrows and crows
pages.text:
When a field ripens, flocks of §6crows§r come from the sky, at most §lone crow per 20 planted cells§r (fewer than 20: none; 6 at most): each glides down onto an advanced crop, pecks, then §lravages§r it (three stages lost, the whole plant if it was young). Full after three to five plants, they leave.
They flee from players (sneaking lets you get closer). A §6scarecrow§r guards §l12 blocks§r around it: no crow targets a crop there, and one that flies in leaves again, cawing. Like scavengers, they §lprowl at the edge of its zone§r: they circle above it or land on it, waiting for a crop left unguarded. It also stops farmland trampling within 8 blocks.
Give it a §lcarved pumpkin§r or a §ljack o'lantern§r head (which gives light); sneak with an empty hand to take it back. It sways in the wind. Crows can be turned off in the config (farm.crows).

pages.title: The weather station
pages.text:
The §6weather station§r shows the §ltemperature§r (in °C), §lhumidity§r, weather and wind when looked at; its anemometer spins faster in rain and thunder, its vane follows the wind.
Right-click: the list of §lideal§r and §ltolerable crops§r here (in irrigated soil), and of the §lfruit trees§r that bear here. Great for choosing what to plant before clearing land.
It gives a §lredstone§r signal: 8 in the rain, 15 in a thunderstorm — enough to close a greenhouse or stop sprinklers.

pages.title: Bees and honey
pages.text:
An §6apiary§r placed near flowers, crops or blossoming trees (at least 4 within 6 blocks) gets a §lcolony§r by itself in two minutes. By day, without rain, the bees go out foraging: they §lpollinate§r (faster growth, seeds improve more often, tree blossoms set fruit sooner) and fill the §lframes§r (4 per apiary; one frame in 5 minutes with 12 flowers or more).
Frames go in and out through the apiary's screen (right-click) — without a lit §lcampfire§r under the apiary, the bees sting when you open it.
The §6honey extractor§r has its own §lscreen§r (right-click): full frames in the input slot, then the “Turn the crank” button (or Shift + right-click with an empty hand), 6 turns per frame. Each frame gives §l250 mB of honey§r (in the tank), §l1 beeswax§r (candles), a §lhoneycomb§r every other time, and the empty frame comes back. An §lempty bottle§r (250 mB) or a §lbucket§r (1,000 mB) put in the “Fill” slot fill up with honey by themselves.

pages.title: Eggs, nesting boxes and incubators
pages.text:
Hens lay at the pace of their breed and care. With a §6nesting box§r within 12 blocks, they §lgo and lay there§r: up to 12 eggs in the straw, collected by clicking or with a hopper below.
If an §ladult rooster§r lives within 8 blocks, most eggs are §6fertile§r: they carry the mother's breed. Six fertile eggs in an §6incubator§r rock in the warmth and §lhatch in 5 minutes§r: chicks of their breed, already tame.
The §6auto feeder§r keeps the farm running: loaded with feed (hopper) and water (pipe), it fills every §lfeeder and trough within 8 blocks§r every 5 seconds.

pages.title: Fish
pages.text:
§l55 species§r live in nine habitats: cold, temperate or warm fresh water, swamps, underground waters, cold, temperate or warm sea, and the deep sea (oceans, below y 30). Cod, salmon, pufferfish and tropical fish remain Minecraft's items.
Some have a §lproperty§r: venom (piranha, lionfish, pufferfish), sight in the dark (lanternfish, anglerfish), a shock when caught (§6electric eel§r), strength (swordfish), caviar roe (§6sturgeon§r). The §6coelacanth§r, the §6oarfish§r and the §6arapaima§r are §llegendary§r. The §6gray reef shark§r can be §lcaught§r in warm seas (rare, strength 9): it gives its item like the others (4 shark meats on the cutting board); released, it is the real shark.
Wild fish despawn far from players, like Minecraft's (which no longer spawn); a fish released from a bucket or named stays. A water bucket catches them with their species and size. Each species is an §lanimal of its own§r (its spawn egg), at its size: from 0.3 block (cavefish) to 0.9 block (pike) and up to 3 blocks (oarfish).
Right-click water with a §lraw fish§r (or a crustacean's raw meat): it is §lreleased alive§r, at its size, and stays; Shift + right-click on the side of a block sets it down there alive (out of water, it flops). Shift + right-click on the §ltop§r of a block lays it out on the stall, next to the others of its species.

pages.title: Tension fishing
pages.text:
1. §lWind up§r: hold right-click (power gauge), then §llet go§r to cast — the longer you hold, the farther the bobber flies, up to the line's length. It floats; the wait depends on the rod, the water (a puddle bites poorly) and the bait.
2. §lBite§r: the bobber dips and "!" shows. Click quickly to §lstrike§r.
3. §lFight§r: §lhold right-click§r to reel — tension rises, distance drops. §lLet go§r when it pulls too hard: the fish takes line. In the red for too long, the §lline snaps§r; slack for too long, the fish §lgets off§r.
The gauge's §lgreen zone§r depends on the fish: the stronger, bigger (species and specimen) and livelier it is, the §lnarrower§r it gets; a better rod widens it. Needle in the green, the fish comes in at full speed; outside the green, the reel slips.
Each species has its strength and behavior: steady, violent rushes, jumps (do not reel during a jump), erratic, runner. The power and tension gauges show §lin the middle of the screen§r.
Rods: §6bamboo§r (fragile, 10 m of line), §6bronze§r (15 m), §6steel§r (22 m; stronger line, faster reel). An §6earthworm§r (found when digging dirt, 2.3% of blocks; or bought from the fisherman) or §6bait§r in the off hand: faster bites and rare species more often.

pages.title: Fish farming
pages.text:
Very rarely, an adult fish §lspawns§r in seagrass: the seagrass becomes a §6roe cluster§r in the species' color. After a long while, the eggs §lhatch§r into an adult fish (no fry) — if the area is not overcrowded: at most §l4 fish§r within 16 blocks, and in a small body of water §l1 fish per 32 water blocks§r (a 3 × 3 × 2 pond keeps only one).
A §lbottle§r or a §lbucket§r collects the roe; right-click seagrass to replant it: a pond of seagrass becomes a fish farm. Sturgeon roe makes §6caviar§r.
In the Living Age, the §6aquaculture farm§r also raises all the mod's species (fish feed, water, oxygen or compressed air).

pages.title: Serving and replanting
pages.text:
§lServing§r: Shift + right-click with a dish or a §ldrink§r on top of a block serves it (up to 4 servings of the same): on a bronze-rimmed wooden §6bowl plate§r, a §6board§r for cured meats and bread, or in its bowl, bottle, cup, mug or jar. Right-click: one §lbite§r or §lsip§r, and the serving visibly shrinks; the last one gives the effects and returns the container. Shift + right-click with an empty hand: take back a serving not yet started. Cakes, pies and pizzas are placed whole and eaten slice by slice.
§lSetting down§r: everything else you eat or cook can be set down too, Shift + right-click on top of a block: fruit and vegetables in §lheaps§r, roots, ears and fish lying in rows, berries in a §lbasket§r, eggs in a nest, flour and grain in a §lsack§r, sugar and salt in a §lcrock§r, jars, bottles, doughs and empty tableware standing or stacked. Shift + right-click on a heap: one more; right-click with an empty hand: take one back, with Shift: all of it. Planting, eating and releasing a fish into water come first.
§lDisplaying§r: the §6dish shelf§r (carpenter's bench) holds §l4 dishes, drinks or ingredients§r in a row; against a wall it hangs on brackets, on the floor it stands on legs; it stacks and aligned shelves (same facing, same height) join up. Right-click with a dish: it goes to the spot you aim at; empty hand: take it back.
§lReplanting§r: carrots, potatoes, beetroots, onions, parsnips, radishes, leeks and sweet potatoes give their §lseeds or seed tubers§r at the §6cutting board§r (knife). When one product has two cuts (potato: sticks or seed potatoes), sneak to pick the other one.

pages.title: From farm to factory
Crop storage
Hemp
pages.text:
§6Hemp§r is a tall crop (2 blocks) for temperate to warm climates; its seeds turn up in grass, like the others. A ripe plant gives the §lstalk§r, §lseeds§r and its §lbuds§r (1 or 2).
• §lStalk§r: §6hemp fiber§r (knife, tanner), then §lcanvas§r, §lrope§r, §lstring§r (grid) and §lpaper§r (3 fibers + water bucket → 3 paper).
• §lSeeds§r: replant them, or press them into §lplant oil§r at the kitchen press (6 seeds → 250 mB) and the extractor (oil pressing); chickens eat them.
• §lBuds§r: on the §6drying rack§r (2 min), then rolled in paper at the agricultural bench (knife): §l2 joints§r from 2 dried buds and 1 paper.
§lThe joint§r: right-click with matches to light it; it burns for §l2 minutes§r, even in your pocket. Hold right-click to draw, release to exhale (sneaking: a smoke ring). Each puff gives short effects: §lHunger§r (30 s), §lSlowness§r (8 s), §lRegeneration§r (5 s); then a 20 s rest. Dried buds and joints §lsell well§r to Peddlers.

pages.title: Cotton thread
Rabbit farming
pages.text:
Every rabbit has a §6breed§r, chosen by climate like other livestock: coat, size and yields depend on it.
• §lBurgundy Fawn§r: fawn, good meat (litter 7, size ×1.15)
• §lFlemish Giant§r: huge, slow to grow (litter 6, size ×1.55)
• §lAngora§r: can be shorn: angora wool (litter 6, size ×1.05)
• §lRex§r: fine fur: pelts (litter 7, size ×1.00)
• §lNew Zealand White§r: yield: grows fast, big litters (litter 9, size ×1.15)
• §lLop§r: calm: does not flee (litter 7, size ×1.10)
The §6rabbit hutch§r (2 blocks long, rabbits visible inside; carpenter: 6 planks, 2 iron bars, 1 hay bale) holds up to §l8 rabbits§r. Bring your rabbits §lon a lead§r and click the hutch: they all go in. Food on top (carrots, dandelions, hay, kale, lettuce…): when fed, two adults have a §llitter§r about every 10 minutes; kits grow up in 20 minutes. Adults give §lpelts§r, §langora wool§r and §lmanure§r (compost) in the bottom slots (hopper). §lKnife + sneak§r: slaughter an adult (2 meat × the breed, 1 pelt; two always stay). Sneak empty-handed: a rabbit comes out.
§6Heredity§r: the young takes one parent's breed (half and half); each stat (growth, litter, meat, pelt, wool) is the parents' average, within 6%: select your best breeders (look card, sneaking). The §lAngora§r can also be shorn in the wild (shears); 4 angora wool → 1 white wool at the tanner.

pages.title: Horses
pages.text:
Every horse has a §6breed§r (by climate), with its coat and size; the §ldonkey§r and the §lmule§r have theirs. Two new stats matter for transport: §6draft strength§r (what it pulls) and §6pack load§r (what it carries), in kilograms.
• §lPercheron§r: heavy draft: strength, load — draft 850-1000 kg, pack 140-170 kg, 7.2-8.9 blocks/s
• §lBoulonnais§r: draft: strength, load — draft 800-950 kg, pack 130-160 kg, 7.2-8.9 blocks/s
• §lThoroughbred§r: speed, little stamina — draft 250-330 kg, pack 70-90 kg, 12.6-14.2 blocks/s
• §lArabian§r: speed, loves the heat — draft 230-300 kg, pack 70-90 kg, 11.8-13.5 blocks/s
• §lMerens§r: hardy jumper, mountain horse — draft 450-550 kg, pack 110-130 kg, 9.3-11.0 blocks/s
• §lCamargue§r: hardy jumper of the marshes — draft 420-520 kg, pack 100-120 kg, 9.7-11.4 blocks/s
• §lFriesian§r: prestige: proud carriage — draft 550-650 kg, pack 110-130 kg, 10.1-11.8 blocks/s
• §lPony§r: small: young riders, light pack — draft 180-240 kg, pack 45-60 kg, 7.6-9.3 blocks/s
• §lProvence Donkey§r: pack animal: frugal, loves the heat — draft 300-380 kg, pack 90-110 kg, 7.4-7.4 blocks/s
• §lMule§r: pack and draft: the toughest — draft 500-600 kg, pack 130-160 kg, 7.4-7.4 blocks/s
• §lPoitou Donkey§r: the largest donkey: heavy pack — draft 380-450 kg, pack 110-130 kg, 7.2-8.0 blocks/s
• §lCotentin Donkey§r: hardy, likes cold damp weather — draft 300-360 kg, pack 95-115 kg, 7.4-8.0 blocks/s
§6Heredity§r: the foal takes one parent's breed (half and half); speed, jump, health, draft and pack are the parents' average within 6%, inside its breed's range (a little beyond through selection). Horse × donkey always gives a mule. Look card: breed, draft, pack; sneaking: speed (blocks/s), jump (blocks), health.
The §llead§r is now made at the tanner's bench (knife): 2 fiber ropes and an iron ring.

pages.title: Living breeds: donkeys, llamas, eggs
pages.text:
Every §lrabbit§r, §lhorse§r, §ldonkey§r and §lllama§r breed is now a §6creature of its own§r, with its §6spawn egg§r (Worlds tab, fauna). Vanilla rabbits, horses, donkeys and llamas spawning in the world take the breed of their climate; those of your older worlds keep theirs.
Three §6donkeys§r:
• §lProvence Donkey§r: pack animal: frugal, loves the heat — pack 90-110 kg
• §lPoitou Donkey§r: the largest donkey: heavy pack — pack 110-130 kg
• §lCotentin Donkey§r: hardy, likes cold damp weather — pack 95-115 kg
Four §6llamas§r (mountains, savannas; chest and llama caravan as in vanilla):
• §lCcara Llama§r: pack llama: the best carrier — pack 45-55 kg
• §lTampuli Llama§r: woolly llama of the cold highlands — pack 35-45 kg
• §lSuri Llama§r: silky fleece in locks — pack 30-40 kg
• §lChaku Llama§r: all-rounder, copes with heat — pack 40-50 kg
Heredity as with horses: the young takes one parent's breed, its stats are their average. The §6rabbit hutch§r is now §l2 blocks long§r: you can see the lodged rabbits (their breed, their size) hopping. An old one-block hutch grows by itself as soon as the space beside it is free.

pages.title: The mechanical kitchen
pages.text:
From the Mechanical Age, five §6mechanical machines§r do the work for you: hooked to a shaft, they run §lthe same recipes§r as the hand stations, at the pace of the rotation.
• §6Mechanical Fruit Press§r: fruit press and cheese press (320 N·m, 16 rpm). Two worms turn the press screws, the head comes down and squeezes the basket; juice runs into the trough.
• §6Mechanical Churn§r: milk into cream, cream into butter (60 N·m, 60 rpm); the paddle beater turns in the barrel.
• §6Mechanical Chopper§r: cutting board recipes (90 N·m, 60 rpm); two cams, two knife strokes per turn.
• §6Mechanical Kneader§r: mixing bowl recipes, up to six ingredients and a liquid (140 N·m, 36 rpm). §lShaft from below§r, like the millstone.
• §6Mechanical Honey Extractor§r: full frames → honey, wax, honeycombs and empty frames, each in its own slot; bottles and buckets put in the “Fill” slot fill up with honey (50 N·m, 120 rpm). §lShaft from below§r.
One hand §lstroke§r is worth §lone shaft turn§r (half at the chopper, two at the extractor): the faster the shaft, the faster the machine, up to 1.5 times its rated speed. Below its minimum speed, it waits.

pages.title: Hooking up and filling
pages.text:
Right-click: the screen (speed gauge on the left, tanks, progress, status screen, age chip). §lIngredients§r go in the input slots, §lone item per slot§r: a hopper never fills two slots with the same item, so there is room for the others. In §lautomatic§r mode the machine makes the most complete recipe that is fully present; the §lRecipes§r tab (the selector square) §llocks a recipe§r (potatoes into fries rather than seedlings, for example).
§lAutomating§r: hoppers and logistic cables §lfeed through the top and sides§r and §ltake out through the bottom and sides§r; pipes §lfill§r the input tank (churn milk, kneader water) and §ldrain§r the output tank (juice, honey). By hand (1.0.5): the screen's slot pairs: “Empty” (a full bucket pours into the input tank, the empty bucket comes back) and “Fill” (a bucket, an empty bottle, an empty mug or a glass bottle fills from the output tank); no more bucket clicks on the station.
Leftovers (buckets, bottles) come out in the output slots. Output full: the machine stops and lets the shaft go.

pages.title: The electric kitchen
Bases and sauces
Ingredient families
Around the vegetable garden
The bakery
Sandwiches
Sweets and candies
Crustaceans
pages.text:
Six crustaceans live in the world. On §lbeaches§r, between land and water: the §6green crab§r (cold and temperate seas, it walks sideways) and the §6hermit crab§r (temperate and warm seas, it leaves a §6seashell§r: in a mortar, bone meal).
§lOn the bottom§r, 100% aquatic (out of water they suffocate): the §6lobster§r (cold and temperate seas), the §6crayfish§r (rivers, lakes and swamps), the §6shrimp§r (temperate and warm seas) and the §6king crab§r (cold seas and the deep).
They flee from players and barely pinch. Their meat can be eaten raw, but is much better §lcooked§r: furnace, smokehouse, campfire, or boiled in the §6cooking pot§r (2 for 250 mB of water). Look at one: its §lcard§r gives its size and its waters.

pages.title: Net and crab pot
pages.text:
Two traps work on their own, set §lin the water§r:
• the §6fishing net§r (farming bench: ropes, sticks, flint), stretched between its two posts, catches the §llocal fish§r. The more water around (5 × 3 × 5), the faster it catches; it needs at least 20 water blocks. One catch every 2 to 4 minutes in open water;
• the §6crab pot§r (farming bench: planks, sticks, ropes) sits §lon the bottom§r and is §lbaited§r (raw fish, fillet, earthworm, bait, rotten flesh; up to 16): it catches the §laquatic crustaceans§r of those waters — crayfish in fresh water, lobsters, shrimp or king crabs at sea — and eats one bait per catch (about 3 minutes).
Right-click with an empty hand: collect. Nine catch slots; when full, it stops. A §lhopper§r or a §llogistic cable§r takes the catch out (and fills the pot with bait). Look at them: their card shows the water, the bait and the next catch.

pages.title: The aquarium
Laying out an aquarium
Tobacco
pages.text:
§6Tobacco§r is a tall crop of §lwarm climates§r: its seeds come from grass in warm regions, like the other wild seeds. When ripe, it bears broad leaves and clusters of pink flowers.
§6Tobacco leaves§r are dried on the §6drying rack§r (3 minutes): §6cured tobacco§r. On the §6cutting board§r, one cured tobacco gives 2 §6pipe tobacco§r; at the §lfarming bench§r (knife), 3 cured tobacco roll 2 §6cigars§r.
Smoking is purely §lcosmetic§r: no effect on health, hunger or sight. It is for role-play — a pipe by the fire, a cigar to celebrate a fine harvest.

pages.title: Pipe and cigar
pages.text:
Three §6pipes§r: §lcorncob§r (carpenter, knife), §lbriar§r (carpenter, knife and saw) and §lclay§r (potter). The §6matchbox§r (carpenter: paper, sticks, sulfur) lasts 24 uses; the §lfire starter§r and §lflint and steel§r work too, in the off hand or in the inventory.
Pipe in hand, §lright-click§r: fill it (one pipe tobacco = 8 puffs), then light it; then §lhold§r to draw and release to blow. §lSneak§r when releasing: a §6smoke ring§r. After a minute without a puff it goes out (light it again).
A §6cigar§r is lit the same way and burns for 8 minutes, even in your pocket (each puff uses it a little more). Rested on an §6ashtray§r (potter), it smokes by itself, half as fast: empty hand to take it back.

pages.title: Musical instruments
pages.text:
§6Instruments§r are made at the §6luthier’s bench§r (planks, logs, string, file): §6wooden flute§r (turned wood, brass rings, beeswax plug), §6guitar§r (spruce top, strings, nickel-wire frets, resin varnish), §6accordion§r (leather bellows, brass reeds, springs, bone keys) and §6drum§r (log shell, leather heads, rope). The note block and the jukebox are made there too.
Right-click: the §lkeyboard§r opens (the game keeps running). Flute, guitar and accordion play §l15 notes§r, C to C over two octaves: bottom row of your keyboard for low notes, middle row for high ones (the letters shown follow your layout), or click a key. The drum has §l8 strokes§r: kick, snare, toms, hi-hat, crash, clap.
§6Known tunes§r play by themselves (Au clair de la lune, Frère Jacques, Ode to Joy…) and the drum has its §6rhythms§r: they keep going with the screen closed, as long as the instrument is in hand. Players within 48 blocks hear you and §lsee you play§r: guitar against the belly, accordion bellows breathing, drum on a strap with a stick in each hand, flute raised to the lips. Enough for a village band.

pages.title: Music of the Earth
pages.text:
On §lEarth§r, ten pieces composed for Pioneer's mix with the game's music: when Minecraft starts a track, one time in two it is a piece from the mod. The silences stay the game's own.
They follow your §6progress§r: §6Dawn over the Furrows§r, §6Song of the Wheat§r and §6Vigil under the Stars§r from the start; then §6The Mill’s Sails§r (first crank or first mill), §6Anvil and Bellows§r (first bronze), §6Breath of Steam§r (first boiler), §6The Coast Train§r (steam engine), §6The Tall Chimneys§r (industry), §6Retorts and Stills§r (chemistry) and §6Cherenkov Glow§r (atomic age).
§lDawn§r calls for the dawn piece, §lnight§r for the vigil and the atom, the §lseaside§r for the coast train. The title shows discreetly when a piece starts. Settings (file §lpioneers-client.toml§r, audio section): §learthMusic§r, §learthMusicShare§r (share of the mod's pieces, 0 to 1), §learthMusicProgression§r, §learthMusicTitle§r.

pages.title: Pioneer’s records
pages.text:
Each piece has its §6record§r, made at the §6luthier’s bench§r. First a §6blank record§r: a §lshellac§r blank (2 rosin, 1 beeswax, 1 coal, with a knife), or 2 records at once with §lprimitive plastic§r and coal.
Then the grooves are cut with a §lfile§r: blank record, §lpaper§r, the label's §ldye§r and an item of the theme — feather (dawn), wheat, wooden cog (mill), bronze ingot (forge), brass gear (steam), steel ingot (industry), sulfur (chemistry), seashell (coast train), yellowcake (atom), candle (vigil).
Records can also be found, rarely, in the §lchests§r that suit them (village houses, smiths, cartographer, fisher, shipwrecks, treasure, dungeons, mineshafts, temples, igloos…) and drop from a §lcreeper killed by a skeleton§r. The jukebox sound fades with distance; a comparator gives the record's rank (1 to 10).

pages.title: Backpacks
pages.text:
Two §6backpacks§r, at the §ltanner's bench§r (knife): §lleather§r (5 leather, 2 fiber ropes, 2 pegs): §l16 slots§r; §ltanned leather§r (6 tanned leather, 2 ropes, 2 iron rings): §l32 slots§r.
§lRight-click§r: the bag opens; its contents stay in the item (you can give it away, store it in a chest). Bags do not go inside bags. Kept in the §lhotbar§r or the off hand, it shows §lon your back§r.
§lUpgrade§r at the crafting grid: the leather backpack in the middle, 4 tanned leather and 2 iron rings around it: a tanned backpack that §lkeeps all its contents§r.

pages.title: Storage bags
Furniture for every wood
The wicker basket
pages.text:
The §6wicker basket§r (carpenter, with a knife: 4 sticks, 6 sugar cane, 2 fibers) sits on the floor or on a stall and holds §la single kind§r of farm produce: vegetables, fruit, grain, raw and cooked meat, fish, seafood, eggs, wool, honey, cheese… up to §l8 items§r; the §6tall basket§r (6 sticks, 10 sugar cane, 3 fibers), almost a block tall, holds §l16§r. It is a decoration: the heap rises with the amount, up to the brim when full.
• §lRight-click with the produce§r: one item (Shift: the whole stack). §lEmpty hand§r: a stack comes back (Shift: just one). The first item put in sets the kind; any other produce is refused until the basket is empty.
• You §lsee what is inside§r: the item itself, in a tight heap that fills the basket layer after layer up to a dome (6 steps, 10 for the tall basket); pumpkins, melons and other blocks as small cubes.
• Broken, it §lkeeps its contents§r (the tooltip tells what and how many). Hoppers, cables and robots fill and empty it; a comparator reads how full it is.

pages.title: Standing and wall shelves
pages.text:
Two shelves, in all §l11 woods§r, at the carpenter's bench (saw), each holding §l4 dishes, drinks or ingredients per board§r (right-click with the item: it goes to the spot you aim at; empty hand: take it back):
• the §6standing shelf§r (3 planks of the wood, 2 laths → 2) §lgoes on the floor§r: 4 legs, a §lbottom board§r and a §ltop board§r, both can be filled. Stacked, §lonly one board remains at each joint§r and the posts run all the way up; only the top one keeps its top board (what stood on it moves onto the added shelf). Side by side, posts are shared and boards become continuous (2 × 2, rows…);
• the §6wall shelf§r (2 planks, 1 lath, 2 pegs → 2) §lonly goes against the side of a block§r: a board on two brackets. Side by side, wall shelves make §lone long board§r, brackets at both ends (and one in the middle now and then in a long row). It falls, with what it holds, if the wall goes away.
Shelves of different woods join up too. Shelves placed before this patch are standing shelves (contents kept); those that hung on a wall become wall shelves of the same wood.

pages.title: Clothesline and drying
pages.text:
The §6rope hook§r (carpenter) goes on §lany face§r. With a rope from the mechanical system (§6fiber rope§r, tarred, leather belt), click one hook then another, up to §l16 blocks§r apart, with nothing in between: the line stretches and sags a little.
§lRight-click with an item§r on the line (or a hook): it hangs there, one spot every half block, held by a §lclothespin§r (clothes, banners) or a §lstring and hook§r (the rest); the line dips a little under each piece; §lempty hand§r: take the nearest one back; Shift + empty hand on a hook: the line comes down with everything hanging on it. Breaking a hook gives the rope back.
§lClothes§r (leather armor, tanner outfits, banners) are decoration. §lFish, meat, herbs and fruit§r with a drying rack recipe §ldry§r: 1.5 times the rack time in the shade, as fast as the rack §lin the sun§r, faster in a dry climate, slower in a humid one, §lnever in the rain§r. A lit §lcampfire§r 1 to 3 blocks below §lsmokes§r what has a smokehouse recipe (dried fillets → smoked fish…) and dries the rest twice as fast. A whole dried fish gives 2 dried fillets. JEI: “Drying” category.

pages.title: Timber beams
pages.text:
One decorative §6beam§r per wood (the eleven vanilla woods and §ltreated wood§r): a 12-pixel section, placed §lalong the axis you choose§r like a log; aligned beams join end to end for exposed framing, half-timbering and ceilings.
At the §lcarpenter§r, with a saw: §l1 log → 1 beam§r of its wood (stems for Nether woods, bamboo block for bamboo). §l8 beams + 1 creosote bucket → 8 treated wood beams§r, dark. Listed after the furniture (Building tab, "beams").

pages.title: Old masters
The railroad
pages.text:
Vanilla minecarts are gone (so are the rails and minecarts in the world): here comes a complete §6miniature railroad§r. Each vehicle is §lone block long§r; a train is a consist of coupled vehicles, pulled by one or more locomotives.

Everything is §lautomatic§r: give a train a schedule (a list of stations and when to leave them), switch it to automatic, and it §lfinds its way§r on its own, §lsets the switches§r ahead and stops exactly at the end of the platform. No redstone, no lever.

Trains keep running when nobody is around (unloaded chunks): a remote mine line keeps delivering.

pages.title: Laying track
pages.text:
Five qualities, each with its §ltop speed§r: §6wooden track§r 4 blocks/s, §6MKI§r 8, §6MKII§r 14, §6MKIII§r 22, §6MKIV§r 34. A train runs at the speed of the slowest track under it.
1. A track sits §lon a solid block§r: never in mid-air or on another track. Remove the block underneath and it falls.
2. Place blocks one after another: each track §ltakes the best shape§r from its neighbors, and the neighbors are recalculated at every placement: a line that turns makes its own curve.
3. Place a track §lnext to a line§r: the line becomes a §6switch§r toward it (the heel is on the side you stand on). A second one on the other side makes a three-way switch. Break the branch: the line turns straight again.
4. §6Gentle slope§r: place the next track §lone block higher§r at the end of a straight line; the last two blocks turn into a slope (one block up over two long), on an embankment made of the block that carries it.
5. The §6wrench§r (right-click) only offers shapes that fit the neighboring tracks: both heels of a switch, the wye, straight, curves…; Shift + right-click: previous shape.
A §lcurve§r (one block) limits to 6 blocks/s: keep fast lines straight.

pages.title: Special track
pages.text:
§6Bumping post§r: end of the line, trains stop against its buffers (it faces the way you look).
§6Brake track§r and §6booster track§r: for vehicles §lwithout a locomotive§r (mine carts, yards): one slows them down, the other launches them at 8 blocks/s.
§6Detector track§r: redstone and comparator signal while a train is on it, for players who want their own circuits. Trains §lnever need it§r.
§6Weighbridge§r: weighs the train on it (mass, vehicles, fill); comparator: the fill, from 1 to 15; right-click: the last reading; a computer reads it with §lrail.weigh(x, y, z)§r.
§6Uncoupler track§r: placed under a §lcoupling§r of a train stopped at a station, it splits the train there: the front leaves with its schedule, the rear stays in manual (cars left at the station, yards).

pages.title: Trains and vehicles
pages.text:
§lPlace§r: right-click a track with the vehicle's item; it faces where you look. Placed against another, it §lcouples§r on its own (on contact, buffer to buffer). §lPick up§r: hit it.
§6Steam locomotive§r: 8 blocks/s (+1 per tier), hauls 4 cars at full speed (6, 9, 13 at the next tiers) and slows down beyond that. It burns any fuel and drinks water: its own reserve, then that of the §6tenders§r. Refill them at an §6item loader§r (fuel), a §6water crane§r or with a bucket.
§6Boxcar§r: items; §6hopper car§r: bulk of a single kind; §6mine cart§r: pushed by hand (walk into it); §6handcar§r: board and pump.
§lRight-click§r a vehicle: its reserves (fuel and water of the locomotive and tender, cargo of the cars); §lShift + right-click§r: the train sheet. §lDriving§r: button on the sheet. Forward / back: movement keys; left / right: picks the branch of the next switch (straight otherwise).
A consist with a locomotive §lat each end§r (a tender may be at the end) is §lreversible§r: place them facing either way, the rear one turns outward by itself; in automatic the train leaves in either direction (shuttle between two dead-end stations). A station served both ways: one sign per direction, with the same name.

pages.title: Stations and schedules
pages.text:
The §6station sign§r is placed §lby clicking the track§r, looking in the direction trains arrive: it goes on their right, at the end of the platform (an arrow and a ghost show where; Shift: reverse): the train's head stops at the exit of the neighboring track block, the cars stretch out behind. Right-click: its §lname§r and its §ltrain limit§r.
Several stations may share the §lsame name§r: a train going to “Ore” picks the nearest one with room (limit: trains on their way or at the platform; closed = 0).
§lSchedule§r (train sheet): a list of stops, visited in order then looped. Each stop has its departure conditions: time at stop, inactivity (nothing loaded or unloaded for…), full, empty, count of an item, player aboard or not, fuel, fluid or gas, loaded, platform or robotic network stock, a computer's signal, the sign's redstone, room at the next stop. §lAND§r binds tighter than §lOR§r: “full OR time 60 s” leaves as soon as either is true.
Along the platform, the §6item loader§r loads (or unloads) the vehicle stopped in front of it; the §6water crane§r refills locomotives and tenders. They are also placed by clicking the track, on the aimed side. Schedule durations are typed on the keyboard (click the number).

pages.title: All traction types
pages.text:
Each age has its own traction, each in MKI to MKIV (×1.5 power and ×2 tanks per tier). Cars hauled at full speed at MKI; beyond that the locomotive slows down instead of stalling:
• §6Steam§r (bronze): fuel and water, 8 blocks/s, 4 cars.
• §6Fireless§r (industry): steam reservoir filled at the §6steam charger§r, 10 blocks/s, 6 cars, short range: ideal in factories.
• §6Diesel§r (chemistry): diesel, biodiesel, renewable diesel, kerosene, fuel oil or LNG at the §6fuel pump§r; 14 blocks/s, 8 cars.
• §6Gas§r (chemistry): natural gas, methane, propane, butane, biogas or §lhydrogen§r (×1.5 efficiency, no smoke); 14 blocks/s, 8 cars.
• §6Electric§r (atom): catenary, third rail or MKIV track; backup battery charged under the wire and when braking; 22 blocks/s, 12 cars.
• §6Nuclear§r (atom): one §lfuel assembly§r (uranium or MOX) lasts a very long time, the spent one goes back to the shielded station for reprocessing; 22 blocks/s, 16 cars, no radiation.
• §6Maglev§r (space): levitates §lonly on MKIV track§r, which carries the energy; 34 blocks/s, 24 cars. A train with a maglev only looks for MKIV paths.
Several locomotives in one consist add up their power, at the front, the back or in the middle.

pages.title: Electrification
pages.text:
Electric locomotives take their energy from a §6substation§r, fed by the mod's logistic cables; its storage (8 M FE at MKI, ×8 per tier) is kept by the rail network, so trains draw it even far away.
• §6Catenary pole§r: placed by clicking the track; its bracket carries the wire over the neighboring track, which it covers over 6 blocks. Poles within 16 blocks of each other (and of the substation) form a §lgrid§r.
• §6Third rail§r: conductor rail beside the track, for tunnels and low lines; it covers its block and links every 3 blocks.
• §6MKIV track§r: it carries the energy itself: all MKIV track connected to a substation placed against it is live (it is the maglev's only track).
Under power the §lpantograph rises§r; off the wire, an electric locomotive runs on its battery.

pages.title: Cars and platform posts
pages.text:
One car per resource family of the mod (MKI to MKIV: ×2 capacity per tier), each with its §lplatform post§r, which serves the vehicle stopped in front of it:
• §6Tank car§r (16,000 mB) and §6gas tank car§r (32,000 mB): §6filling arm§r.
• §6Battery car§r (8 M FE): §6platform power socket§r; it also charges electric locomotives.
• §6Server car§r (data): §6platform data link§r. §6Compressed air car§r: §6pneumatic coupling§r.
• §6Flat car§r: one block on top, by the §6platform crane§r. §6Robot van§r: robotic units.
• §6Hopper car§r: §6loading silo§r from above, §6unloading pit§r under the track (click the track to place it underneath).
• §6Passenger car§r: two seats (right-click to sit); the §6passenger platform§r boards villagers.
Refueling: §6coaling tower§r and water crane (steam), steam charger, fuel pump, §6charging post§r, §6shielded fuel station§r.
Each post is set up like a machine (sides, input or output); those that can have a load / unload button.

pages.title: Signals and traffic
pages.text:
§lSwitches are always automatic§r: each train reserves the path ahead and the blades move on their own. A train §lalways§r stops behind another train, signal or not: trains never collide.
Signals split the line into §6blocks§r: one train per block. Place them §lby clicking the track§r, looking in the trains' direction: they go on their right. Hold a railroad item (track, signal, wrench…) to see the §ldirection§r of every signal and station: an arrow on the track (yellow: block, blue: chain, green: station).
• §6Block signal§r (semaphore): closes the next block while a train occupies or has reserved it.
• §6Chain signal§r (light): before a switch, crossing or station: only lets a train in if its §lwhole exit§r is clear (up to the next block signal). Nobody gets stuck in the middle of a junction.
A signal on one side only makes the track §lone-way§r for pathfinding. Blocked for more than 5 s, a train looks for another route.
Trains §lhit§r whatever stands on the track (damage by speed, knockback): look before crossing!

pages.title: Groups and interrupts
pages.text:
§6Group§r (Schedule tab of the sheet): trains in the same group §lshare their schedule§r and interrupts; editing one edits all the others (each keeps its stop). Ten ore trains, a single schedule to maintain.
§6Interrupts§r (tab of the same name): a §llibrary shared§r by every train in the world. An interrupt has conditions (“fuel ≤ 20 %”) and stops (“Fuel depot”, wait for “fuel ≥ 100 %”). Enabled on a train, it is checked at every departure (and when the train has found neither path nor room for 10 s): if its conditions are true, the train first visits its stops, then §lresumes its schedule§r where it was.
§6Wildcards§r: in an interrupt's station name, §l{item}§r, §l{fluid}§r or §l{gas}§r are replaced by the train's most abundant resource. Name your stations by resource (“+ res.” button of the sign: “Drain ‹Water›”) and a single “loaded → Drain {fluid}” interrupt sends each tank car to the right place.
Picking a station: the menu also offers “Type a name”, for wildcards and stations not built yet. The orange banner of the schedule shows the current temporary stops (Cancel: the train resumes its schedule).

pages.title: Logistic railroad
pages.text:
The §6dispatcher§r runs trains on its own, the way robots serve chests. On the station sign, Logistics column, give a §lrole§r:
• §6Depot§r: logistic trains wait there, empty.
• §6Supplies§r: the station offers what is on its platform (its loaders, over 48 blocks behind the sign, within 2 blocks of the track).
• §6Requests§r: the station keeps a §ltarget level§r of each listed resource; the shortfall (minus what is already on its way) beyond the threshold triggers a delivery.
• §6Both§r: exchange station.
Check §lLogistic train§r (Logistics tab of the sheet) and give the train a schedule that brings it to a depot. Every second, the dispatcher picks the free train nearest to the supplier (empty, suitable cars, fuel ≥ 20 %, in the group both stations allow): load the planned amount (or leave after 15 s of inactivity with a partial load), unload, go back to the depot. The loaders of these stations are §ldriven§r: they only load the delivery's resource and amount.
§lRobots§r: in a robotic network, the loaders of a supplying station are §lrequesters§r (robots bring what must stay on the platform) and those of a requesting station are §lunload points§r; the target stock then counts across the whole network. With §lTerminal orders§r, a station also requests what the network lacks for its §6logistic terminals§r' orders: the order arrives by train.

pages.title: The map and PioScript
Diagonals
pages.text:
A line can leave §lat 45°§r: place the tracks §las a staircase§r (one block ahead, one block aside, and so on). Automatic placement turns it into a straight §6diagonal§r from the middle of one block to the next, with §lno speed limit§r.
• At the end of a straight line, the staircase starts with a smooth §6transition§r curve over two blocks (10 blocks/s), and ends the same way against the next line.
• A staircase leaving §la line§r makes a §6diagonal switch§r; a staircase §lcrossing§r a line or another staircase makes a crossing (trains go straight on).
• A single curve between two straights stays a tight curve (6 blocks/s): shifting a line by one track with a staircase gives a nice S-curve.
Diagonals stay flat: climb before or after.

pages.title: Structures and railroad crossings
pages.text:
§6Railroad crossing§r: planked straight track you walk across. Place a §6crossing barrier§r on the road, on each side: it closes with a bell and red lights when a train is within 8 blocks, and then blocks the way.
§6Viaduct pillar§r: connects vertically (footing at the bottom, capital under the track); §6railing§r: connects like a fence.
§6Tunnel portal§r: place the masonry around a one-block-wide, two-high opening: jambs, lintel and keystone form by themselves.
§6Platform slab§r (half block, yellow line facing the track) and §6platform lamp§r.

pages.title: Laying out a line
pages.text:
§6Zone planner§r, §lRailroad§r tool (G key): click the ground at the start, then at the end.
