The gentlest route is laid out (45° headings, at least two straight blocks between turns, gentle slopes on straights), with real automatic placement: diagonals, transitions and slopes are already in the preview. Above ground: embankment, then §lviaduct§r (deck and a pillar every 4 blocks); below: a 3-block-high §lcut or tunnel§r. The job goes to the robots like any other job.
§lCopy and paste§r (planner, Paste tool): tracks turn with the paste, stations keep name, limit and logistics, posts their direction; each time a robot lays a track, the existing tracks around connect to it (switch, curve, slope, diagonal) while the job's tracks keep their planned shape; a track of the wrong shape is reshaped in place, never under a train.
§6Track layer§r: in a train stopped at the end of the line, it lays the job's blocks ahead (one every half second), with what is in its 18 slots; move forward and it carries on.
§6Railroad Works§r: a multiblock shaped like a real engine shed (9 × 11 footprint): floor slab, walls with frame pillars, gabled roof with a lantern, a large door where the track comes in; inside, the vehicle being built stands on the pit track under the overhead crane. It builds §levery vehicle§r, from the draisine and the mine cart to MKIV locomotives: since 1.0.4, none is made at a bench.

pages.title: Merchant shipping
pages.text:
On the water, §lreal ships§r several blocks long carry your goods from one §6harbor§r to another. A ship carries §la single resource§r: passengers, items, a fluid, a gas, energy, compressed air or data.

Like trains, they are §lautomatic§r: a schedule (a list of harbors and when to leave them), automatic mode, and the ship §lfinds its own route on the water§r, sails around islands, docks along the quay, then sets off again. They keep sailing when nobody is around.

pages.title: The seven ships
pages.text:
Their holds are those of the §lcars of the same tier§r (2 holds at MKI, 4, 6, then 8 at MKIV):
• §6Ferry§r: 4 to 16 seated passengers (players and villagers).
• §6Cargo ship§r: 18 to 432 item slots.
• §6Tanker§r: one fluid, 32,000 to 1,024,000 mB.
• §6Gas carrier§r: one gas in its spheres, 64,000 to 2,048,000 mB.
• §6Power barge§r: 16 M to 512 M FE.
• §6Compressed air carrier§r: 4,000 to 128,000 L.
• §6Data ship§r: data, 8 M to 256 M MB.
Right-click a ship: its §lsheet§r (schedule, engines and holds, inventory of each hold); three hits: it turns back into an item, contents included.

pages.title: Propulsion and tiers
pages.text:
Each tier is bigger, faster and runs on a different energy:
• §6MKI paddle steamer§r (8 × 2 blocks, 3 blocks/s): solid fuel in its bunker (sea water feeds the boiler).
• §6MKII diesel§r (10 × 3, 5 blocks/s): diesel, biodiesel, kerosene, fuel oil or LNG, like locomotives.
• §6MKIII electric§r (12 × 3, 7 blocks/s): two motors and their batteries, §lrecharged at the harbor§r.
• §6MKIV nuclear§r (16 × 4, 9 blocks/s): fuel assemblies; spent ones are taken back at the harbor. Its tungsten hull holds on the §llava seas§r of Venus, TRAPPIST-1b and Proxima d.
Docked, the engine rests; at anchor, it idles.

pages.title: The harbor
pages.text:
The harbor is a §lU-shaped basin§r of §6quay slabs§r: the §6harbor office§r (MKI to MKIV harbor block) in the middle of the far end, two parallel arms reaching into the water. The ship §lsails into the basin§r, in line with the office. Like any multiblock, the shape is §lfixed§r, but the §ltier of the office§r sets it: a 3-wide basin with 9-block arms for a MKI, 5 × 11 (MKII), 5 × 13 (MKIII), 5 × 17 (MKIV). The basin opens §lbehind§r the office (its front faces the land); the walls of the U are §l3 blocks high§r (the top level with the office, two rows below, under it too); the whole basin in open water (two blocks deep, nothing above). Slabs connect by themselves: yellow band and fenders along the water edges, plain wall under another slab. A §6harbor interface§r, placed instead of any slab, gives access to the harbor office's stock through all its faces: logistic cables plug into it. The office shows the §lfirst cell to fix§r (missing slab or dry cell). §lEquipment§r replaces slabs, facing the ship.
§lSneak + right-click§r the harbor office with an empty hand: the §lbasin blueprint§r sized for its tier; a second sneak + right-click hides it (in creative, holding the office builds it). A §6water bucket§r emptied on a steamer fills its boiler.
Right-click: stock (9 slots, fluid, gas, energy, data, air), §lLoad / Unload§r button, §lSheet§r button (name, limit, logistics).

pages.title: Dock equipment
pages.text:
Each resource only goes through §lits equipment§r, placed instead of a slab (on an arm of the U) and connected to cables (it gives access to the harbor office’s stock):
• §6Dock crane§r: items; the jib swings to the ship and shuttles a container back and forth.
• §6Loading arm§r, §6gas§r, §6compressed air§r: they land on the ship’s deck.
• §6Dock charger§r: the barge’s energy and electric ships’ batteries.
• §6Data mast§r: beam to the data ship. §6Gangway§r: the ferry’s villagers.
• §6Bunkering station§r: solid fuel, liquid fuel and assemblies for the engines.
Two pieces of the same kind double the rate (four at most). Without equipment, nothing goes through.

pages.title: Navigation
Sea beacons
pages.text:
For §llong trips§r and continents to sail around, place §6sea beacons§r (lit buoys, on water like a lily pad, or on a rock) and §llink them yourself§r with the §6navigation chart§r: right-click a beacon, then the next one (chain A → B → C; clicking a link again removes it; 6,000 blocks at most).
• Each link becomes a §lsea lane§r charted offshore (computed once, the player is told the result); the map (O key) shows them in blue, beacons as yellow diamonds.
• A ship that §lsees a beacon§r (256 blocks) from where it starts knows the destinations of its network: it joins it, follows the links to the beacon closest to its harbor, then finishes the route on its own.
• Right-click a beacon with an empty hand: its links and the harbors reachable through its network.
Tip: one beacon in front of each harbor, and one at each cape or strait along the way.

pages.title: Schedules and logistics
pages.text:
The ship sheet is the trains' one: §lschedule§r (harbors and conditions: time, inactivity, full, empty, fuel, passengers, harbor stock…), §lsend§r to a harbor, and §6logistic§r service.
Logistics (like the railroad): a logistic ship waits §lempty at a Depot harbor§r. When a harbor that §lrequests§r lacks a resource that a harbor §lsupplies§r, the dispatcher sends the ship of the right kind to load, deliver, then come back.
Logistic harbors become §6robotic network points§r: robots bring goods to the supplying harbor and empty the requesting one. A mining island thus connects itself to the factory.

pages.title: The shipyard
pages.text:
Every ship is made at the §6Shipyard§r (since 1.0.4, none at a bench): a steel hull, an engine and §ltwo cars§r of the resource for the holds; each tier builds on the previous ship. §lWooden boats§r (all 8 woods), §lchest boats§r and §lbamboo rafts§r are made at the shipyard §land§r at the §6carpenter’s bench§r (1.0.5): 5 planks of their wood for a boat (saw), the boat and a chest for a chest boat (hammer); never at the vanilla crafting table nor in any other machine.
It is a §ldry dock§r multiblock (a 9 × 17 block basin) where you watch the ship grow on its keel blocks, the gantry roll overhead and the welders at work.

pages.title: The Voltaic set
pages.text:
Between metal armor and modular gear: the §lVoltaic§r set, fully electric, no modules. It is built in the MKI §6Assembler (components)§r around a §6voltaic cell§r (lead-acid batteries, coils, MKI circuit).
§lArmor§r: §l21§r while powered (3 / 8 / 7 / 3, toughness 2.5), above hardened steel and titanium; drained, it falls back to 18 (steel) and loses its effects, but never breaks.
• §6Helmet§r: night vision in the dark (5 FE/t).
• §6Chestplate§r: energized plating (1 FE/t).
• §6Leggings§r: +10% speed (3 FE/t while walking).
• §6Boots§r: half of the fall damage avoided (100 FE per point).
Each piece stores 250,000 FE.

pages.title: Voltaic tools
pages.text:
Speed §l10§r (diamond: 8) at diamond level, §l100 FE per block§r, 250,000 FE; drained, they mine at fist speed.
• §6Drill§r: pickaxe and shovel in one; right-click: path.
• §6Chainsaw§r: an axe that fells the whole tree (sneak: one block); right-click: strip.
• §6Hedge Trimmer§r: hoe and shears (leaves, wool, cobwebs), shears sheep; right-click: till. 50 FE per block.
• §6Shock Baton§r: 7 damage and a shock (slowness and weakness for 2 s) for 250 FE; drained, 3 damage.
Graviton is crafted §lfrom§r the armor, the drill (pickaxe), the chainsaw (axe), the hedge trimmer (hoe) and the baton (blade): the energy carries over to the Graviton piece.

pages.title: The hydrogen jetpack
pages.text:
It is worn §lin place of the chestplate§r. A §l24,000 mB§r hydrogen tank and a 500,000 FE battery.
• In the air, §lhold jump§r: thrust (moving forward adds speed); 160 mB/s + 500 FE/s, about 2 min 30 per tank.
• Mode key (§6Z§r): §lhover§r: in the air without jumping you keep your altitude; sneak to go down slowly; 80 mB/s + 240 FE/s.
Empty tank or battery: thrust stops (mind the fall). Bottom left: energy and hydrogen gauges, and the jetpack state.
Hydrogen comes from the §6electrolyzer§r (water) or from refinery gases.

pages.title: The flamethrower
pages.text:
§lHold right-click§r: a §l6-block§r cone of flame. Creatures hit (in line of sight) burn for 4 s and take fire damage. An 8,000 mB tank and a 200,000 FE battery; 200 mB/s + 800 FE/s (40 s per tank). Nothing comes out underwater.
Blocks: only a targeted §lflammable§r block can catch fire, and only if the §lmobGriefing§r rule is true (config option “flamethrowerIgnitesBlocks”); the jet never breaks anything. In a clan §6claim§r, you need the right to build there to ignite, and the right to hit animals there.

pages.title: Charging and filling
pages.text:
§lEnergy§r: put the item in the top slot of an §6energy buffer§r: it charges, then moves to the bottom slot (2,500 FE/t for a Voltaic piece). The §6Modulation Bench§r charges too.
§lHydrogen§r: the top slot of a §6gas buffer§r full of hydrogen fills the jetpack and the flamethrower; or pick up a hydrogen §6capsule§r and drop it onto the item in your inventory (1,000 mB, the empty capsule comes back).
Tooltip: energy, hydrogen and consumption of each item.

pages.title: Modular gear
pages.text:
Beyond metal armor: four §lmodular sets§r, each with its armor, its tools, a §6blade§r and a §6plasma rifle§r. Everything runs on §lenergy (FE)§r: nothing wears out, but an empty piece loses its modules and an empty tool mines like a fist.
Each item has §lslots§r where you install §6modules§r (night vision, thrusters, flight, shield, excavation…) at the §6Modulation Bench§r, which also recharges the item.

pages.title: The four tiers
pages.text:
• §6Graviton§r (MKI, titanium alloys and nitinol): 3 slots, 1 M FE per item, armor 24 (toughness 3.5), separate tools.
• §6Stellaris§r (MKII, tungsten carbide, osmiridium, stellite): 4 slots, 4 M FE, armor 25 (toughness 4.5).
• §6Neutronic§r (MKIII, lunar alloy, meteoritite, sputnikite): 6 slots, 16 M FE, armor 26 (toughness 5.5), the §lmultitool§r, and the §lflight module§r.
• §6Singularity§r (MKIV, neutronium, quasar crystal, singularity cell): 8 slots, 64 M FE, armor 27 (toughness 6.5).
A module has a maximum level, capped at II on MKI and III on MKII. The armor counts as a §lspace suit§r of the same tier (1 to 4).

pages.title: The Modulation Bench
pages.text:
Put the item in the top slot, a module in the bottom one, then §lInstall§r: one module per level (two thruster modules = thrusters II). The screen lists the installed modules: §lON / OFF§r switches them without removing them, §l–§r removes one level (the module comes back).
The bench connects to logistic cables (or a battery in its slot) and recharges the item up to 20,000 FE/t.
Anywhere else, the §6G§r key opens the screen of worn modules: a click switches a module on or off.

pages.title: Helmet and chestplate modules
pages.text:
Helmet: §6night vision§r; §6air recycler§r (breathe underwater and in vacuum); §6entity detector§r (12 blocks per level); §6nutrient synthesizer§r (MKII+); §6photovoltaic skin§r (recharges in sunlight).
Chestplate: §6back thrusters§r (I to IV); §6stellar flight§r (MKIII+); §6energy shield§r (20% of damage per level); §6repair nanites§r (MKII+); §6thermal coating§r (fire and lava); §6gravity magnet§r (4 blocks per level, off while sneaking).

pages.title: Leg and foot modules
pages.text:
Leggings: §6servo motors§r (+15% speed per level: the “fast runners”); §6step assist§r (walks up one-block steps); §6hydro-thrusters§r (+60% swim speed per level).
Boots: §6jump springs§r; §6gravity dampers§r (no fall damage while energy lasts); §6kinetic generator§r (recharges the armor as you walk).
Anywhere: §6composite plating§r (+1 armor per level, even without energy) and §6auxiliary cell§r (+50% capacity per level, tools too).

pages.title: Tools, blade and rifle
pages.text:
Graviton and Stellaris have a §lpickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe§r; Neutronic and Singularity merge them into a §6multitool§r (right-click: strip or path; sneaking: till). 250 FE per block.
Tool modules: §6excavation§r 3 × 3 then 5 × 5 (sneak: one block), §6overclock§r, §6quantum fortune§r, §6silk touch§r, §6instant smelting§r, §6loot teleporter§r, §6telescopic arm§r.
§6Blade§r (600 FE per hit): plasma edge, vampirism, loot collector. §6Plasma rifle§r (2,000 FE per shot, held two-handed): overcharge, volley, rapid fire.

pages.title: Flying and surviving
pages.text:
§6Back thrusters§r: in the air, §lhold jump§r = thrust (stronger each level, moving forward adds speed); 40 FE/t per level, blue flames on your back.
§6Stellar flight§r (Neutronic or Singularity chestplate): free creative-style flight, §ldouble jump§r to take off; level II is faster; 80 FE/t while flying. Out of energy: you fall, dampers help.
In space, the §6air recycler§r lets you breathe on the helmet’s energy (its reserve shows in place of oxygen); the armor protects like a suit of its tier.
Bottom left: one energy gauge per worn piece.

pages.title: Upgrading your gear
pages.text:
Each tier is made with its §6plating§r and §6energy cell§r; one tier’s cell goes into the next one’s.
From Stellaris on, a piece is crafted §lfrom the previous tier’s piece§r (in the middle of the grid): it §lkeeps its modules, their settings and its energy§r. The Neutronic multitool needs the four Stellaris tools and takes over the pickaxe’s modules.
Modules are crafted on a §6module frame§r (titanium, circuit, chip) with their components.

pages.title: First launch: the initiation
pages.text:
The first time you enter a world, a full-screen cover page opens, in two steps:
1. §lYour name§r: your username is suggested; 24 characters at most (letters, digits, space, hyphen, apostrophe, period).
2. §lYour trade§r: eleven vocation cards (ten if the economy is off); hover over a card to read its affinities, advantage and drawback on the right. The §6Jack-of-All-Trades§r has none of these.
Then comes a page to read to the very end: the §lYes§r button only turns on at the bottom. Read, then say yes.

Until you say yes nothing can hurt you, and the screen comes back if it is closed; logging out resumes at the current step. The server checks the name and the vocation. Your face, beard and hair are your skin's; clothes are made at the tanner's bench. Then: the notebook in your bag, a first line in its log.

pages.title: The notebook tabs
pages.text:
• §6Profile§r: at the top, your portrait, name, vocation (advantage and flaw), clan and role; §ltiles§r for the key numbers (days, levels, Shining, Masteries, texts read); your three best skills and your Masteries; then the §lnotebook log§r (day in the margin). Hover a tile for its explanation.
• §6Skills§r: the seventeen skills, their level as a number, the XP “current / next level” and the bar; at the bottom, the current effect and the next level's for the hovered skill.
• §6Codex§r: everything you have read, by chapter (archive pages, memory modules, the Trades), and the §lScattered Notes§r of parchment notes.
• §6Reputation§r: each people, its tier and gauge; its card tells its §lrole§r, a fragment of its §lorigin§r, §lwhat it likes and dislikes§r (the deeds that raise or lower its reputation, with the points) and what it §ltrades§r; Changes and Known villages chips.
• §6Exchange§r: your Shining balance, your latest transactions, transfers.
• §6Documents§r: your documents with other players or clans (invoices, contracts, letters, quotes, receipts…; sign, pay installments, print).

The notebook does not judge. It copies.

pages.title: The Rule of the Hand
pages.text:
A Restorer learns by doing, not by watching.
• §lBy hand§r (breaking, placing, striking, forging, harvesting, cooking, driving…): §l100%§r of the XP.
• §lThrough your machines, robots and programs§r: §l20%§r, if you are online within 32 blocks, the machine is yours and the action succeeds; at most §l300 XP§r per skill per game day.
• §lFatigue§r: past 30 identical actions per minute, XP drops to 50%; past 60, to 10%. The same action at the same spot only counts once a day.
• §lAffinity§r: the two skills of your vocation gain XP × 1.5.
• §lBrigade§r: with pioneers of other vocations within 24 blocks, +5% per different vocation, +15% at most, on hand actions.
Nothing in creative mode. Automation stays whole: it just teaches you less.

pages.title: Skills and Mastery
pages.text:
Sixteen skills, one per major activity: Building, Mining, Smithing, Engineering, Robotics, Farming, Husbandry, Fishing, Cooking, Combat, Logistics, Salvage, Restoration, Spaceflight, Nuclear and Trade (with the economy on).
• Each goes from 0 to 10. Reaching level n costs §l100 × n§r XP: 5,500 XP in all for level 10.
• Its bonuses grow by a tenth per level, full value at level 10. They make the §laction§r more efficient (speed, wear, delays); none goes above 25%.
• Nothing is locked: every activity stays open at level 0.
• At level 10, §6Mastery§r: a title (“Mastery of Smithing”), a colored clasp on the notebook, a line in the log. No extra power.
XP comes from the trade's actions: an ore mined (1), a dish finished (5), a Sentinel defeated (40), a structure completed (50), a restoration finished (200)…

pages.title: What skills give
pages.text:
Values at level 10, a tenth per level:
• §lBuilding§r: robot work on your plans +25%, placement reach +1 block.
• §lMining§r: speed +20%, pickaxe wear −15%.
• §lSmithing§r: metal cooling −25%, loss per anvil hit −25%.
• §lEngineering§r: tool and wrench wear −25%, up to a 25% chance to keep an upgrade kit.
• §lRobotics§r: Data Link Tool range +25%, operations per work plan +20%.
• §lFarming§r: hand harvesting and sowing +25%, hoe wear −20%.
• §lHusbandry§r: feeding and milking +25%, delay between births −20%.
• §lFishing§r: bite delay −25%, reeling in +20%.

pages.title: What skills give (continued)
pages.text:
• §lCooking§r: preparing by hand +25%, dish effect duration +20%.
• §lCombat§r: damage dealt +15%, damage taken from Sentinels −25%.
• §lLogistics§r: speed of driven trains +15%; from level 1, sneak + right-click with a wrench copies a machine's sides, then pastes them on another of the same block.
• §lSalvage§r: breaking derelict blocks +25%, scrap sorting by your recyclers +25%.
• §lRestoration§r: site cost −20%, duration −25%; level 3 to open an MKII site, 6 for an MKIII.
• §lSpaceflight§r: oxygen use −20%, fuel for hand-flown launches −10%.
• §lNuclear§r: radiation exposure −25%, decontamination +25%.
• §lTrade§r: NPC purchase quotas +25%, stall tax −2.5 points, +3 listings per stall (+9 per counter).

pages.title: Vocations
pages.text:
A vocation is a way of life, not a class. It gives an §laffinity§r (its two skills gain XP × 1.5), an §ladvantage§r (what the skill does not give) and a light, logical §ldrawback§r, 15% at most. Nothing is ever locked.
• §6Builder§r (Building, Mining): −10% materials for structures, and a structure's plan lists what is missing; hunger drops 15% faster while placing or breaking.
• §6Miner-Smelter§r (Mining, Smithing): light night vision below level 40, +10% chance of an extra nugget from an ore; blurred vision for 3 s when stepping out into daylight.
• §6Engineer§r (Engineering, Nuclear): reads the efficiency, losses and bottleneck of any machine, no tool needed; damage taken +10%.
• §6Logistician§r (Logistics, Robotics): wrench in hand, rails, cables and robots highlighted within 16 blocks; damage dealt −10%.
• §6Farmer§r (Farming, Cooking): +15% chance of an extra harvest, +10% seeds from their own crops; mining −10%.

pages.title: Vocations (continued)
pages.text:
• §6Herder-Angler§r (Husbandry, Fishing): fishing rods, shears and buckets never wear out, +10% chance of twins or an extra rare catch; at the Assembly Bench, 10% chance of wearing the tool by one extra point.
• §6Scout§r (Combat, Salvage, Hunting: the only vocation with three affinities): hostile creatures and Sentinels spot them 25% closer; a restoration costs them 10% more.
• §6Salvager§r (Salvage, Restoration): derelict blocks glow faintly within 24 blocks, +25% recycling draws; radiation and fume exposure +15%.
• §6Astronaut§r (Spaceflight, Nuclear): 10 more seconds without oxygen before taking damage; cooked dishes fill 15% less.
• §6Trader§r (Trade, Logistics; with the economy on): −10% when buying and +10% when selling with villagers and Peddlers; hostile creatures and Sentinels spot them 15% farther.
• §6Jack-of-All-Trades§r (no affinity): no advantage, no drawback, everything is learned at the same pace. It counts in a brigade as one more vocation; leaving it at the Desk costs no XP.
The drawbacks answer each other: everyone needs someone. Alone, nothing is blocked; in a group, the brigade rewards variety.

pages.title: Your appearance
pages.text:
Your face, beard and hair are your §lskin§r's: the mod leaves them alone.
• §lClothes§r: 20 outfits of 4 pieces (headwear, top, bottoms, footwear), made at the §6Tanner's Bench§r and worn in the inventory's §lcosmetic panel§r. They protect against nothing.
• §lArmor or costume§r: one switch per piece shows the garment or the worn armor; the armor protects either way.
• §lNotebook clasp§r: one per mastered skill. The only one you have to earn.
A client option hides the clothes of others, or your own. Details: the “Mechanics: Tools and benches” chapter.

Dressing as an Astronaut does not make you fly.

pages.title: The Restorer's Desk and changing vocation
pages.text:
You do not rewrite a notebook. You can only turn one of its pages, at the §6Restorer's Desk§r (Carpenter's Bench: 6 planks, 2 wooden slabs, 1 Blank Notebook, with a saw).
• §lCost§r: a §6Blank Notebook§r (8 paper, 2 leather, 1 string) and §l5,000 Shining§r. With the economy off: the Blank Notebook, 16 MKIII scrap of at least 4 kinds and 4 components of the most advanced age you have reached.
• §lExperience§r: −25% XP on the two skills of the old vocation (nothing when leaving the Jack-of-All-Trades). Levels may drop; Masteries, clasps and the log remain.
• §lTime§r: 30 game days before the next change.
Pick the card, type its name, then “Turn the page” twice. The ceremony lasts §l10 s§r: one hit taken or four steps too far, and nothing is taken.

pages.title: Shining and the Exchange
pages.text:
The currency is the §6service Shining§r: an old Stewardship account unit, one Shining for one service rendered. No one mints them anymore. There is §lno Shining item§r: it is a balance, written in your notebook.
• It starts at 0, is never negative, is not lost on death; one billion at most.
• §lYou earn§r them by selling: to a villager, to a Peddler, or through your stalls (other players pay you).
• §lYou spend§r them on: purchases, changing vocation (5,000), a restoration's cash share, stall tax (5%), village workers (20 a day).
• The notebook's §6Exchange§r tab shows the balance, the latest transactions and the §lSend§r button; or §l/pay <player> <amount>§r. Both players online, no fee, 50,000 Shining a day at most.
The server computes everything; a trade happens whole or not at all. No clink of coins: money is a written line.

pages.title: Prices, simply
pages.text:
Prices are §lfixed§r: the same item is worth the same everywhere, every day.
• §lBase value§r: 1 iron ingot = 4 Shining, the reference for the whole table. A crafted item is worth its ingredients, a little more at each age.
• §lPartner§r: a villager buys from you at 50% and sells to you at 120%; a Peddler, 60% and 130%.
• §lModifiers§r: the people's reputation, the villager's affinity, the Trader's Haggling; they add up and are then §lcapped§r: never under 85% of the base when buying, never over 120% of the selling price.
• §lEvents§r: Shortage and Surplus go past the caps.
• §lQuotas§r: each merchant only buys, per day, 64 units of a raw material, 16 of a crafted item, 4 of a component, 1 MKIII scrap. The price does not drop: they simply have enough.
Buying, crafting and selling back never makes money in a loop. Prices are shown with their percentage.

pages.title: Peddlers
pages.text:
The third people: they know the Ways, count everything and laugh at the rest. They replace the wandering trader.
• §lOn the road§r: each morning, a 20% chance that a Peddler and their two llamas show up 24-40 blocks from you, preferably near an old Way (mod rail, path, quay). They stay three days.
• §lIn a caravan§r: the Caravan event sets two Peddlers and their crates on a village square for three days.
• §lAt Halts§r: a permanent camp on an old Way, roughly every 1,500 blocks, with two Peddlers.
They sell about ten lots drawn at each visit: materials, tools up to the Bronze Age, a few MKI and MKII scrap. They buy almost anything at 60%, scrap included, except components and machines: you do not buy your progression step.
Killing a Peddler: −100 with the Peddlers, none on your road for 20 days, and no caravan within 500 blocks of you. The books are the books.

pages.title: Stalls and counters
pages.text:
A stall §lsells for you§r, day and night, for Shining.
• §6Market Stall§r (Carpenter's Bench: planks, slabs, 2 canvas, with a saw): 9 listings, 27 stock slots. §6Market Counter§r (Carpenter's Bench: wood, 3 bronze plates, 2 canvas): 27 listings, 54 slots. Four stalls and two counters per player per world.
• Right-click: the listings (item, lot size from 1 to 64, lot price in whole Shining, between 25% and 400% of its value). Shift + right-click empty-handed: the stock. The mod's logistic cables can fill it: your factory keeps shop.
• Each sale takes a §l5% tax§r, which vanishes; you get the rest, even while away (a message tells you how much when you return).
• Only the owner sets up, empties or breaks their stall. Placed in a clan's territory near a Market, it also pays that clan's market tax (“Clans” chapter).
The Trade skill lowers the tax and adds listings. The Trader's Haggling does not apply here: between players, the gain stays between players.

pages.title: The village sale bin
pages.text:
No time to visit every villager's stall? Place a §6Village Sale Bin§r on the square (within 32 blocks of the bell; one per player per village; Carpenter's Bench: planks, slabs, canvas, iron nuggets, with a saw).
• Fill it like a §llarge chest§r (54 slots): by hand, hopper, cable or robot. Nothing comes out of its sides; only you open and break it.
• Every night at §lmidnight§r, the village buys what a Peddler would buy (no components or machines, nothing damaged, renamed or enchanted), at §l70% of a villager's price§r (35% of the value), with no reputation or Haggling bonus, and at most twice a villager's quota per kind of item. The rest waits for the next night.
• The Shining go to your account (clan tax included), even while you are away; the §lvillage's reputation§r rises by 1 per 200 Shining, §l3 at most per night§r (if you are away: on your next visit to the bin).
• Trading face to face still pays more: 50% instead of 35%, reputation discounts, and up to +5 affinity per villager per day, plus the peoples' deeds. The bin is for the surplus.

pages.title: Villages and peoples
pages.text:
When you come within 96 blocks of a village's bell, it is recorded; the notebook's Reputation tab shows the ten nearest known villages. Each village belongs to §lone people§r, drawn from the world seed:
• §6Bare Hands§r (half of the villages): they refuse machines. They only trade in field and livestock goods, wood, wooden and stone tools; no scrap, no worked metal, no component. Ash-gray banners.
• §6Restorers§r (three in ten): your tribe. Always a Librarian; they pay 25% more for paper and ink, and take no scrap or component. Ink-blue banners.
• §6Peddlers§r (two in ten): way-station villages, which also buy MKI and MKII scrap and see caravans more often. Verdigris banners.
On the first visit, a §lsquare§r is laid out in one piece near the bell, facing it: the §6Needs Board§r at the back, facing the bell; a dry §6fountain§r in the middle; two unlit §6lampposts§r on either side; four banners on their poles at the corners. Never on a path, a field, water or a hole, never against a house. If space runs short, there are fewer pieces, the Board first. A ruin restored nearby will bring fountain and lampposts back to life. These blocks can also be crafted (Board and Peddler Crate at the carpenter, fountain at the mason, lamppost at the metalworker).

pages.title: Founding your village
pages.text:
Place a §6Needs Board§r (Carpenter's Bench) and the village becomes yours: it is the §lheart of the village§r.
• Far from any village: a village is born there, “§l<your name>'s Village§r”, over a §l64-block radius§r around the Board. In a village without a founder (the NPC ones): it becomes yours. In another player's village: nothing, it already has its founder.
• Villagers who §llive§r in the radius (their bed, otherwise their workstation) become your villagers, and so do those born or settling there later. They keep their name, their people and their affinity.
• Each other §6Board§r, §6fountain§r or §6lamppost§r placed in the radius grows the village by 4 blocks, up to 96.
• For you alone, in your village: §lpurchases 15% cheaper§r, §lsales paid 15% more§r, and every §laffinity gain ×1.5§r (rounded up: a sale bin gives 2 instead of 1). Losses do not change; nothing changes for other players.
• A renamed §6name tag§r used on the Board renames the village (only you). The name shows on the Board and in the notebook's Reputation tab.

pages.title: Villagers
pages.text:
Every villager has a §lname§r, their village's §lpeople§r, a §lprofession§r and an §laffinity§r toward you. Right-click opens their sheet: §6Trade§r, §6Talk§r, §6Show the notebook§r. Trading and talking happen in the same sheet: their answer is written in the dialog panel, under their name, with what they have said since the visit began (the mouse wheel scrolls). Nothing goes to the chat.
• Thirteen Minecraft professions trade, depending on the people: Armorer, Butcher, Cartographer, Cleric, Farmer, Fisherman, Fletcher, Leatherworker, Librarian, Mason, Shepherd, Toolsmith, Weaponsmith.
• The §lToolsmith repairs§r, the §lWeaponsmith sharpens§r: a third of the item's value, half price at the Memories tier.
• The §6Nitwit§r does not trade, only talks; the §6Idler§r is waiting for a workstation.
• §lShowing the notebook§r (Snippets tier or higher, once): +5, +15 for a Librarian; doubled among the Restorers, nothing among the Bare Hands.
Professions from other mods keep their original screen. With the economy off, villagers go back to Minecraft's trades.

pages.title: Affinity
pages.text:
A number from −100 to +100, per villager and per player. §lIt never moves on its own§r: no forgiving, no forgetting.
• Hostile (−60 and below): refuses to talk (their sheet is only an insult), runs at the sight of you and calls the golem. Scornful (−59 to −20): dry scorn, no more trading, keeps their distance. Reserved (−19 to −1): cold.
• Gestures (0), Snippets (20, −3% when buying), Tales (40, −5%), Memories (60, −7%, repairs at half price), Confidences (80, −8%).
§lWhat raises it§r: Talk, +2 once a day (+3 with the Archives service); a trade of at least 100 Shining, +1, five times a day; showing the notebook; a raid fought off, +15 for the village; a ruin restored within 400 blocks, +10; a Standby, +3 a day.
§lWhat lowers it§r: a hit, −30 (and −10 for those who see it); breaking their bed or workstation, −10; killing a village golem, −40 for the whole village; killing a villager, −100 for the whole village and −20 for villages of the same people within 200 blocks.
Below −20, Talk earns nothing anymore: trust is won back through what touches the whole village, or by making amends (page “Making amends”).

pages.title: Talk, sayings and Confidences
pages.text:
Villagers do not tell the lore. They talk about the weather, the crops, the night coming; they scorn or insult those they hate.
• At the Snippets tier or higher, one time in four, a §6saying§r of their people: one vague sentence, six per people, that explains nothing. The Nitwit lets them slip from the first tier.
• The village's event, its services and your vocation sometimes color the answer.
• §6Confidences§r (80 or more): §lonly once§r, a concrete secret: the location of a nearby ruin, the §lConsole code§r of the nearest ruin, or a cache buried within 200 blocks (scrap; rare seeds among the Bare Hands). The Nitwit gives one more, always a ruin. The coordinates are written in the notebook log.
Nothing is locked: these secrets exist elsewhere. Affinity only makes them easier to find.

“Wheat doesn't say hmm.”

pages.title: The Needs Board and services
pages.text:
The §6Needs Board§r, on the square, has two tabs. §lNotices§r: the current event, the five services, the five players who did the most for the village; workers are hired there. §lAmends§r: the amends and tasks of a village that holds something against you (page “Making amends”). Every three days, a 25% chance of an §levent§r: §6Shortage§r (the village pays double for one item, double quota, 5 days), §6Surplus§r (it sells one at 60%, 5 days) or §6Caravan§r (3 days).
A ruin restored within 400 blocks gives a §lservice§r to the nearest village, as long as it stands:
• §6Water§r: the fountain runs; quotas for crops, fish and wool ×1.5.
• §6Energy§r: the lampposts light up at night; no more monsters spawn under the open sky within 48 blocks of the square; repairs −25%.
• §6Workshop§r: the Armorer, the smiths and the Mason sell MKI-age tools and parts (not among the Bare Hands); one free repair a day at the Tales tier.
• §6Warehouse§r: quotas of the whole village doubled; two events at once.
• §6Archives§r: Talk gives +1 more; the Cartographer sells the Ruin Map, the Librarian the manuals.

pages.title: Manuals, maps, workers and golems
pages.text:
• §6Manuals§r (200 Shining): one per Trade. The first reading files its entry in the Codex and gives, once, XP in the first skill of its vocation: never more than one level. It is the only XP you can buy.
• §6Ruin Map§r: unfolded for the first time, it records the three nearest ruins and copies them into the log; read again, it repeats their direction.
• §6Workers§r: during a restoration site within 100 blocks of the village, hire at the Board up to four Masons, Toolsmiths, Weaponsmiths or Armorers at the Tales tier (Snippets if you are an Ally of the people). Each one cuts 10% of the remaining duration and costs 20 Shining a day (10 once the village average reaches +40). Empty balance: they do not work, at no cost. The Bare Hands refuse.
• §lThe village average§r: at +40, your name on the Board; at +60, its golems ignore your hits and help you fight; at −40, no one trades anymore and the golems attack on sight. A Hostile villager who sees you calls the golem; a blow struck in front of a golem makes it charge.

pages.title: Reputation with the peoples
pages.text:
Two scales judge you: each §lvillage§r, by the average affinity of its villagers (a stranger counts as 0), and each §lpeople§r, from −300 to +300.
• §6Hostile§r (−200 and below): trade refused, all its villagers flee, its golems attack. §6Wary§r (−199 to −60): +10% when buying, −10% when selling. §6Unknown§r (−59 to 59). §6Esteemed§r (60 to 149): −5% / +5%, and an exclusive stock (manuals at the Restorers' Librarian; seeds, compost and tools at the Bare Hands' Farmers, Shepherds and Fishermen; the Ruin Map at the Peddlers' Cartographer). §6Ally§r (150 and up): −10% / +10%.
• §lActs§r: dismantling a ruin, destroying a Sentinel (Bare Hands and Peddlers +6); restoring (Restorers +20, Bare Hands −15); a Standby (Restorers +6); selling scrap for 100 Shining or more (Peddlers +6, Bare Hands −6); delivering farm goods for as much (Bare Hands +3); reading a page (Restorers +1); killing a villager (−10 everywhere, −60 more with their people); killing a Peddler (−100).
Gains are capped at 30 points per people per day; losses never are. Time forgives nothing: only acts count. To make up for a wrong: page “Making amends”.

pages.title: Making amends
pages.text:
Time forgives nothing. Acts, sometimes. Three ways to make up for a wrong, all possible even at the Hostile tier, all under the cap of §l+30 points per people per day§r. They make up, they don't make friends: a gain stops at 0.
• §6Amends§r (Amends tab of the Board in one of their villages): pay in Shining, or deliver the goods the village asks for (the current Shortage if it fits). +10 with the people, +5 with each angry villager. The price follows the hatred: 50 + depth² / 40 Shining (140 at −60, 1,050 at −200, 2,300 at −300; a village average of −100 counts as −300), doubled for the second one of the day; two a day per people.
• §6Peddler envoy§r (§lShift + right-click§r on a Peddler): he carries an offering to an angry people (amends × 1.5), which arrives §l2 days§r later: +15. One sent a day, one envoy per people. Refused if the Peddlers hold you Hostile; they don't make up with themselves through one of their own.
• §6Tasks§r on the Board, one at a time: deliver a quantity of a good (+12 / +6), hold the square for a night and kill 3 monsters there (+15 / +8), put 6 plots of the fields back under crops (+10 / +6), fight off a raid (+25 / +10, within 5 days).
§lWhite flag§r: a white banner in hand calms the village golems near the Board and during one of its tasks. A blow struck at a villager or a golem breaks it for the day.

pages.title: Notebook documents
Contracts and invoices
pages.text:
A §6contract§r sells your time or your work to another player, in §lreal time§r (the server's clock; its time zone is shown). Notebook (J), §6Documents§r tab, “+ New”, Contract type, “Real-time contract…” (1.0.5: the other documents, page “Notebook documents”):
• a §lletter§r: the §lrecipient§r (picked from the list of players who have joined the server, or their name typed), the §lsubject§r and a free §ltext§r over several lines (1,200 characters and 24 lines at most; copy / paste), signed with your name; the client reads it in their notebook and gets it in their mailbox;
• the §lstart§r and §lend§r: month / day / year, hour : minute, with “Now”, “+1 h” and “+1 day”; one minute to 366 days;
• the §lpayment§r: §lTotal§r (one amount for the whole period, up to one billion Shining) or §lHourly§r (a rate per real hour, 1 to 1,000,000 Shining); the duration and the §lplanned amount§r are shown.
“Save draft” to come back to it, “Send to client” to send it. §lNothing is taken until the client accepts§r: they get a message and a letter, and accept or refuse in their notebook; with no answer before the end, the contract expires.
§lTotal§r: the amount is taken as the hours pass, pro rata (the last hour to the minute). Balance too low: a §ldebt§r (“Unpaid”), settled as soon as the balance allows or with “Pay now”; an absent client is charged when they return.
§lHourly§r: on acceptance, the client pays a §lreserve§r (24 hours at most), refilled from their account whenever they are online. §lEach real hour§r is paid from the reserve, players online or not; hours due while the server was stopped are caught up on restart, each one only once. Empty reserve: the contract is §lsuspended§r (hours stop counting, a letter to both sides) until the client pays and resumes it (“Pay and resume”). At the end, the remaining reserve goes back to them.
Either side can §lterminate§r: everything stops, to the minute. An absent provider is paid when they log in. A contract's detail is its §linvoice§r; “Print invoice” puts it on a §lsheet of paper§r. 20 open contracts at most; closed and settled ones go away after 90 days.

pages.title: The mailbox
pages.text:
The §6mailbox§r receives your mail, even while you are offline: every §ltransfer§r you receive (Ledger, /pay) and every piece of news about your §lcontracts§r (offered, withdrawn, signed, refused, expired, suspended, resumed, terminated, completed, payment overdue, debt settled) leaves a §lletter§r in it.
• It is made at the §lmetalworker's bench§r (hammer and file): 2 iron plates, 1 iron rod, 4 iron nuggets, 2 planks. Whoever places it owns it; only they open and break it (and operators).
• It is also a §lchest§r: 27 slots. All your mailboxes show the §lsame contents§r (like the Ender chest): breaking one loses nothing. No sending items between players: only the server writes letters.
• A §lgolden “!”§r floats above your mailboxes, for you alone, as long as a letter is unread; it disappears when you open a mailbox.
• Full mailbox: letters wait (64 at most) and come in as soon as a slot frees up.
• A letter is read with a §lright-click§r: sender, subject, contract, amount, date (server time).

pages.title: Paper boxes
pages.text:
Two wooden boxes to keep what you write and what you find. They are made at the §lcarpenter's bench§r, with a saw.
• The §6letter tray§r (4 planks, 2 paper) holds §l54§r letters and invoices. Its screen shows them as a §llist§r: a wax dot for an unread letter, subject, sender, date. Sort by §ldate§r, §lsender§r or §lkind§r, search a name or a subject, keep only the §lunread§r ones. §lClick§r: read (Esc brings you back); §lright-click§r: take; §lShift + click§r in your inventory: store. “Store all” takes the papers from your inventory, “Empty mailbox” those from your mailbox (§lShift + right-click§r with an empty hand on the tray does the same).
• The §6archive box§r (6 planks, 4 paper, 4 iron nuggets) holds §l192§r Codex writings (the whole Codex): parchment notes, pages, memory modules. On the left, the Codex §lchapters§r and your §lcollection§r (different writings stored / writings of the chapter); on the right, the stored writings of the chapter, in Codex order or by title. Missing writings are only §lcounted§r: nothing is revealed. §lClick§r: read (and file in the Codex); §lright-click§r: take.
• Whoever places a box owns it; members of §ltheir clan§r can open it too (and operators). Broken, it drops its contents.

pages.title: Solo, clan, faction, people
pages.text:
Every player is a Restorer. Clans are §loptional§r: alone, you trade, explore and restore on equal terms. Belonging has four rungs:
• §6Solo§r: an automatic solo clan, for a lone player who wants a territory.
• §6Clan§r: a brigade that decided to last, up to 40 members: territory, roles, regime, treasury, diplomacy, war.
• §6Faction§r: a federation of 2 to 8 clans, allies by right.
• §6Player people§r: a faction that seceded, ranking with the three villager peoples.
Nothing is lost from one rung to the next: a Solo who joins a clan brings their territory, Seals, points and treasury.

Clans are managed in the notebook's §6Clan§r tab (J key) and with the §l/clan§r command. War breaks no block: you take chunks.

pages.title: The Solo
pages.text:
The first chunk you claim alone (§l/clan claim§r, or the Clan tab's map) creates your §6solo clan§r: no Charter, no cost, under the “Solo” regime.
• Territory: 9 + 3 + 4 × level chunks, §l100 at most§r; a (paid) chunkloading slot keeps a chunk loaded.
• It earns points and levels, places Seals, keeps a treasury.
• §lNever besieged§r: no war, no treaty, no vote.
• Inviting a second member turns it into a §lregular clan§r (provisional Empire; the Representative picks a regime once, for free). If the last companion leaves, it becomes solo again.
• Joining or founding another clan: your solo clan merges into it, territory included.

Alone does not mean without an address.

pages.title: Founding a clan: the Charter
pages.text:
The §6Clan Charter§r is made at the Carpenter's Bench: 3 paper, 1 ink sac, 1 beeswax, with a knife.
1. §lDraft§r (right-click): name (3 to 24 characters), tag (2 to 4), color, motto (60 at most) and regime.
2. §lSign§r: two other players, within 8 blocks of the founder, within 10 minutes (right-click the founder holding the Charter, right-click with the Charter, or §l/clan sign <founder>§r). An expired Charter becomes blank again.
3. §lSeal§r: everything is checked again, §l1,000 Shining§r are taken, the Charter is used up. The founder becomes the first Representative.
“We, the undersigned, have read. We say yes.”
Then: invitations (§l/clan invite§r, valid for 10 minutes), departures, expulsions; 3 days before joining another clan. Membership follows the clan's level: 8 members at level 1, 40 at level 9.

pages.title: Roles and permissions
pages.text:
Nine starting roles, sorted by rank: §6Representative§r (100, everything), §6Right Hand§r (80, nearly everything: members, territory, treasury, lower roles; neither the regime nor the title), §6Treasurer§r (60, the budget: treasury, withdrawals, bonuses, dues and taxes, buying claims), §6Surveyor§r (55, the territory: claims, zones, Seals), §6Guard§r (50, territory and sieges), §6Recruiter§r (45, invite, expel, promote), §6Artisan§r (40, machines and Seals), §6Member§r (30), §6Recruit§r (10, build and use machines). You can create others, twelve roles at most.
Twenty-six §lpermissions§r, in five families:
• §lMembers§r: invite, expel, promote, see identities, see statistics.
• §lTerritory§r: claim, manage zones, build, open containers, use machines, transit, chunkloading, place Seals, buy claims.
• §lTreasury§r: see, withdraw, set taxes, pay bonuses.
• §lGovernment§r: start a vote, edit roles, edit identity, declare war, diplomacy, siege windows.
• §lCommunication§r: moderate, pin.
Each role has a daily withdrawal cap (2,000 for the Representative and the Treasurer, nothing for a Member). Members sheet, §l“Roles”§r view: the roles on the left (who holds them), on the right the chosen role's §lrights§r, family by family; a box is checked with one click (“Edit Roles” permission), only for a role ranked below yours and for a permission you have. When the regime gives a decision to the Representative (R mark: in an Empire, taxes, roles, expulsion, identity, war, diplomacy), checking it §ldelegates§r it: the role exercises it on their behalf. The regime change can't be delegated.

pages.title: The four regimes
pages.text:
The regime says who says yes.
• §6Democracy§r: the Representative is elected by the members for 14 days. Check: recall, by two thirds (7 days between two). Activity tax 20% and dues of 50 Shining a day at most.
• §6Empire§r: the Representative decides alone and names an heir. Check: the Revolution, by three quarters of the active members, one attempt per 30 days; it imposes Democracy. Caps 40% and 150.
• §6Council§r: 3 to 7 seats (half the membership), elected for 28 days; the Council elects the Representative for 14 days and decides. Check: a vote of no confidence, by two thirds of the seats. Caps 25% and 100.
• §6Cooperative§r: a spokesperson rotating every 14 days; everything is decided by two thirds of the members. Territory budget +10%, and the previous day's activity tax is shared out equally. Caps 10% and 50.
Changing regime: 2,000 Shining, effective after 7 days, then 30 days before the next.

pages.title: Who decides what
pages.text:
Eight decisions: taxes, roles, expulsion, spending, war, treaty, regime, identity.
• §6Democracy§r: members by simple majority; roles, the Representative; war and treaties at 60%; the regime by two thirds.
• §6Empire§r: the Representative, alone, for everything.
• §6Council§r: the Council by simple majority; the regime by two thirds of the Council.
• §6Cooperative§r: members by two thirds; the regime unanimously.
When a decision belongs to the Representative, it applies at once; otherwise a §lvote§r opens.
• Starting a vote needs the “Start a Vote” permission; only one open vote per kind of decision.
• A vote lasts §l24 hours§r; 40% of the active members must have voted. If it fails, it waits 24 hours before being started again.
• Elections use the same engine, by secret ballot; in a tie, the most senior wins.
The Government sheet of the Clan tab, or §l/clan vote§r.

pages.title: The treasury
pages.text:
The treasury is a Shining account. It never creates money and never goes into debt; everything is written in the clan log.
• §lDonations§r: any member (§l/clan treasury donate <amount>§r).
• §lWithdrawals and bonuses§r: within the role's daily cap; beyond it, or above 25% of the treasury, it is a “spending” decision.
• §6Dues§r: Shining per game day, taken from the balance of members online that day, never more than they have.
• §6Activity tax§r: a percentage of what members sell to NPCs, taken at the source.
• §6Market tax§r: up to 15% of the sales of stalls placed in the territory within 32 blocks of a Market, taken from the seller's share; nothing for a buyer whose clan has a trade agreement with yours.
Caps on dues and activity tax: those of the regime. The treasury pays for bought claims, declarations of war, a possible tribute. An empty clan loses its treasury.

pages.title: Territory
pages.text:
You claim a chunk (§l/clan claim§r, or the Territory sheet's map) with the “Claim and Release” permission. The server checks everything again.
• §lBudget§r: 9 + 3 × active members + 4 × level chunks, +10% for a Cooperative, 400 at most, then the bought claims.
• §lBuying territory§r: the clan treasury buys claims on top of the budget (Territory sheet, “Settings” view; “Claim and Release” and “Withdraw” permissions). Each bought claim costs §l100 Shining§r (fixed price, server setting). 200 purchases at most (50 for a solo player). Releasing a chunk refunds nothing: the bought claim stays in the budget and never declines.
• A chunk §ldoes not need to touch§r the territory: members claim wherever they need, even far away, and each chunk counts as one claim. (Existing outposts stay as they are.)
• §lRefused§r: a chunk touching another clan, within 8 chunks of the spawn point, within 96 blocks of a village bell, or on an intact ruin or one under restoration.
• §lDecline§r: if the budget drops (inactive members), the chunks farthest from the center decline for 72 hours, then are released. The chunks of a dissolved clan are released after 7 days.
• §lBorders§r: after each claim, or with the §lU§r key or §l/clan borders§r, a thin line on the ground in the clan's color shows the nearby borders for a few seconds.

pages.title: Zones and protection
pages.text:
Each chunk has a §lzone§r:
• §6Members§r (default): each member according to their role's permissions (build, containers, machines).
• §6Private§r: from a chosen rank up.
• §6Open§r: by default, everyone passes through and uses doors and buttons; an ally also opens containers and machines there. No one but members breaks or places.
§lVisitor permissions§r (Territory sheet, “Settings” view, “Manage Zones” permission): for the Members and Open zones, a grid sets what §6Allies§r, §6Neutrals§r (another clan, with no treaty and no war), §6Strangers§r (no clan, or solo players) and §6Enemies§r (at war) may do: interact, containers, machines, vehicles, build, crops, animals, slaughter. The Private zone stays closed to every visitor. Capture seals, sieges and federal zones come first; a refused visitor reads why in the action bar.
§lProtection§r covers every action: breaking, placing, clicks, containers, machines, vehicles, mounts, item frames and armor stands, buckets, tilling. For everyone, inside a claim: explosions without block damage, fire and fluids stopped at the border, pistons blocked, no creature breaks or places, no trampling.
The §lmod's transfers§r (cables, pipes, robots, rails, hypertubes, mod hoppers) stop between a claim and the wild, or between two clans that are not allies. Another clan's robots do not work there. A member with the §6Transit§r permission opens the territory to a named clan (§l/clan transit grant <clan>§r, §lrevoke§r, §llist§r): its robots work there, and if both clans grant it to each other, transfers cross their shared border. Passing through is never forbidden: a robot or a train crosses, it does not act.

pages.title: Chunkloading
pages.text:
A claimed chunk §lis not loaded§r when nobody is around. To keep a base running without you (machines, farms, warehouses), take a §lchunkloading slot§r: the chunk then stays loaded at all times, even offline and after a server restart (§l/clan load§r, §l/clan unload§r, or the Territory map buttons; “Manage Chunkloading” permission).
• §lPrice when placed§r, paid by the treasury: the clan's n-th slot costs 50 + 108 × ln n Shining, rounded, §l500 at most§r: 50 for the 1st, 125 for the 2nd, 169 for the 3rd, 200 for the 4th, 224 for the 5th, 244 for the 6th.
• Then §l200 Shining per day§r per slot; empty treasury: 48-hour notice, then it stops until the next paid day.
• 1 to 6 slots depending on the clan's level (3 for a solo player), only in your chunks and the dimensions from the config; server cap with a queue.

pages.title: Function Seals
pages.text:
No building is imposed: a §6Function Seal§r (carpenter: beeswax, leather, feather, with a knife) says what a block is. Right-click a block of the territory, with the “Place Seals” permission; on a container, sneak + right-click. The Seal is used up; it drops back at the block's foot if the designation falls (block broken or replaced, chunk lost).
• §6Town Hall§r (level 1, one): opens the Clan tab; without a bed, members respawn there; a banner placed on top becomes the clan's emblem.
• §6Warehouse§r (level 1, four): a container becomes clan stock, shown in the statistics.
• §6Workshop§r (level 2, four): the brigade reaches 48 blocks around.
• §6Market§r (level 2, three): market tax on stalls within 32 blocks.
• §6Watchtower§r (level 3, three): warns the guards when a stranger enters, and reveals the map within 128 blocks (for the clan and its allies).
• §6Barracks§r (level 4, two): backup respawn; a night within 16 blocks restores health.
• §6Archives§r (level 5, one): pages and notes are left there; each member reads a copy, which joins their Codex.

pages.title: Points and levels
Diplomacy
pages.text:
Three treaties, proposed by a member with the “Diplomacy” permission (§l/clan treaty§r or the Diplomacy sheet), accepted by the other clan according to its regime (“treaty” row). An offer lasts 48 hours.
• §6Non-aggression§r: no declaration of war between the two for 7 days; renewable.
• §6Trade agreement§r: no market tax between the two.
• §6Alliance§r: your Open zones open up to the ally (containers and machines), transfers cross the border, friendly fire is off.
Breaking a treaty follows the regime, with 24 hours' notice. Declaring war ends the trade agreement. Clans of the same faction are allies by right.
A Solo has no diplomacy.

pages.title: War
pages.text:
War destroys §lno block§r: it moves chunks.
• §lDeclaring§r (§l/clan war declare§r, the regime's “war” decision): 500 Shining from the treasury, a reason of 100 characters, §l24 hours' notice§r in real time. Refused if either clan is less than 3 days old, if the attacker weighs more than four times the defender (strike potential, at least 10 per active member), or if a non-aggression pact or a truce is running. One outgoing war at a time, three in all; never a Solo.
• §lSiege windows§r: twice two hours a day, on the server clock (19:00 and 21:00 by default), set by the defender (“Siege Windows” permission), changed after 7 days. Outside a window, the territory is §linviolable§r.
• §lFighting§r: members of both sides fight anywhere; PvP between other players does not change.
• §lEnd§r: a ceasefire accepted by both sides; surrender, with a §ltribute§r of 5% of the loser's treasury (5,000 Shining at most); or 7 days without a capture. Then 3 days of §ltruce§r.

pages.title: The siege
pages.text:
The §6Siege Flag§r (carpenter: 4 sticks, 2 planks, 1 cobblestone, 3 canvas, 1 rope, 2 bronze nuggets, with a saw and a knife) is planted in enemy territory, §lduring a window§r, on a chunk touching your territory or a chunk already taken in this war; it needs the “Siege Windows” permission.
• Stay within §l8 blocks§r: the banner rises. §l10 minutes§r if a defender is online, §l30§r otherwise. It stops if the defenders are at least as many, and goes back down if they are alone.
• The flag falls outside a window, at the end of the war, or after 5 minutes without an attacker.
• At 100%: the chunk changes hands, its Seals fall, its containers are §lsealed for 24 hours§r (only the former owners open them). A chunk beyond your budget is held while the seals last, then released.
• Three captures per day per war; the Town Hall only falls after half of the territory.

pages.title: Clan reputation
pages.text:
A clan is a small people: it has its three gauges, from −300 to +300, with the Restorers, the Bare Hands and the Peddlers.
• §lCascade§r: an act counts 100% for you, §l50%§r for your clan, §l25%§r for your faction or your player people. Gains capped at 30 points per people per day, losses never; time forgives nothing.
• §lCollective acts§r, 100% for the clan: restoring a ruin (once per ruin), funding village workers.
• §lEffects§r: villagers' effective affinity toward you shifts (Hostile −15, Wary −5, Esteemed +5, Ally +10; clan and faction together, ±15 at most), for prices and tone, never a village's average; a Hostile clan only counts within 128 blocks of its territory. When your clan is an Ally of a people, workers from its villages cost you 20% less.

pages.title: Statistics and strike potential
pages.text:
Over 30 days, the clan counts: its members' §lproduction§r (Shining value of what they produce), fights, contributions to the treasury, presence, and §lstrike potential§r.
• §lA player's potential§r: P = 10 × Combat level + 20 × tier of the best weapon + 10 × average armor tier (+10 for a Scout); 230 at most.
• §lA clan's potential§r: the sum of its active members, +5% per different vocation, +15% at most. It sets the balance of power for a war; the directory ranks it weak (under 400), medium or strong (1,500 and up).
• No account name leaves the clan; inside, only with the “See Identities” permission. Elsewhere, only character names are shown.
Figures refresh every 10 minutes.

pages.title: The Clan tab
pages.text:
The notebook's §6Clan§r tab (J key, or right-click the Town Hall) changes with what you are:
• §lNo clan§r: the welcome page, the map, your statistics, the directories.
• §lSolo§r: Overview, Members, Statistics, Territory, Treasury, Log.
• §lMember§r: the §leight sheets§r, Overview, Members, Statistics, Territory, Treasury, Government, Diplomacy and Log, plus Faction if your clan has one.
• Two §ldirectories§r: “Clans” and “Peoples”.
The Territory sheet carries the §lmap§r: the terrain your minimap has seen (the rest in gray), with each clan's chunks in its color and its borders on top, allies, enemies, outposts, decline, sieges, federal zones, rallied villages, your position and the chunk grid. §l− / +§r buttons: zoom; arrows: move around. Hover a chunk: coordinates, owner, “always loaded”. Click a chunk: claim, release, change the zone. §lDrag§r to draw a rectangle (Shift or the “Draw: Release” button to release): a summary gives the accepted chunks, the cost, the budget left and the refusals with their reason; “Confirm” applies everything at once, checked again by the server. An area must touch the territory (no outpost), 256 chunks at most. The §l“Settings”§r view buys claims with the treasury and sets the visitor permissions.
The client only sends intentions; the server checks everything.

pages.title: Factions
pages.text:
A §6faction§r federates 2 to 8 clans, which remain masters in their own houses.
• §6Federal Pact§r (carpenter: 4 paper, 2 ink sacs, 2 beeswax, 1 string, with a knife): the Representative of a clan of level 2 or higher drafts it (name, tag of 3 to 5 letters, color, motto, federal regime). Other clans sign it, each by its own regime (§l/faction sign§r). The founder seals it as soon as one clan has signed: §l3,000 Shining§r from the founding clan's treasury.
• Its clans are §lallies by right§r. A clan leaves by a decision of its regime (24 hours' notice), then waits 7 days before another.
• §lLevel 1 to 5§r, from its clans' combined points (5,000, 15,000, 40,000, 100,000); it opens 20 §lfederal zones§r per level, where its clans do everything but break and place, and federal chunkloading.
“We remain masters in our own houses, and we say yes together.”

pages.title: Governing a faction
pages.text:
The §lDelegates§r are the clans' Representatives. The §lfederal regime§r takes up the four regimes:
• §6Democracy§r: all members vote, one player one vote; they elect the federal Representative for 14 days from the Delegates.
• §6Empire§r: the founding clan's Representative decides alone; the Delegates can recall them by three quarters.
• §6Council§r: the Delegates vote, one vote per clan, and elect the federal Representative.
• §6Cooperative§r: the Delegates vote by two thirds; the spokesperson rotates every 14 days.
§lNo clan weighs more than 40%§r of the votes. Each decision follows a row of the clan table: admit or expel, contribution, spending, war, peace, treaties, workers, regime.
• §lContribution§r: a percentage of each clan's income, settled daily (10% at most in a Democracy, 20 in an Empire, 12 in a Council, 5 in a Cooperative), never more than the treasury.
• §lFederal treaties§r and §lfederal war§r: the whole faction is engaged.

pages.title: Player peoples
pages.text:
A faction can leave the Restorers and become a §6people§r, ranking with the three villager peoples. Conditions, all checked:
• a faction of §llevel 3§r, §l30 days§r old, with at least §l3 clans§r and §l24 active members§r;
• §l20,000 Shining§r from the federal treasury, destroyed; 4 player peoples at most on the server;
• the strongest majority of the federal regime (three quarters, unanimity in a Cooperative, the Representative in an Empire).
The federal Representative prepares the people: name, one of eight tints, banner, motto, salute and §ldoctrine§r: §6Lettered§r (like the Restorers), §6Earthbound§r (like the Bare Hands) or §6Mercantile§r (like the Peddlers); it can change once every 60 days.
The §lSchism§r has a price: −60 with the Restorers for each member, once.
“We leave the Restorers. We have read. We sign. Names follow.”

pages.title: Rallying, decline and dissolution
The ages at a glance
pages.text:
§6Age§r → what opens it → what it gives
• §lPrimitive§r → your hands → flint, fire, clay, first cast metal, smithing.
• §lMechanical§r → the shaking sifter, then iron → rotation, millstone, crusher, saw, beam engine.
• §lBronze and steam§r → copper and tin in bulk → boiler, steam engine, drill, blast furnace, §lsteel§r.
• §lIndustrial (MKI)§r → steel → industrial benches, power, MKI machines, multiblocks, level 2 deposits.
• §lChemical (MKII)§r → aluminum, oil → plastics, gaskets, electronics, MKII and MKIII circuits.
• §lAtomic and computing (MKIII)§r → titanium, processors → reactors, computers, the three space milestones.
• §lSpace (MKIV)§r → titanium, kerolox, programmed flight computer → research, the Moon, lunar alloy, other worlds.
• §lEndgame§r → mordorite, plutonium, tritium → captive star and black hole, simulated planets and galaxies.

pages.title: MK tiers
pages.text:
§6Tier§r: color · frame · circuit · casing · workshop machine · multiblock parallel
• §lMKI§r: green · steel · vacuum tube · MKI (steel, bronze) · 1,024 FE/t · 4
• §lMKII§r: blue · aluminum · transistor · MKII (aluminum, gaskets) · 4,096 FE/t · 8
• §lMKIII§r: red · titanium · microcontroller · MKIII (stainless, titanium) · 16,384 FE/t · 16
• §lMKIV§r: burgundy · tungsten · photonic · MKIV (lunar alloy, tungsten) · 65,536 FE/t · 32

Each tier, a machine runs §ltwice as fast§r and draws §lfour times more§r. An industrial multiblock does the same work in 80% of the time and 75% of the energy, in parallel. A recipe of a given tier needs a machine of at least that tier (“Tier too low”).

pages.title: Making energy
Steam: the cooling tower
Fuels
Glossary (A to L)
pages.text:
• §lOutcrop§r: colored surface block that gives away a deposit; broken, it drops fragments.
• §lAge§r: a stage of the game (primitive, mechanical, bronze and steam, industrial, chemical, atomic, space, endgame).
• §lBuffer§r: storage block (items, fluids, gases, energy, heat, air) linked to cables.
• §lLogistic cable§r: one cable for everything (items, fluids, gases, steam, energy, data, heat, air), from wood to superconductor.
• §lCasing§r: wall block of a multiblock; its tier sets the machine's tier.
• §lFrame§r: the base of every workshop machine of a tier.
• §lTorque§r (N·m): the force of a spinning network; too much, and a part breaks.
• §lBench§r: a crafting station with tools (toolmaker, carpenter, mason, potter, metalworker, coppersmith, assembly…).
• §lFE§r: the unit of electric energy; FE/t per tick.
• §lPlug§r: a cable end connected to a machine; right-click the cable: the diagram.
• §lDeposit§r: a region's ore reserve (level 1: steam drill; level 2: drill).

pages.title: Glossary (M to Z)
pages.text:
• §lMKI to MKIV§r: the four machine tiers (green, blue, red, burgundy).
• §lModule§r: interior block of a multiblock, specific to its trade.
• §lMultiblock§r: a machine built block by block (controller, casings, glass, ports); Shift + right-click empty-handed on the controller: its blueprint.
• §lWorkshop tool§r: hammer, file, saw, knife, mortar, wrench; placed in a bench, it loses one point per piece.
• §lPort§r: wall block through which items, fluids, gases, energy, heat or data go in and out; the wrench toggles input / output.
• §lResearch§r: the K-key tree; it costs data and compute.
• §lRecipe selector§r: a machine slot that locks it onto one recipe.
• §lTier too low§r: the recipe needs a higher-tier machine.
• §lRoute§r: one of the ways to get a metal out of its ore (simple, productive or profitable).

pages.title: Machines and data
pages.text:
§6A recipe does not start§r: an orange warning tab appears on the right of the GUI; hover it to see what is missing (research, data, output room...).

§6Data does not come out§r: check that the side touching the cable is set to §loutput§r (sides panel, Data channel) and that the socket shows on the model. You need a logistic cable §lMKI or better§r; in auto mode, data goes to the connected machines that accept it, otherwise set up a §lData channel§r in the network diagram (right-click the cable).

§6The research lab is full§r: it holds 16 types at most, 100,000 MB each. Put data banks on the network for the surplus.

pages.title: Travel and survival
pages.text:
§6I cannot board the rocket§r: it needs a §lcrew cabin§r module (sneak + right-click the placed rocket).

§6Destination grayed out on the map§r: the rocket tier is too low, or the world's orbit research is not done.

§6I suffocate despite the suit§r: it must be complete, with oxygen in the chestplate, and of a high enough tier for the world (Moon: space suit; Mars: thermal; Venus and beyond: acid-proof).

§6My rocket vanished on arrival§r: it is folded inside the capsule; take it out before leaving.

pages.title: Capsule, giants, stars
pages.text:
§6I crash on every landing§r: turn on the autopilot (V), or open the parachute (B) higher and brake with Space over the last blocks.

§6I fall into a gas giant§r: you need all four pieces of the atmospheric suit. Otherwise, the abyss.

§6My drones do not take off§r: the bay must be fully built (controller blueprint, one pad per drone), inside a giant, powered, with drones in its slot and room in the tanks. In "Marked" mode, tag pockets with the scanner. Check the filter.

§6The absorber makes nothing§r: it must stand on a station around a star, under open sky, research done, shutters open and not overheating.

§6I cannot see the other stars§r: complete the survey research, then press G on the map.

pages.title: Data-driven recipes
Environments and API
pages.text:
§bdata/<ns>/pioneers/environments/*.json§r: per dimension, gravity, breathable, suit_tier (0 to 4), hazard (none, vacuum, cold, heat, acid, radiation, pressure), nitrogen, temperature. Add some for other mods' dimensions.

The §bfr.pioneers.api§r package exposes the key concepts: data type registry (§bpioneers:data_type§r), §bDATA_HANDLER§r capability (IDataHandler, IDataTank, DataStack), data sides (IDataConfigurable), world environment, breathability of a position, worn suit tier, recipe types.

The guide itself is a file: §bassets/pioneers/guide/<language>.json§r.
